36362.e: The Holy Crown of Hungary lies in the domed hall. Guards keep a close watch on it.
36362.m: The Hungarian crown is kept in the parliament in Budapest.

36363.q: Roughly how many rooms does the parliament in Budapest have?
36363.e: The building has 691 rooms. There are also many staircases and courtyards.
36363.m: The parliament in Budapest has almost 700 rooms.

36364.q: What did the architect of the parliament in Budapest not live to see?
36364.e: The architect Imre Steindl died in 1902. The parliament was only fully completed in 1904.
36364.m: The architect did not live to see the parliament in Budapest completed.

36365.q: Which is the largest building in Hungary?
36365.e: The parliament building is 268 metres long. It is considered the largest building in the country.
36365.m: The parliament is Hungary’s largest building.

36366.q: What rises in the middle of the parliament in Budapest?
a: A bell tower with a clock
36366.e: A tall dome stands in the middle of the building. Beneath it is the domed hall.
36366.m: The parliament in Budapest has a large dome in the middle.

36367.q: What is it called when a parliament consists of two parts?
36367.e: Each part of such a parliament is called a chamber. Switzerland also has a parliament with two chambers.
36367.m: A parliament with two parts has a bicameral system.

36368.q: What are the two chambers of the British Parliament called?
a: House of Lords and House of Commons
National Council and Council of States
36368.e: The British Parliament consists of the House of Lords, the upper house, and the House of Commons, the lower house.
36368.m: Great Britain has an upper house and a lower house.

36369.q: What are the two chambers of the Swiss Parliament called?
a: National Council and Council of States
Council of States and Federal Supreme Court
36369.e: The Swiss Parliament has two chambers: the National Council for the people and the Council of States for the cantons. Together they form the Federal Assembly.
36369.m: The Swiss Parliament consists of the National Council and the Council of States.

36370.q: Are the members of the British House of Lords elected by the people?
a: No, they are chosen by lot
36370.e: The Lords are not elected. Most are appointed on a recommendation and often remain members for life.
36370.m: The members of the British House of Lords are not elected by the people.

36371.q: Which chamber of the US Congress is considered the upper house?
36371.e: The US Congress has two chambers. The Senate is the smaller one and is considered the upper house.
36371.m: The Senate is the upper house of the USA.

36372.q: What is the larger chamber of the US Congress called?
36372.e: The House of Representatives has 435 voting members. Big states send more members than small ones.
36372.m: The House of Representatives is the larger chamber in the USA.

36373.q: What is the chamber in the British Parliament that exists alongside the House of Commons called?
36373.e: The British Parliament has two chambers: the House of Commons and the House of Lords.
36373.m: Great Britain has a House of Commons and a House of Lords.

36374.q: How many senators does each US state send to the Senate?
36374.e: Each state has exactly two seats in the Senate, no matter how big it is. That way small and large states are equally represented.
36374.m: Each US state has two senators.

36375.q: In what shape are the seats arranged in the National Council chamber in Bern?
36375.e: The seats of the 200 members of the National Council are arranged in a semicircle. The president sits at the front.
36375.m: The National Council sits in a semicircle.

36376.q: How do the government and opposition sit in the British House of Commons?
36376.e: In the House of Commons the benches are in two blocks. Government and opposition sit directly opposite each other.
36376.m: In the British House of Commons government and opposition sit facing each other.

36377.q: Which country do the terms “left” and “right” for political parties come from?
36377.e: In the French National Assembly of 1789 the groups sat on the left or right side according to their views. Since then people have spoken of left-wing and right-wing parties.
36377.m: Left and right in politics come from France.

36378.q: From where is it decided who sits on the left and who on the right in the Bundestag?
36378.e: In the Bundestag left and right are seen from the point of view of the presiding officers. For the spectators it is therefore the other way round.
36378.m: In the Bundestag left and right are seen from the President’s seat.

36379.q: How do the members sit in the European Parliament?
36379.e: In the European Parliament people from one country don’t all sit together. They sit with their political group.
36379.m: In the European Parliament members sit by political group.

36380.q: In what shape are the seats arranged in the European Parliament in Strasbourg?
a: In two rows facing each other
36380.e: Like many parliaments, the European Parliament sits in a semicircle. In French such a chamber is called a “hémicycle”.
36380.m: The European Parliament sits in a semicircle.

36381.q: Why do many parliaments sit in a semicircle?
a: Everyone can see the speaker well
It saves a lot of electricity
36381.e: In a semicircle everyone looks forward towards the middle. That way everyone can see and hear whoever is speaking.
36381.m: In a semicircle everyone has a good view of the speaker.

36382.q: On which side of the Speaker does the government sit in the British House of Commons?
36382.e: Seen from the Speaker’s chair, the government sits on the right. The opposition sits on the left.
36382.m: In the British House of Commons the government sits to the Speaker’s right.

36383.q: Which goddess stands as a large statue in front of the parliament in Vienna?
36383.e: In front of the building there is a fountain with a statue of the Greek goddess about four metres tall. It is a landmark of the parliament.
36383.m: Pallas Athena stands in front of the parliament in Vienna.

36384.q: What does the goddess whose statue stands in front of the parliament in Vienna stand for?
36384.e: For the ancient Greeks, Athena was the goddess of wisdom. She is meant to show that decisions in parliament should be made wisely.
36384.m: The goddess Athena stands for wisdom.

36385.q: What does the parliament building in Vienna look like?
a: Like a Greek temple with columns
36385.e: The parliament in Vienna was built in the style of the ancient Greeks, as a reminder of democracy in Athens. A statue of the goddess Athena stands in front of the building.
36385.m: The parliament in Vienna looks like a Greek temple.

36386.q: Which ancient culture was the model for the parliament in Vienna?
36386.e: The building has columns like a Greek temple. Greece is considered the birthplace of democracy.
36386.m: The parliament in Vienna looks like a Greek temple.

36387.q: Which two chambers work in the parliament in Vienna?
a: National Council and Council of States
House of Lords and House of Commons
36387.e: In Austria the two chambers are called the National Council and the Federal Council. In Switzerland, by contrast, there are the National Council and the Council of States.
36387.m: The National Council and the Federal Council work in Vienna.

36388.q: In which year was the parliament in Vienna reopened after a long renovation?
36388.e: From 2017 to early 2023 the building was completely renovated. In January 2023 it was ceremonially reopened.
36388.m: The parliament in Vienna was reopened in 2023.

36389.q: What is the larger chamber of the Austrian parliament called?
36389.e: The National Council is the larger chamber of the parliament in Austria. It has 183 members. Switzerland also has a National Council.
36389.m: In Austria the National Council is the larger chamber.

36390.q: Where did the Austrian parliament meet during the renovation?
36390.e: During the building work the parliament moved into the Hofburg. That is the former palace of the emperors in Vienna.
36390.m: During the renovation the parliament met in the Hofburg.

36391.q: What does the Speaker in the British House of Commons shout loudly when it gets too noisy?
36391.e: The Speaker calls out “Order!” loudly. That way he gets the MPs to calm down.
36391.m: The British Speaker shouts “Order!” when it gets too loud.

36392.q: What do MPs do with a newly elected Speaker in the British House of Commons?
a: They drag him to the chair
They carry him on their shoulders
36392.e: The new Speaker pretends not to want the job. So, for fun, the MPs drag him to his chair.
36392.m: A new British Speaker is dragged to his chair.

36393.q: What does the British Speaker have to give up after being elected?
36393.e: The Speaker is meant to be completely neutral. That is why he leaves his party.
36393.m: The British Speaker gives up his party.

36394.q: What is the main job of the president of a parliament?
a: To chair the sessions of parliament
36394.e: The president of the parliament gives members the floor and keeps order during sessions. In Germany this has been Julia Klöckner since 2025.
36394.m: The president of the parliament chairs the sessions.

36395.q: What does the president in a parliament often use to call for quiet?
36395.e: In many parliaments, including in Bern, there is a bell at the president’s desk. When it gets too noisy, the president rings it.
36395.m: In parliament the president rings a bell for quiet.

36396.q: What does the presiding officer in the US House of Representatives bang on the desk?
36396.e: The Speaker in the USA uses a small wooden hammer called a gavel. With it he opens sessions and keeps order.
36396.m: The Speaker in the USA uses a gavel.

36397.q: What is the president of the Swiss National Council often called?
a: Mother or father of the nation
36397.e: According to protocol, whoever chairs the National Council ranks first in the country. That is why people speak of Switzerland’s highest citizen.
36397.m: The president of the National Council is called Switzerland’s highest citizen.

36398.q: When does the British Speaker vote?
a: Never, he is not allowed to
36398.e: The Speaker does not normally vote. Only when there are equal numbers of yes and no votes does his vote decide.
36398.m: The British Speaker votes only in a tie.

36399.q: Where does a member of the Bundestag stand when giving a speech?
36399.e: Anyone giving a speech in the Bundestag goes to the lectern at the front. There is a microphone there.
36399.m: In the Bundestag you speak at the lectern.

36400.q: What do you call it when someone briefly shouts out during another person’s speech?
36400.e: Heckling is a short remark called out from the benches. It interrupts the speech for a moment.
36400.m: A short shout during a speech is called heckling.

36401.q: What is a debate in parliament?
36401.e: In a debate the members say what they think and give their reasons. That way a topic is discussed from all sides.
36401.m: In a debate people exchange opinions and reasons.

36402.q: What is the time someone gets for their speech in parliament called?
36402.e: Each speaker has only a certain amount of speaking time. That way many people get to speak.
36402.m: In parliament each speaker has a speaking time.

36403.q: What is a call to order in parliament?
a: A sign that the session is starting
A request for more speaking time
36403.e: Anyone who behaves badly in a debate can receive a call to order. It is a warning from the presiding officers.
36403.m: A call to order is a reprimand for bad behaviour.

36404.q: What is a very long speech in the US Senate meant to delay a vote called?
36404.e: In a filibuster someone talks for hours so that no vote can take place. It is well known in the US Senate.
36404.m: A deliberately long speech in the US Senate is called a filibuster.

36405.q: What normally comes after the debate on a law in parliament?
36405.e: First the law is discussed and argued about. Then the members vote.

36406.q: Which colour appears on the flag of Germany?
36406.e: The German flag has three colours, and one of them is black.
36406.m: There is a black stripe on the German flag.

36407.q: Which way do the stripes on the German flag run?
36407.e: The three stripes of the German flag lie one above the other, in other words horizontally.
36407.m: The German stripes lie horizontally one above the other.

36408.q: How many stripes does the flag of Germany have?
36408.e: The German flag consists of three stripes of equal width.
36408.m: The German flag has three stripes.

36409.q: What colour is the middle stripe of the German flag?
36409.e: In the middle of the German flag there is a red stripe.
36409.m: The middle stripe of the German flag is red.

36410.q: What is the official name of the colour of the bottom stripe of the German flag?
36410.e: The colour is officially called gold, even though it looks like a strong yellow.
36410.m: The bottom German stripe is officially called gold.

36411.q: What is the national flag of Germany officially called?
36411.e: Germany is a federal state, so its national flag is called the federal flag.
36411.m: The German national flag is called the federal flag.

36412.q: Which animal can be seen on the German flag used by public authorities, the federal service flag?
36412.e: The federal service flag shows the federal coat of arms with the federal eagle in the middle.
36412.m: The federal eagle can be seen on the federal service flag.

36413.q: Which of Switzerland’s neighbours has a black, red and gold flag?
36413.e: Germany lies to the north of Switzerland and has a black, red and gold flag.
36413.m: The black, red and gold flag belongs to Germany.

36414.q: What is the flag of France often called?
36414.e: The French flag has three colours, so it is called the Tricolour.
36414.m: The flag of France is called the Tricolour.

36415.q: Which colour does NOT appear on the flag of France?
36415.e: The French flag is blue, white and red; green does not appear.
36415.m: There is no green on the French flag.

36416.q: Which way do the stripes on the French flag run?
36416.e: The three stripes of the Tricolour stand side by side, in other words vertically.
36416.m: The French stripes stand vertically side by side.

36417.e: “Tri” means three and “colour” means colour, so it means three-coloured.

36418.q: From which period does the French Tricolour date?
36418.e: The Tricolour came into being during the French Revolution from 1789.
36418.m: The Tricolour dates from the French Revolution.

36419.q: Blue and red on the French flag are the old colours of which city?
36419.e: Blue and red were the colours of the city of Paris, white was the colour of the king.
36419.m: Blue and red are the colours of Paris.

36420.q: Which colour on the French flag is right next to the flagpole?
36420.e: On the Tricolour, the blue stripe is next to the flagpole.
36420.m: On the Tricolour, blue is next to the flagpole.

36421.q: What colour is the stripe at the fluttering end of the French flag?
36421.e: The stripe furthest from the flagpole is red.
36421.m: Red is at the fluttering end of the Tricolour.

36422.q: Which colour appears on the flag of Italy?
36422.e: The Italian flag has three colours, and one of them is green.
36422.m: There is green on the Italian flag.

36423.q: Which colour on the Italian flag is next to the flagpole?
36423.e: On the Italian flag, the green stripe is next to the flagpole.
36423.m: On Italy’s flag, green is next to the flagpole.

36424.q: What colour is the middle stripe of the Italian flag?
36424.e: In the middle of the Italian flag there is a white stripe.
36424.m: The middle stripe of the Italian flag is white.

36425.q: Which colour is at the fluttering end of the Italian flag?
36425.e: The stripe furthest from the flagpole is red.
36425.m: Red is at the fluttering end of the Italian flag.

36426.q: Which way do the stripes on the flag of Italy run?
36426.e: The three stripes of the Italian flag stand side by side, in other words vertically.

36427.q: Which country in the Americas has a flag similar to Italy’s, but with an eagle in the middle?
36427.e: The flag of Mexico is green, white and red and shows a coat of arms with an eagle in the middle.
36427.m: Mexico’s flag has Italy’s colours and an eagle.

36428.q: What do Italians call their flag?
36428.e: “Il Tricolore” means “the three-coloured one”, because the flag has three colours.
36428.m: Italians call their flag Il Tricolore.

36429.q: Which flag looks like the Italian one but has orange instead of red?
36429.e: The flag of Ireland is green, white and orange with vertical stripes.
36429.m: The flag of Ireland has orange instead of red.

36430.q: What colours is the flag of Austria?
36430.e: The Austrian flag is made up of just two colours, red and white.
36430.m: Austria’s flag is red and white.

36431.q: How many stripes does the flag of Austria have?
36431.e: The flag of Austria has three horizontal stripes.
36431.m: The Austrian flag has three stripes.

36432.q: What colour is the middle stripe of the Austrian flag?
36432.e: The middle stripe is white; above and below it is red.
36432.m: The middle stripe of Austria’s flag is white.

36433.q: Which way do the stripes on the flag of Austria run?
36433.e: The three stripes of the Austrian flag lie one above the other.

36434.q: According to a legend, a duke’s white robe was covered in blood after a battle. Which part stayed white?
36434.e: When the duke took off his belt, a white stripe was left underneath. That is said to be how red, white and red came about.
36434.m: The legend tells of the white stripe under the belt.

36435.q: Which animal is in the coat of arms on Austria’s state flag?
36435.e: The Austrian coat of arms shows a black eagle.
36435.m: There is an eagle in Austria’s coat of arms.

36436.q: Which neighbouring country to the east of Switzerland has a red, white and red flag?
36436.e: Austria borders Switzerland to the east and has a red, white and red flag.
36436.m: The red, white and red flag belongs to Austria.

36437.q: Which country on the Baltic Sea has a flag similar to Austria’s, but in dark red?
36437.e: The flag of Latvia is dark red with a narrow white stripe in the middle.
36437.m: Latvia’s flag is dark red and white.

36438.q: What is the flag of the United Kingdom often called?
36438.e: The British flag is called the Union Flag, but it is usually known as the Union Jack.
36438.m: The British flag is called the Union Jack.

36439.q: What colours is the Union Jack?
36439.e: The Union Jack consists of red and white crosses on a blue background.
36439.m: The Union Jack is red, white and blue.

36440.q: Which part of the country does the upright red cross on white stand for in the Union Jack?
36440.e: The red cross on white is the Cross of St George, the flag of England.
36440.m: The upright red cross stands for England.

36441.q: Which part of the country does the white diagonal cross on blue stand for in the Union Jack?
36441.e: The white diagonal cross on blue is the Cross of St Andrew, the flag of Scotland.
36441.m: The white diagonal cross stands for Scotland.

36442.q: What does the red diagonal cross in the Union Jack stand for?
36442.e: The red diagonal cross is the Cross of St Patrick and stands for Ireland.
36442.m: The red diagonal cross stands for Ireland.

36443.q: Which part of the United Kingdom cannot be seen in the Union Jack?
36443.e: Wales was already joined with England when the Union Jack was created, which is why it is missing.
36443.m: Wales has no symbol of its own in the Union Jack.

36444.q: Which animal can be seen on the flag of Wales?
36444.e: The flag of Wales shows a red dragon on white and green.
36444.m: There is a red dragon on the flag of Wales.

36445.q: How many crosses are laid on top of each other in the Union Jack?
36445.e: In the Union Jack three crosses lie on top of each other: one each for England, Scotland and Ireland.
36445.m: The Union Jack combines three crosses.

36446.q: On which country’s flag can the Union Jack be seen in the top left corner?
36446.e: Australia has the Union Jack in the top left, with stars on a blue background.
36446.m: Australia’s flag shows the Union Jack in the top left.

36447.q: What colours is the flag of Spain?
36447.e: The Spanish flag has red and yellow stripes.
36447.m: Spain’s flag is red and yellow.

36448.q: How many stripes does the flag of Spain have?
36448.e: The Spanish flag has three horizontal stripes.
36448.m: The Spanish flag has three stripes.

36449.q: What colour is the wide stripe in the middle of the flag of Spain?
36449.e: In the middle of the Spanish flag there is a wide yellow stripe. Above and below there is a red stripe.
36449.m: The wide middle stripe of Spain’s flag is yellow.

36450.q: How wide is the yellow stripe of the Spanish flag compared with a red one?
36450.e: The yellow stripe is twice as wide as each of the two red stripes.
36450.m: Spain’s yellow stripe is twice as wide as a red one.

36451.q: What can be seen on the Spanish state flag near the flagpole?
36451.e: On the yellow stripe near the flagpole is the coat of arms of Spain.
36451.m: The Spanish flag shows a coat of arms.

36452.q: What stands on the left and right of the Spanish coat of arms?
36452.e: The two pillars stand for the Pillars of Hercules near Gibraltar.
36452.m: Two pillars stand in the Spanish coat of arms.

36453.q: Which words are written on the ribbons on the pillars in the Spanish coat of arms?
36453.e: “Plus Ultra” is Latin and means “further beyond”. It is Spain’s motto.

36454.q: What sits on top of the Spanish coat of arms?
36454.e: Spain is a kingdom, so the coat of arms has a royal crown.
36454.m: The Spanish coat of arms has a crown.

36455.q: Which fruit is shown at the very bottom of the Spanish coat of arms?
36455.e: The pomegranate stands for Granada, because “granada” means pomegranate in Spanish.
36455.m: The pomegranate in the coat of arms stands for Granada.

36456.q: What is a Nordic cross on a flag?
a: A cross exactly in the middle
36456.e: In a Nordic cross the crossing point is shifted towards the flagpole.
36456.m: A Nordic cross lies closer to the flagpole.

36457.q: Which country has a blue flag with a yellow cross?
36457.e: The flag of Sweden shows a yellow Nordic cross on a blue background.
36457.m: Sweden’s flag has a yellow cross on blue.

36458.q: Which country has a white flag with a blue cross?
36458.e: The flag of Finland shows a blue Nordic cross on white.
36458.m: Finland’s flag has a blue cross on white.

36459.q: Which country has a red flag with a blue cross edged in white?
36459.e: The flag of Norway is red with a blue cross edged in white.
36459.m: Norway’s flag is red with a blue cross.

36460.q: Which country has a blue flag with a red cross edged in white?
36460.e: The flag of Iceland is blue with a red cross edged in white.
36460.m: Iceland’s flag is blue with a red cross.

36461.q: How many independent countries have a Nordic cross on their flag?
36461.e: Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland and Iceland have a Nordic cross; that makes five.
36461.m: Five countries have a Nordic cross.

36462.q: Which flag was the model for the other Nordic cross flags?
36462.e: The flag of Denmark is the oldest with a Nordic cross; the other countries took it as their model.
36462.m: The Danish flag was the model for the Nordic cross.

36463.q: Which country do the Faroe Islands in the North Atlantic belong to?
36463.e: The Faroe Islands belong to Denmark but largely govern themselves. They have their own flag with a Nordic cross.
36463.m: The Faroe Islands belong to Denmark.

36464.q: Which of these countries has a Nordic cross on its flag?
36464.e: The flag of Denmark is red with a white Nordic cross. It is considered the oldest national flag in the world.
36464.m: Denmark has a Nordic cross on its flag.

36465.q: What is the flag of Denmark called?
36465.e: The Danes call their flag the Dannebrog.
36465.m: The Danish flag is called the Dannebrog.

36466.q: What does the flag of Denmark look like?
36466.e: The Dannebrog shows a white Nordic cross on a red background.
36466.m: The Dannebrog is red with a white cross.

36467.q: According to a legend, where did the Danish flag come from?
36467.e: The legend says that the flag fell from the sky during a battle.
36467.m: According to legend, the Dannebrog fell from the sky.

36468.q: The legend of the Dannebrog is set in the year 1219. About how many years ago was that?
36468.e: From 1219 to 2026 is 807 years, so about 800 years.
36468.m: The legend of the Dannebrog is about 800 years old.

36469.q: According to the legend, when did the Dannebrog fall from the sky?
a: At a wedding in a castle
36469.e: The legend says that the flag fell from the sky in 1219 during a battle fought by the Danes in what is now Estonia.
36469.m: According to legend, the Dannebrog fell from the sky during a battle.

36470.q: What is often said about the Dannebrog?
a: It is one of the oldest flags
36470.e: The Dannebrog is considered one of the oldest flags in the world.
36470.m: The Dannebrog is one of the oldest flags in the world.

36471.q: Which country has a red flag with a white cross, similar to Switzerland?
36471.e: The flag of Denmark is red with a white cross, just like the colours of Switzerland. But the cross is shifted a little to one side.
36471.m: Denmark and Switzerland both have red and white.

36472.q: Where is the cross on the flag of Denmark?
a: A little closer to the flagpole
36472.e: The white cross of the Danish flag is shifted towards the flagpole. On the Swiss flag the cross is in the middle.
36472.m: The Danish cross is closer to the flagpole.

36473.q: What colours is the flag of Greece?
36473.e: The Greek flag is made up of blue and white areas.
36473.m: Greece’s flag is blue and white.

36474.q: How many stripes does the flag of Greece have?
36474.e: The Greek flag has nine horizontal stripes.
36474.m: The Greek flag has nine stripes.

36475.q: What can be seen in the top left of the Greek flag?
36475.e: In the top left there is a white cross on a blue field.
36475.m: There is a cross in the top left of Greece’s flag.

36476.q: Which cry are the stripes of the Greek flag said to stand for?
36476.e: It is said that the stripes stand for the syllables of the Greek cry “Eleftheria i thanatos”.
36476.m: The Greek stripes recall the cry “Freedom or death”.

36477.q: What does the blue on the Greek flag often stand for?
36477.e: It is often said that the blue is a reminder of the sea and sky of Greece.
36477.m: Greece’s blue recalls the sea and sky.

36478.q: How many blue stripes does the flag of Greece have?
36478.e: Of the nine stripes, five are blue and four are white.
36478.m: Greece’s flag has five blue stripes.

36479.q: What does the cross on the Greek flag stand for?
36479.e: The cross stands for the Orthodox Christian faith that many people in Greece have.
36479.m: The Greek cross stands for the Christian faith.

36480.q: What colour is the top stripe of the Greek flag?
36480.e: The top and bottom stripes of the Greek flag are blue.

36481.q: What colours is the flag of Ukraine?
36481.e: The Ukrainian flag has a blue stripe and a yellow stripe.
36481.m: The flag of Ukraine is blue and yellow.

36482.q: Which colour is at the top of the flag of Ukraine?
36482.e: On the Ukrainian flag the blue stripe is at the top.
36482.m: On the Ukrainian flag blue is at the top.

36483.q: What does the blue on the flag of Ukraine often stand for?
36483.e: The blue is often seen as the wide sky over the country.
36483.m: Ukraine’s blue stands for the sky.

36484.q: What does the yellow on the flag of Ukraine often stand for?
36484.e: The yellow is often seen as ripe fields of grain, because Ukraine grows a lot of wheat.
36484.m: Ukraine’s yellow stands for fields of grain.

36485.q: How many stripes does the flag of Ukraine have?
36485.e: The Ukrainian flag consists of two horizontal stripes.
36485.m: The Ukrainian flag has two stripes.

36486.q: How wide are the two stripes of the Ukrainian flag?
a: The top one twice as wide
The bottom one twice as wide
The top one three times as wide
36486.e: The two stripes of the Ukrainian flag are exactly the same width.
36486.m: Ukraine’s stripes are the same width.

36487.q: Which country has a flag with a blue stripe at the top and a yellow stripe at the bottom?
36487.e: The flag of Ukraine has a blue stripe at the top and a yellow one at the bottom.
36487.m: The blue and yellow flag belongs to Ukraine.

36488.q: Which symbol can be seen in the coat of arms of Ukraine?
36488.e: The coat of arms of Ukraine shows a golden trident on a blue background.
36488.m: The Ukrainian coat of arms shows a trident.

36489.q: What colours is the flag of Liechtenstein?
36489.e: The flag of Liechtenstein has a blue stripe and a red stripe.
36489.m: Liechtenstein’s flag is blue and red.

36490.q: Which colour is at the top of the flag of Liechtenstein?
36490.e: On the flag of Liechtenstein the blue stripe is at the top.
36490.m: On Liechtenstein’s flag blue is at the top.

36491.q: What can be seen in the top left of the flag of Liechtenstein?
36491.e: In the top left is the golden princely hat, a kind of crown.
36491.m: There is a crown on Liechtenstein’s flag.

36492.q: At the 1936 Olympic Games, Liechtenstein noticed that another country had the same flag. Which one?
36492.e: The flag of Haiti is also blue and red. That is why Liechtenstein’s flag was given an extra symbol.
36492.m: Haiti once had almost the same flag as Liechtenstein.

36493.q: Since which year has the flag of Liechtenstein had the crown?
36493.e: The princely hat was added to the flag in 1937, one year after the Olympic Games in Berlin.
36493.m: The crown has been on Liechtenstein’s flag since 1937.

36494.q: What does the crown on the flag of Liechtenstein stand for?
36494.e: Liechtenstein is a principality. The crown is called the princely hat and stands for the prince.
36494.m: The crown on Liechtenstein’s flag stands for the prince.

36495.q: Which small neighbouring country of Switzerland has a blue and red flag with a crown?
36495.e: Liechtenstein lies to the east of Switzerland, on the Rhine.
36495.m: The blue and red flag with a crown belongs to Liechtenstein.

36496.q: Which way do the stripes on the flag of Liechtenstein run?
36496.e: The two stripes of Liechtenstein’s flag lie one above the other.

36497.q: Which other country also has a square flag?
36497.e: Only Switzerland and Vatican City have a square national flag.
36497.m: Vatican City also has a square flag.

36498.q: Which symbol do you get if you swap the colours of the Swiss flag?
36498.e: In honour of Switzerland, the Red Cross movement took the Swiss flag with its colours swapped as its symbol.
36498.m: The Red Cross is the Swiss flag reversed.

36499.q: What shape are the arms of the Swiss cross?
a: A little longer than they are wide
Exactly as long as they are wide
Twice as wide as they are long
36499.e: Each arm of the Swiss cross is one sixth longer than it is wide.
36499.m: The arms of the Swiss cross are a little longer than they are wide.

36500.q: Which canton had a red flag early on, from which the Swiss flag developed?
36500.e: The cross on a red background comes from the flag of Schwyz. The name Switzerland also comes from Schwyz.
36500.m: The Swiss flag comes from the flag of Schwyz.

36501.q: How many arms does the cross on the Swiss flag have?
36501.e: The Swiss cross has four arms of equal length that come out from the middle.
36501.m: The Swiss cross has four arms.

36502.q: Which Swiss flags are rectangular instead of square?
36502.e: Ships sailing under the Swiss flag on the high seas fly a rectangular flag.
36502.m: On ships the Swiss flag is rectangular.

36503.q: How many stripes does the flag of the USA have?
36503.e: The flag has 13 stripes. They recall the first colonies from which the USA was formed.
36503.m: The stripes of the US flag recall the first colonies.

36504.q: What colours are the stripes of the US flag?
36504.e: The stripes alternate between two colours.
36504.m: The stripes of the US flag are red and white.

36505.q: What colour is the field with the stars on the US flag?
36505.e: In the top left of the flag of the USA there is a blue field. The stars are on it.
36505.m: The stars of the US flag are on a blue field.

36506.q: What is the flag of the USA often called in English?
36506.e: The flag of the USA is often called the “Stars and Stripes”. The name describes what you see on it.
36506.m: Americans like to call their flag the “Stars and Stripes”.

36508.q: What colour are the stars on the flag of the USA?
36508.e: The stars on the US flag are white and are on a blue background.
36508.m: The stars on the US flag are white.

36509.q: What do the 50 stars on the flag of the USA stand for?
36509.e: Each star stands for one state. When Hawaii joined in 1959, the flag got its 50th star.
36509.m: Each star on the US flag stands for a state.

36510.q: What colour are the top and bottom stripes of the US flag?
36510.e: The flag begins and ends with a red stripe. That is why there is one more red stripe than white ones.
36510.m: The US flag has a red stripe at the top and bottom.

36511.q: Which leaf is on the flag of Canada?
36511.e: In the middle of Canada’s flag is a maple leaf. The maple is a symbol of Canada.
36511.m: The maple leaf is the symbol of Canada.

36512.q: What colour is the leaf on the flag of Canada?
36512.e: The leaf on the flag is red. That is how maple leaves look in autumn.
36512.m: The leaf on Canada’s flag is red.

36513.q: Which two colours does the flag of Canada have?
36513.e: The flag of Canada is red and white. These are the same colours as on the Swiss flag.
36513.m: Canada and Switzerland both have a red and white flag.

36514.q: How many points does the leaf on the flag of Canada have?
36514.e: The leaf on the flag has 11 points. It is drawn in a simplified way so that it is easy to recognise.
36514.m: The leaf on Canada’s flag has eleven points.

36516.q: Where are the two red bars on the flag of Canada?
36516.e: There is a red bar on the left and one on the right. Between them is a white field.
36516.m: Canada’s flag has a red bar on the left and right.

36517.q: What colour is the field in the middle of the flag of Canada?
36517.e: The field in the middle is white. The leaf is on it.
36517.m: The middle field of Canada’s flag is white.

36518.q: What can be seen in the middle of the flag of Canada?
36518.e: In the middle of Canada’s flag is a red maple leaf. Maple trees grow everywhere in Canada.
36518.m: There is a red maple leaf on Canada’s flag.

36519.q: What can be seen on the flag of Japan?
36519.e: The flag of Japan is white with a red circle. It is very simple and easy to recognise.
36519.m: Japan’s flag shows a red circle on a white background.

36520.q: What does the red circle on the flag of Japan stand for?
36520.e: The red circle is a sun. The sun is an important symbol in Japan.
36520.m: The red circle on Japan’s flag is a sun.

36521.q: Where is the red circle on the flag of Japan?
36521.e: The red circle is exactly in the middle of the flag.
36521.m: The circle on Japan’s flag is in the middle.

36522.q: Which country is called the “Land of the Rising Sun”?
36522.e: Japan lies in the far east of Asia. The Japanese name of the country means roughly “origin of the sun”.
36522.m: Japan is also called the Land of the Rising Sun.

36523.q: What shape is the flag of Japan?
36523.e: The flag of Japan is a rectangle. It is wider than it is tall.

36524.q: What is the flag of Japan often called?
36524.e: The flag of Japan shows a red sun on a white background. Japan is also called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
36524.m: Japan’s flag is the sun flag.

36525.q: The flag of Japan is called “Hinomaru”. What does that mean?
36525.e: “Hinomaru” is Japanese and means roughly circle of the sun or sun disc.

36526.q: Which country has a flag similar to Japan’s, but with a red circle on green?
36526.e: The flag of Bangladesh is green with a red circle. It looks similar to the flag of Japan.
36526.m: Bangladesh has a red circle on a green flag.

36527.q: What is the background colour of the flag of Brazil?
36527.e: The flag of Brazil is green. Other shapes in other colours lie on top of it.
36527.m: Brazil’s flag has a green background.

36528.q: What shape is the yellow field on the flag of Brazil?
36528.e: On the green background lies a yellow diamond. A diamond shape is a square or rectangle tilted on its corner.
36528.m: There is a yellow diamond on Brazil’s flag.

36529.q: What is in the middle of the flag of Brazil?
36529.e: In the middle there is a blue circle. It shows the sky with stars.
36529.m: The middle of Brazil’s flag shows a starry sky.

36530.q: What does the motto “Ordem e Progresso” on the flag of Brazil mean?

36531.q: In which language is the motto on the flag of Brazil written?
36531.e: In Brazil people speak Portuguese. The country used to be a colony of Portugal.

36532.q: How many stars are on the flag of Brazil?
36532.e: There are 27 stars on the flag. Each one stands for a state or for the federal district with the capital.

36533.q: Which sky do the stars on the flag of Brazil show?
a: The sky over Rio de Janeiro
36533.e: The stars show the sky over Rio de Janeiro on 15 November 1889. On this day Brazil became a republic.
36533.m: Brazil’s flag shows the sky over Rio de Janeiro.

36534.q: What colour is the band with the motto on the flag of Brazil?
36534.e: A white band runs across the middle of the flag. The motto is written on it in green letters.
36534.m: The band on Brazil’s flag is white.

36535.q: What is the background colour of the flag of China?
36535.e: The flag of China is completely red. There are only stars in the top left.
36535.m: China’s flag has a red background.

36536.q: What colour are the stars on the flag of China?
36536.e: The stars on the flag of China are yellow.
36536.m: The stars on China’s flag are yellow.

36537.q: Where are the stars on the flag of China?
36537.e: All the stars are in the top left corner. The rest of the flag is empty.
36537.m: The stars on China’s flag are in the top left.

36538.q: Which stars are on the flag of China?
36538.e: There is one big star on the flag. Four small stars stand in an arc beside it.
36538.m: China’s flag has one big and four small stars.

36539.q: Since which year has China had its present flag?
36539.e: The People’s Republic of China was founded on 1 October 1949. This flag has been used since then.
36539.m: China’s present flag has existed since 1949.

36540.q: What does the red colour on the flag of China stand for?
36540.e: The red stands for the communist revolution. Red is also a lucky colour in China.
36540.m: The red on China’s flag stands for the revolution.

36541.q: In which city was China’s new flag first raised ceremonially?
36541.e: The flag was raised in Beijing in Tiananmen Square. Beijing is the capital of China.
36541.m: Beijing is the capital of China.

36542.q: What does the big star on the flag of China stand for?
36542.e: The big star stands for the Communist Party. The small stars stand for the people.
36542.m: The big star on China’s flag stands for the Party.

36543.q: Which three colours are the stripes of the flag of India?
36543.e: The colours are saffron orange, white and green.
36543.m: India’s flag is orange, white and green.

36544.q: What is in the middle of the flag of India?
36544.e: In the middle of the white stripe there is a wheel. It is an old symbol from India.
36544.m: There is a wheel in the middle of India’s flag.

36545.q: How many spokes does the wheel on the flag of India have?
36545.e: The wheel has 24 spokes. You can compare them with the 24 hours of a day.
36545.m: The wheel on India’s flag has 24 spokes.

36546.q: Which ancient emperor is the wheel on the flag of India named after?
36546.e: The wheel is called the Ashoka Chakra. Ashoka was a powerful emperor in India more than 2,000 years ago.
36546.m: The wheel on India’s flag is named after Emperor Ashoka.

36547.q: What colour is the wheel on the flag of India?
36547.e: The wheel is dark blue. It stands out clearly on the white stripe.
36547.m: The wheel on India’s flag is blue.

36548.q: Since which year has India had its present flag?
36548.e: The flag was adopted in July 1947. Shortly afterwards India became independent from Great Britain.
36548.m: India has had its flag since 1947.

36549.q: The flag of India is called “Tiranga”. What does that mean?
36549.e: “Tiranga” is Hindi and means three-coloured. The flag has three stripes in three colours.

36550.q: How do the stripes lie on the flag of India?
36550.e: The three stripes lie horizontally one above the other.
36550.m: The stripes of India’s flag are horizontal.

36551.q: How many colours does the flag of South Africa have?
36551.e: The flag has six colours: red, blue, green, black, yellow and white.
36551.m: South Africa’s flag has six colours.

36552.q: Which letter does the green band on the flag of South Africa form?
36552.e: The green band starts on the left with two arms and joins into one band towards the right. This forms a Y lying on its side.
36552.m: There is a green Y on South Africa’s flag.

36553.q: Since which year has South Africa had its present flag?
36553.e: The flag was introduced on 27 April 1994. Around then the first free elections for everyone took place.
36553.m: South Africa has had its flag since 1994.

36554.q: What colour is the narrow border around the black triangle on the flag of South Africa?
36554.e: The black triangle is surrounded by a narrow yellow border. Then comes the green band.
36554.m: There is a yellow border around the black triangle.

36555.q: What is the green band on the flag of South Africa meant to show?
36555.e: The two arms join into one band. This shows that the people of the country are moving forward together.
36555.m: The green band shows that South Africa is growing together.

36556.q: What colour is the triangle on the left of the flag of South Africa?
36556.e: On the left there is a black triangle. It points towards the middle of the flag.
36556.m: There is a black triangle on the left of South Africa’s flag.

36557.q: What colour is the large upper field of the flag of South Africa?
36557.e: At the top there is a red field and at the bottom a blue field. The green band lies between them.
36557.m: The upper field of South Africa’s flag is red.

36558.q: Which nickname does South Africa have because of its many peoples?
36558.e: South Africa is often called the Rainbow Nation. Like the many colours of the flag, many different people live together there.
36558.m: South Africa is also called the Rainbow Nation.

36559.q: What is the background colour of the flag of Australia?
36559.e: The flag of Australia is dark blue. On it are a flag and stars.
36559.m: Australia’s flag has a blue background.

36560.q: What is the big star in the bottom left of the flag of Australia called?
36560.e: The big star is called the Commonwealth Star. It stands for the joining of Australia into one federation.
36560.m: The big star on Australia’s flag is called the Commonwealth Star.

36561.q: What is the constellation on the flag of Australia called?
36561.e: On the right of the flag is the constellation of the Southern Cross. It is a well-known constellation.
36561.m: Australia’s flag shows the Southern Cross.

36562.q: What colour are the stars on the flag of Australia?
36562.e: All the stars on the flag of Australia are white.
36562.m: The stars on Australia’s flag are white.

36563.q: How many stars does the flag of Australia have altogether?
36563.e: There are five stars on the right and one big star at the bottom left. Together that makes six stars.

36564.q: How many points does the big star under the Union Jack on the flag of Australia have?
36564.e: The big star has seven points. Six stand for the states and one for the territories.
36564.m: The big star on Australia’s flag has seven points.

36565.q: Which neighbouring country has a flag similar to Australia’s, but with red stars?
36565.e: The flag of New Zealand is also blue with the Union Jack. But its stars are red with a white border.
36565.m: New Zealand has red stars on its flag.

36566.q: Why is the constellation of the Southern Cross on the flag of Australia?
a: It can be seen well in the southern sky
It is a symbol of the Church
It shows the way to Europe
36566.e: Australia lies in the Southern Hemisphere. There you can see the Southern Cross clearly in the night sky.
36566.m: The Southern Cross can be seen in the Southern Hemisphere.

36567.q: How was the flag of Australia chosen in 1901?
36567.e: In 1901 there was a competition for the new flag. Tens of thousands of people sent in ideas.
36567.m: Australia’s flag was chosen in a competition.

36568.q: Which three colours does the flag of Mexico have?
36568.e: The flag of Mexico has a green stripe on the left, a white one in the middle and a red one on the right.
36568.m: Mexico’s flag is green, white and red.

36569.q: Which animal is in the middle of the flag of Mexico?
36569.e: In the middle is the coat of arms of Mexico. It shows an eagle.
36569.m: There is an eagle on Mexico’s flag.

36570.q: What does the eagle on the flag of Mexico hold in its beak?
36570.e: The eagle is fighting a snake and holds it in its beak.
36570.m: The eagle on Mexico’s flag holds a snake.

36571.q: What is the eagle on the flag of Mexico sitting on?
36571.e: The eagle sits on a prickly pear cactus. The cactus grows on a rock in the water.
36571.m: The eagle on Mexico’s flag sits on a cactus.

36572.q: Which ancient people told the legend of the eagle on the cactus?
36572.e: According to the legend, the people were to build a city where they saw an eagle on a cactus.
36572.m: The legend of the eagle on the cactus comes from the Aztecs.

36573.q: Which country in Europe has the same colours in the same order as Mexico?
36573.e: The flag of Italy has the same three stripes. But it has no coat of arms in the middle.
36573.m: Italy’s flag has no coat of arms, Mexico’s does.

36574.q: In which stripe is the coat of arms on the flag of Mexico?
36574.e: The coat of arms with the eagle is exactly in the middle, in the middle stripe.
36574.m: Mexico’s coat of arms is in the middle stripe.

36575.q: Which city stands today where, according to legend, the eagle sat on the cactus?
36575.e: The city of Tenochtitlan was founded at this spot. Today Mexico City, the capital, stands there.
36575.m: Mexico City stands where Tenochtitlan used to be.

36576.q: What shape is the flag of Nepal?
a: Two triangles one above the other
36576.e: The flag of Nepal consists of two triangles placed one above the other.
36576.m: Nepal’s flag consists of two triangles.

36577.q: What is special about the flag of Nepal?
a: It is the only national flag that is not four-sided
It is the biggest flag in the world
It is the oldest flag in the world
It is the only one without colour
36577.e: Almost all national flags are rectangles; Switzerland has a square. Only Nepal has a flag that is not four-sided.
36577.m: Nepal is the only country without a four-sided flag.

36578.q: What colour is the border of the flag of Nepal?
36578.e: A blue border runs all the way round the flag.
36578.m: The border of Nepal’s flag is blue.

36579.q: What is the background colour of the flag of Nepal?
36579.e: The flag of Nepal is dark red. This colour is also called crimson.

36580.q: The red of the flag of Nepal is the colour of the national flower. Which flower is it?
36580.e: The red rhododendron is the national flower of Nepal. It grows on the mountainsides there.
36580.m: The rhododendron is the national flower of Nepal.

36581.q: What do the two points of the flag of Nepal remind people of?
36581.e: Nepal lies among very high mountains. The two points of the flag recall these mountains.
36581.m: The points of Nepal’s flag recall mountains.

36582.q: What wish is expressed by the sun and moon on the flag of Nepal?
a: That Nepal lasts as long as they do
That the weather is always good
That people work day and night
36582.e: The sun and moon have existed for a very long time. The people wish that their country will last just as long.
36582.m: The sun and moon on Nepal’s flag stand for a long life for the country.

36583.q: What colour are the sun and moon on the flag of Nepal?
36583.e: The sun and moon are white. That way they stand out well on the red background.
36583.m: The sun and moon on Nepal’s flag are white.

36584.q: What is special about the shape of the flag of Nepal?
a: It is made of two triangles one above the other
It is square like the Swiss flag
It is a long, narrow strip
36584.e: Nepal’s flag is the only national flag that is not rectangular. It is made of two pennants, in other words triangles, one above the other.
36584.m: Nepal’s flag is made of two triangles.

36585.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
36585.e: There are five rings on the Olympic flag. They are interlinked.
36585.m: The Olympic flag has five rings.

36586.q: What colour is the background of the Olympic flag?
36586.e: The rings are on a white background.

36587.q: What colours are the Olympic rings?
36587.e: Each of the five rings has its own colour.
36587.m: The Olympic rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red.

36588.q: What do the rings on the Olympic flag stand for?
36588.e: The rings stand for the inhabited continents. They are linked because athletes from all over the world come together.
36588.m: The Olympic rings link the continents.

36589.e: Pierre de Coubertin founded the modern Olympic Games. He drew the flag in 1913.
36589.m: Pierre de Coubertin designed the Olympic flag.

36590.q: What can be seen on the Olympic flag?
a: Five coloured rings on a white background
A golden torch on a blue background
A laurel wreath on a red background
Five stars on a green background
36590.e: The five interlinked rings stand for the five inhabited continents. The flag first flew at the Games in Antwerp in 1920.
36590.m: The Olympic flag shows five rings on a white background.

36591.q: How are the rings arranged on the Olympic flag?
a: Three at the top, two at the bottom
Two at the top, three at the bottom
36591.e: There are three rings in the top row and two in the bottom row. All the rings are linked together.
36591.m: The Olympic rings are three at the top and two at the bottom.

36592.q: What happens to the Olympic flag at the closing ceremony?
a: It goes to the next host city
It stays in the host city forever
It goes into the Olympic Museum
It goes to the country with the most medals
36592.e: At the closing ceremony the flag is handed over to the city that will hold the next Games.
36592.m: The Olympic flag travels from host city to host city.

36593.q: Why were the colours of the Olympic flag chosen?
a: Every national flag had at least one of them
They were the athletes’ favourite colours
They are the colours of the rainbow
36593.e: Together with the white, every national flag at that time contained at least one of these colours. That way every country could find itself in the flag.
36593.m: Every national flag contains an Olympic colour.

36594.q: How many stripes does the well-known rainbow flag usually have today?
36594.e: Today the well-known rainbow flag usually has six stripes in six colours.
36594.m: The well-known rainbow flag has six stripes.

36595.q: Which colour is at the very top of the rainbow flag?
36595.e: Just like a rainbow in the sky, red is at the very top.
36595.m: On the rainbow flag, red is at the top.

36596.q: What is the rainbow flag a sign of?
36596.e: The rainbow flag was designed in the USA in 1978. Its many colours stand for diversity and for respecting all people.
36596.m: The rainbow flag stands for diversity.

36597.q: In which city was the rainbow flag first flown in 1978?
36597.e: The first rainbow flags were flown in 1978 at a parade in San Francisco in the USA.
36597.m: The rainbow flag was first flown in San Francisco.

36598.q: What is the rainbow flag a sign of today?
36598.e: The rainbow flag stands for diversity. It is especially a sign of lesbians, gay people and other queer people.
36598.m: The rainbow flag is a sign of diversity.

36599.q: Where does the rainbow flag get its colours from?
a: From the rainbow in the sky
36599.e: The colours of the flag are arranged like a rainbow in the sky. That is why it is called the rainbow flag.
36599.m: The rainbow flag has the colours of the rainbow.

36600.q: Which word is written on the peace flag in rainbow colours?
36600.e: “Pace” is Italian and means peace. The peace flag comes from Italy.
36600.m: “Pace” is the Italian word for peace.

36601.q: Which colour is between yellow and blue on the rainbow flag?
36601.e: The colours of the flag follow the order of a rainbow in the sky. There, green is between yellow and blue.
36601.m: In a rainbow, green is between yellow and blue.

36602.q: Which is the only country in the world that has an emperor today?
36602.e: Japan is the only country where an emperor is still the head of state today. China and Korea used to have emperors, but not any more.
36602.m: Only Japan still has an emperor today.

36603.q: What is the name of the Emperor of Japan (as of 2026)?
36603.e: Naruhito has been Emperor of Japan since 2019. He followed his father Akihito.
36603.m: Since 2019, Naruhito has been the Emperor of Japan.

36604.q: In which city is the Imperial Palace of Japan?
36604.e: The Imperial Palace is in the middle of Tokyo, the capital of Japan. The emperor lives and works there.
36604.m: The Japanese emperor lives in a palace in Tokyo.

36605.q: Which flower is the symbol of the Japanese imperial family?
36605.e: A golden chrysanthemum with 16 petals is the emblem of the imperial family. That is why the imperial throne is also called the Chrysanthemum Throne.
36605.m: The chrysanthemum is the flower of the Japanese emperor.

36606.q: Who leads the government in Japan, instead of the emperor?
36606.e: In Japan, the Prime Minister leads the government. He is elected by parliament.
36606.m: In Japan, the Prime Minister leads the government.

36607.q: According to Japan’s constitution, what is the Japanese emperor?
36607.e: The Japanese constitution calls the emperor a symbol of the state and of the unity of the people. He does not make laws.
36607.m: The Emperor of Japan is a symbol for his people.

36608.q: What do you call the wife of an emperor?
36608.e: The wife of an emperor is called an empress. In Japan today this is Empress Masako, the wife of Emperor Naruhito.
36608.m: The wife of an emperor is the empress.

36609.q: What happens on the Japanese emperor’s birthday?
a: It is a school day with a test
It is a day of fasting
36609.e: The emperor’s birthday is a national holiday in Japan. For Naruhito, it is on 23 February.
36609.m: The emperor’s birthday is a holiday in Japan.

36610.q: Which country is called the largest democracy in the world?
36610.e: In the 2024 election, almost one billion people in India were allowed to vote. In no other country do so many people elect their parliament.
36610.m: India is the largest democracy in the world.

36611.q: What is the capital of India?
36611.e: New Delhi is the capital of India. The parliament and government are there. Mumbai is a big city, but not the capital.
36611.m: The capital of India is New Delhi.

36612.q: What do voters in India get on their finger after voting?
36612.e: After voting, they are marked with a line of ink that does not wash off for a long time. That way nobody can vote twice.
36612.m: In India, a line of ink on the finger shows that someone has already voted.

36613.q: How do people in India cast their votes in elections?
a: By raising their hands at a meeting
Only by sending a letter by post
36613.e: In India, people vote on electronic voting machines. They press a button next to the symbol of a party.
36613.m: In India, people vote with electronic voting machines.

36614.q: How long did the big parliamentary elections in India last in 2024?
36614.e: Because so many people vote, India votes in several stages. In 2024, the election lasted from April to early June.
36614.m: The big elections in India last several weeks.

36615.q: Who fought peacefully, without violence, for India’s independence?
36615.e: Mahatma Gandhi wanted to win India’s freedom without violence. He became famous all over the world for this.
36615.m: Mahatma Gandhi fought without violence for a free India.

36617.q: What is the capital of Brazil?
36617.e: The capital of Brazil is Brasília. Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo are bigger, but they are not the capital.
36617.m: The capital of Brazil is Brasília.

36618.q: What is special about the city of Brasília?
a: It was newly planned and built
It is the oldest city in the world
36618.e: Brasília was planned from scratch on empty land and built in just a few years. The city was meant to be a modern capital.
36618.m: Brasília is a capital that was planned on the drawing board.

36619.q: In which year was Brasília opened as the capital?
36619.e: Brasília was inaugurated on 21 April 1960. Since then it has been the capital of Brazil.
36619.m: Brasília has been the capital since 1960.

36620.q: Which city was the capital of Brazil before Brasília?
36620.e: Rio de Janeiro on the coast used to be the capital. Then the government moved to the newly built Brasília.
36620.m: Rio de Janeiro used to be the capital of Brazil.

36621.q: What does the street plan of Brasília look like from above?
36621.e: The town planner Lúcio Costa designed the city with two axes. From above it looks like an aeroplane or a bird.
36621.m: The plan of Brasília looks like an aeroplane.

36622.q: Which language is spoken in Brasília?
36622.e: Brazil used to be a colony of Portugal. That is why people in Brasília and all over Brazil speak Portuguese.

36623.q: Why did Brazil build its capital in the interior of the country?
a: So that the interior of the country would grow
36623.e: Brasília is almost in the middle of the country. The government wanted the interior of Brazil to get more people and jobs too.
36623.m: Brasília is in the middle of Brazil so that the whole country develops.

36624.q: What is the name of the large square in Brasília where the parliament, government and supreme court stand?
36624.e: In Portuguese it is called “Praça dos Três Poderes”. The buildings for parliament, government and the court stand close together there.
36624.m: In Brasília, parliament, government and court stand on Three Powers Square.

36625.q: In which part of Brazil was Brasília built?
a: In the interior of the country
On an island in the Atlantic
In the middle of the Amazon rainforest
36625.e: Brasília was built on a plateau in the interior of the country. That way the interior of Brazil would grow too, not just the coast.
36625.m: Brasília is in the interior of Brazil.

36626.q: Which two languages are official languages in Canada?
36626.e: In Canada, English and French are official languages. In the province of Québec, most people speak French.
36626.m: In Canada, people speak English and French.

36627.q: Who is the head of state of Canada (as of 2026)?
36627.e: Canada is a monarchy and part of the Commonwealth. The British King Charles III is also King of Canada.
36627.m: The King of Canada is Charles III.

36628.q: Who leads the government of Canada?
36628.e: In Canada, the Prime Minister leads the government. He sits in parliament in Ottawa.
36628.m: In Canada, the Prime Minister leads the government.

36630.q: What do people do on the Rideau Canal in Ottawa in winter?
36630.e: In winter, the Rideau Canal freezes over. Then it is one of the longest ice rinks in the world.
36630.m: In winter you can go ice skating on a canal in Ottawa.

36632.q: Which large animal lives in the forests of Canada?
36632.e: Moose live in the great forests of Canada. They are the largest deer in the world.

36633.q: Which two cities in Australia argued about which would become the capital?
36633.e: Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to become the capital. So a completely new city, Canberra, was built between them.
36633.m: Canberra was built because Sydney and Melbourne could not agree.

36634.q: How did the city of Canberra come about?
a: It was an old fishing village
It was a gold rush town
36634.e: There was a competition for the best city plan for Canberra. Then the city was built on almost empty land.

36635.q: What is special about Canberra, the capital of Australia?
a: It was planned and built especially as the capital
It is the largest city in Australia
It is on an island off Australia
36635.e: Canberra was planned as the new capital from 1913, because Sydney and Melbourne could not agree. The city plan was designed by the architect Walter Burley Griffin.

36636.q: What do adult Australians have to do at elections?
a: They are not allowed to vote
36636.e: In Australia, voting is compulsory. Anyone who does not vote without a good reason has to pay a small fine.

36637.q: Who is the head of state of Australia (as of 2026)?
36637.e: Australia is a monarchy in the Commonwealth. The British King Charles III is also King of Australia.
36637.m: The King of Australia is Charles III.

36638.q: Which two animals hold up the coat of arms of Australia?
36638.e: A kangaroo and an emu stand on the coat of arms. Both animals are typical of Australia.
36638.m: A kangaroo and an emu hold the Australian coat of arms.

36640.q: How many capitals does South Africa have?
36640.e: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein. Each has a different job.

36641.q: In which of South Africa’s capitals does the government work?
36641.e: Pretoria is the seat of the government and the president. Parliament is in Cape Town.
36641.m: The government of South Africa works in Pretoria.

36642.q: In which city in South Africa does parliament meet?
36642.e: The South African parliament is based in Cape Town by the sea. The government, on the other hand, works in Pretoria.
36642.m: The South African parliament sits in Cape Town.

36643.q: Which animals can you see in the wild in South Africa?
36643.e: South Africa has large nature parks. Lions, elephants, rhinos and giraffes live there in the wild.
36643.m: Lions and elephants live in the wild in South Africa.

36644.q: Who became the first black president of South Africa in 1994?
36644.e: Nelson Mandela was in prison for a long time because he fought against apartheid. In 1994 he became president.
36644.m: Nelson Mandela was the first black president of South Africa.

36645.q: Which of these languages is an official language of South Africa?
36645.e: Since 2023, South Africa has had twelve official languages, including English, Afrikaans, isiZulu and sign language.
36645.m: South Africa has many official languages, and one of them is English.

36646.q: In which city does the President of South Africa have his office?
36646.e: The president works in the Union Buildings on a hill above Pretoria. Pretoria is the seat of government of South Africa.
36646.m: The President of South Africa works in Pretoria.

36647.q: What is the money in South Africa called?
36647.e: In South Africa, people pay with the rand. The name comes from a range of hills where gold was found.
36647.m: In South Africa, people pay with rand.

36648.q: What is the union of almost all the countries of Africa called?
36648.e: In the African Union, the countries of Africa work together, for example for peace and trade.
36648.m: The countries of Africa work together in the African Union.

36649.q: In which city does the African Union have its headquarters?
36649.e: The seat of the African Union is in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia.
36649.m: The African Union has its seat in Addis Ababa.

36650.q: In which year was the African Union founded?
36650.e: The African Union was founded in 2002. It replaced an older organisation.
36650.m: The African Union has existed since 2002.

36651.q: How many members does the African Union have (as of 2026)?
36651.e: The African Union has 55 member states. All the countries of Africa belong to it.

36652.q: Which picture is in the middle of the flag of the African Union?
36652.e: The flag is green and shows a map of the continent of Africa in the middle. Around it is a circle of golden stars.
36652.m: Africa is shown on the flag of the African Union.

36653.q: Which organisation existed before the African Union?
36653.e: The Organisation of African Unity was founded in 1963. Later it became the African Union.
36653.m: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity.

36654.q: What do the countries of the African Union want to achieve together?
a: A single language for all of Africa
36654.e: In the African Union, the countries of Africa work together. They want to secure peace and strengthen trade with each other.
36654.m: The African Union works for peace and cooperation in Africa.

36655.q: In which country does the African Union have its seat today?
36655.e: The seat of the African Union is in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia.
36655.m: The African Union has its seat in Ethiopia.

36656.q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
36656.e: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand. Auckland is the largest city, but not the capital.
36656.m: The capital of New Zealand is Wellington.

36657.q: Which is the southernmost capital of a country in the world?
36657.e: Wellington lies very far south on Earth. No other capital of a country lies further south.
36657.m: Wellington is the southernmost capital in the world.

36658.q: New Zealand lies far away in the ocean. What does the country mainly consist of?
36658.e: New Zealand mainly consists of two large islands, the North Island and the South Island. There are also many small islands.
36658.m: New Zealand mainly consists of two large islands.

36659.q: Where is New Zealand, seen from Switzerland?
a: On the other side of the Earth
Right up at the North Pole
36659.e: New Zealand lies almost exactly on the other side of the Earth. When it is winter here, it is summer there.
36659.m: New Zealand is on the other side of the Earth.

36660.q: Which country was the first to give women the right to vote, in 1893?
36660.e: In 1893, women in New Zealand were the first to be allowed to vote in a whole country. In Switzerland, women only got the vote in 1971.
36660.m: New Zealand was the first country to give women the right to vote.

36661.q: What is the name of the people who lived in New Zealand before the Europeans?
36661.e: The Māori came to New Zealand by boat many hundreds of years ago. Their language is an official language today.
36661.m: The Māori are the first inhabitants of New Zealand.

36662.q: Which bird is the symbol of New Zealand?
36662.e: The kiwi is a small bird that cannot fly. It lives only in New Zealand.
36662.m: The kiwi is New Zealand’s bird.

36663.q: What is New Zealand called in the Māori language?
36663.e: Aotearoa means something like “land of the long white cloud”. Many people in New Zealand use this name.
36663.m: The Māori call New Zealand Aotearoa.

36664.q: Who is the head of state of Thailand?
36664.e: Thailand is a kingdom. The king is the head of state, and a Prime Minister leads the government.
36664.m: Thailand is headed by a king.

36666.q: How long was King Bhumibol King of Thailand?
36666.e: King Bhumibol reigned from 1946 to 2016, so for 70 years. He was one of the longest-reigning kings ever.
36666.m: King Bhumibol was King of Thailand for 70 years.

36667.q: What is the capital of Thailand?
36667.e: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand. The Grand Palace is there too.
36667.m: The capital of Thailand is Bangkok.

36668.q: What was Thailand called in the past?
36668.e: The country was called Siam for a long time. The name Thailand was introduced in 1939 and has been final since 1949. That is where the word “Siamese cat” comes from, for example.
36668.m: Thailand used to be called Siam.

36669.q: What do people in Thailand do in the cinema when the royal anthem is played?
36669.e: Before the film, the cinema often plays the anthem in honour of the king. Out of respect, the audience stands up.
36669.m: In Thailand, people stand up for the royal anthem in the cinema.

36670.q: What is the famous royal palace in Bangkok called?
36670.e: The Grand Palace in Bangkok was the home of the kings for a long time. Today many tourists visit it.
36670.m: The Grand Palace in Bangkok is a famous royal palace.

36671.q: What does the number in the royal title “Rama X” in Thailand show?
36671.e: The kings of today’s royal family are also called Rama with a number. Today’s king is Rama X, the tenth king of this family.
36671.m: The number after Rama shows which number king he is.

36672.q: What is the capital of Egypt?
36672.e: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt. The government and parliament work there.
36672.m: The capital of Egypt is Cairo.

36673.e: Cairo is on the Nile, one of the longest rivers in the world. Almost all Egyptians live close to the Nile.
36673.m: Cairo is on the River Nile.

36674.q: Which famous ancient buildings stand on the edge of Cairo?
36674.e: The Pyramids of Giza are over 4,500 years old. They stand right next to the big city of Cairo.
36674.m: The Pyramids of Giza are near Cairo.

36675.q: Which language is spoken in Egypt?
36675.e: The official language of Egypt is Arabic. Cairo is the largest city in the Arab world.

36676.q: Who is the head of state in Egypt?
36676.e: Egypt is a republic with a president at the top. Pharaohs existed in ancient Egypt a very long time ago.
36676.m: Today Egypt has a president and no longer a pharaoh.

36677.q: What is the weather usually like in Egypt?
36677.e: A large part of Egypt is desert. The sun shines almost all the time there and it very rarely rains.
36677.m: In Egypt it is usually hot and dry.

36678.q: What is the money in Egypt called?
36678.e: In Egypt, people pay with the Egyptian pound. Some banknotes show ancient temples.
36678.m: In Egypt, people pay with the pound.

36679.q: Which important shipping canal is in Egypt?
36679.e: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea. This means ships do not have to sail all the way round Africa.
36679.m: The Suez Canal in Egypt is an important shortcut for ships.

36680.q: What is the capital of Argentina?
36680.e: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina. Santiago is the capital of Chile.
36680.m: The capital of Argentina is Buenos Aires.

36681.q: What does the name Buenos Aires mean in English?
36681.e: Buenos Aires is Spanish and means “good airs” or “good winds”. The city was named after a patron saint of sailors who was supposed to bring good wind.

36682.q: Which language is spoken in Argentina?
36682.e: Argentina used to be a colony of Spain. That is why Spanish is the national language.

36683.q: What colour is the presidential palace in Buenos Aires?
36683.e: The presidential palace is called “Casa Rosada”, which means “pink house”. The President of Argentina works there.
36683.m: The President of Argentina works in the pink house.

36684.q: Which dance comes from Buenos Aires?
36684.e: The tango began over 100 years ago in Buenos Aires and Montevideo. Today it is danced all over the world.
36684.m: The tango comes from Buenos Aires.

36685.q: On which wide stretch of water does Buenos Aires lie?
36685.e: Buenos Aires lies on the Río de la Plata. This river mouth is very wide, and you can hardly see the other bank.
36685.m: Buenos Aires lies on the Río de la Plata.

36686.q: Which pope was born in Buenos Aires?
36686.e: Pope Francis’s real name was Jorge Mario Bergoglio. He was born in Buenos Aires in 1936 and was pope from 2013 to 2025.
36686.m: Pope Francis came from Buenos Aires.

36687.q: Who is the head of state of Argentina?
36687.e: Argentina is a republic. The people elect the president, who leads the country.
36687.m: In Argentina, the people elect a president.

36688.q: What is the money in Argentina called?
36688.e: In Argentina, people pay with the Argentine peso. Other countries in Latin America have a peso too.
36688.m: In Argentina, people pay with pesos.

36689.q: What is the capital of Kenya?
36689.e: Nairobi is the capital and largest city of Kenya. Mombasa is a port city by the sea.
36689.m: The capital of Kenya is Nairobi.

36690.q: Which wild animals can you see in Kenya?
36690.e: Lions, giraffes, zebras and elephants live in Kenya’s national parks. At Nairobi National Park you can even see the city’s tower blocks.
36690.m: Lions and giraffes live in Kenya.

36691.q: Which two languages are official languages in Kenya?
36691.e: In Kenya, Swahili and English are official languages. People also speak many other languages.
36691.m: In Kenya, people speak Swahili and English.

36692.q: How do you say “hello” in Swahili in Kenya?
36692.e: “Jambo” is a well-known greeting in Swahili. Swahili is spoken in many countries in East Africa.
36692.m: In Swahili, you greet people with “Jambo”.

36693.q: In which year did Kenya become independent?
36693.e: Kenya was a colony of Great Britain. It became independent on 12 December 1963.

36694.q: Which line around the Earth runs right through Kenya?
36694.e: The equator divides the Earth into a northern and a southern half. It runs right through the middle of Kenya.

36695.q: Which United Nations organisation has its headquarters in Nairobi?
36695.e: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has its seat in Nairobi. It works to protect nature.
36695.m: The UN Environment Programme is based in Nairobi.

36696.q: Who is the head of state of Kenya?
36696.e: Kenya is a republic. The people elect a president, who also leads the government.
36696.m: In Kenya, an elected president leads the country.

36697.e: Kenya is in East Africa. Many wild animals such as lions and elephants live there.

36698.q: What does the name “United Nations” express?
a: One country rules all the others
All countries have the same language
36698.e: Nations are countries, and united means joined together. In the UN, almost all the countries of the world work together.
36698.m: In the United Nations, many countries have joined together.

36699.q: After which great war was the UN founded?
36699.e: The Second World War ended in 1945. In the same year, countries founded the UN so that something like that would never happen again.
36699.m: The UN was founded at the end of the Second World War.

36700.q: When it was founded in 1945, did the UN have more or fewer members than today?
36700.e: At the beginning there were 51 countries. Today there are 193, because many countries only became independent or joined later.
36700.m: The UN has grown a lot since it was founded.

36701.q: What was the name of the UN’s forerunner, which had its seat in Geneva?
36701.e: The League of Nations was founded after the First World War. It could not prevent the Second World War, so the UN came afterwards.
36701.m: Before the UN there was the League of Nations.

36702.q: Which American president had the idea for the name “United Nations”?
36702.e: Franklin D. Roosevelt suggested this name. He died in April 1945, shortly before the UN was founded.
36702.m: The name “United Nations” comes from Franklin D. Roosevelt.

36703.q: How old did the UN turn in 2025?
36703.e: The UN was founded in 1945. From 1945 to 2025 is 80 years.
36703.m: In 2025 the UN celebrated its 80th birthday.

36704.q: What is the French abbreviation for the UN?
36704.e: In French the UN is called “Organisation des Nations Unies”, or ONU for short. That is what people say in French-speaking Switzerland too.
36704.m: In French-speaking Switzerland, people call the UN “ONU”.

36705.q: What does the “O” in the abbreviation UNO stand for?
36705.e: UNO comes from the English “United Nations Organization”. That means the organisation of the United Nations.
36705.m: The UNO is the Organization of the United Nations.

36706.q: On which river is the UN headquarters in New York?
36706.e: The UN headquarters is in Manhattan, right on the East River. From there you can look out over the water.
36706.m: The UN headquarters is on the East River in New York.

36707.q: In which part of New York is the UN headquarters?
36707.e: The headquarters is in the borough of Manhattan. There are lots of skyscrapers there.
36707.m: The UN has its headquarters in Manhattan.

36708.q: What does the UN Secretariat building in New York look like?
36708.e: The Secretariat building is a narrow skyscraper with 39 floors on the East River. The Secretary-General works there too.
36708.m: The UN Secretariat in New York is a narrow skyscraper.

36709.q: What stands in a long row in front of the UN headquarters?
36709.e: The flags of the member countries fly in front of the building. They are arranged in alphabetical order.
36709.m: Many national flags fly in front of the UN headquarters.

36710.q: Which sculpture with a knotted barrel stands at the UN headquarters?
36710.e: The sculpture is called “Non-Violence”. The pistol with the knot in it can no longer shoot.
36710.m: The knotted pistol at the UN stands for non-violence.

36711.q: Which rich family gave the UN money for the land in New York?
36711.e: In 1946, John D. Rockefeller Junior gave the money to buy the land on the East River. The headquarters was built on it.
36711.m: The land for the UN headquarters was bought with money from the Rockefeller family.

36712.q: When was the UN headquarters in New York finished?
36712.e: The Secretariat skyscraper was finished in 1952. Before that, the UN worked in other places in and around New York.
36712.m: The UN headquarters has stood since the 1950s.

36713.q: In which Austrian city does the UN also have a seat?
36713.e: As well as New York and Geneva, the UN also has a large seat in Vienna. The UN City is there.
36713.m: There is also a large UN seat in Vienna.

36714.q: In which African city does the UN have a large seat?
36714.e: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya. The UN has its largest seat in Africa there.
36714.m: The UN has a large seat in Nairobi in Kenya.

36715.q: What do you call the person who leads the UN?
36715.e: The Secretary-General is the most senior employee of the UN. He speaks for the UN and leads its work.
36715.m: The UN is led by a Secretary-General.

36716.q: What is the name of the UN Secretary-General who took office in 2017 (as of 2025)?
36716.e: António Guterres has been Secretary-General since 1 January 2017. His second term lasts until the end of 2026.
36716.m: António Guterres has been UN Secretary-General since 2017.

36718.q: Who proposes a person to the General Assembly as Secretary-General?
36718.e: The Security Council recommends a person. Then the General Assembly elects the Secretary-General.
36718.m: The UN Secretary-General is proposed by the Security Council.

36719.q: Which country did Kofi Annan, a former UN Secretary-General, come from?
36719.e: Kofi Annan came from Ghana in West Africa. He was Secretary-General from 1997 to 2006.

36720.q: Which famous prize did Kofi Annan receive in 2001?
36720.e: Kofi Annan and the UN received the Nobel Peace Prize together in 2001. They were honoured for their work for a more peaceful world.
36720.m: Kofi Annan received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001.

36721.q: How long is one term of office of the UN Secretary-General?
36721.e: The Secretary-General is elected for five years. After that, he can be elected once more.
36721.m: One term of the UN Secretary-General lasts five years.
