36722.q: The first UN Secretary-General, Trygve Lie, came from a country in northern Europe. Which one?
36722.e: Trygve Lie was Norwegian. From 1946 he was the first Secretary-General of the UN.
36722.m: The first UN Secretary-General came from Norway.

36723.q: How many women had been UN Secretary-General by 2025?
36723.e: Up to 2025, all nine Secretaries-General were men. Many countries would like a woman to be elected one day.
36723.m: By 2025 the UN had never had a female Secretary-General.

36724.q: Which country became the most recent UN member so far, in 2011 (as of 2025)?
36724.e: South Sudan became a separate state in 2011. Shortly afterwards it became the 193rd member of the UN.
36724.m: The newest UN member is South Sudan.

36725.q: Which small state in Rome is not a UN member, only an observer?
36725.e: The Holy See in the Vatican is only an observer at the UN. San Marino, Monaco and Liechtenstein, on the other hand, are full members.
36725.m: The Vatican is only an observer at the UN.

36726.q: Is our neighbouring country Liechtenstein a member of the UN?
36726.e: Liechtenstein joined the UN back in 1990. That was twelve years before Switzerland.
36726.m: Liechtenstein has been a member of the UN since 1990.

36727.q: In which year did our neighbouring country Austria become a UN member?
36727.e: Austria became fully independent again in 1955. In the same year it joined the UN.
36727.m: Austria has been in the UN since 1955.

36728.q: Why were two German states members of the UN from 1973 to 1990?
a: Germany was divided at that time
Each country was allowed two seats
Germany wanted twice as many votes
36728.e: After the Second World War, Germany was divided into West Germany and East Germany (GDR). Both joined the UN in 1973. Since reunification in 1990, there has only been one Germany.
36728.m: Divided Germany had two seats in the UN until 1990.

36729.q: What do all UN member countries have in common in the General Assembly?
a: They all have the same number of inhabitants
36729.e: Big or small, each member country has exactly one vote in the General Assembly. So Switzerland counts just as much as China.
36729.m: In the UN General Assembly, each country has one vote.

36730.q: Which countries are allowed to join the UN?
36730.e: According to the UN Charter, peace-loving states can become members. The Security Council and the General Assembly must agree.
36730.m: Any peace-loving state can become a UN member.

36731.q: Which continent do most UN member countries come from?
36731.e: Africa has 54 countries, and all of them are members of the UN. No other continent has so many.
36731.m: Most UN members are in Africa.

36732.q: Who sits in the UN General Assembly?
36732.e: All 193 member countries are represented in the General Assembly. It is like a big parliament of the world.
36732.m: All UN countries take part in the General Assembly.

36733.q: In which month does the big session of the General Assembly begin every year?
36733.e: In September, many presidents come to New York. There they give their speeches to the General Assembly.
36733.m: The General Assembly begins every year in September.

36734.q: In which city does the UN General Assembly normally meet?
36734.e: The General Assembly meets in the great hall of the UN headquarters. This is in New York.
36734.m: The General Assembly meets in New York.

36735.q: How long does the President of the General Assembly stay in office?
36735.e: The General Assembly elects a new president every year. That way, countries from different regions of the world get a turn.
36735.m: The General Assembly has a new leader every year.

36736.q: How many sustainability goals did the General Assembly agree on in 2015?
36736.e: The 17 goals are called the “Sustainable Development Goals”. They are meant, for example, to reduce hunger and poverty by 2030.
36736.m: The UN has 17 goals for sustainable development.

36737.q: What are most decisions of the General Assembly?
36737.e: The General Assembly can usually only give the countries recommendations. But they carry great weight, because almost every country in the world has a say.
36737.m: The General Assembly mainly gives countries recommendations.

36738.q: Who decides how much money the UN may spend?
36738.e: The General Assembly decides the UN budget. It also decides how much each country has to pay.
36738.m: The General Assembly decides about the UN’s money.

36739.q: Which countries meet in the UN General Assembly?
a: All the countries of the UN
36739.e: All the countries of the UN come together in the General Assembly. Every country is allowed to have its say there.
36739.m: All the countries of the UN meet in the General Assembly.

36740.q: How many countries sit on the UN Security Council?
36740.e: The Security Council has 15 members. Some of them are always there, and the others are elected.
36740.m: 15 countries sit on the Security Council.

36741.q: How many countries are permanently on the Security Council?
36741.e: These five big countries are always on it. The other seats change.
36741.m: The Security Council has five permanent members.

36742.q: Which of these countries is a permanent member of the Security Council?
36742.e: France is one of the five permanent members. Germany, Italy and Spain can only be elected for a certain time.
36742.m: France has a permanent seat on the Security Council.

36743.q: What is the right of the permanent members to stop a decision called?
36743.e: Veto is Latin and means “I forbid”. If a permanent member says no, the decision does not go through.
36743.m: The permanent members can block decisions with their veto.

36744.q: For how long are the non-permanent members elected?
36744.e: Every year the General Assembly elects five new countries for two years. So there are always ten elected countries on the Council.
36744.m: Elected members stay on the Security Council for two years.

36745.q: What is the Security Council mainly responsible for?
36745.e: The Security Council is supposed to prevent and end wars. For example, it can decide on punishments against a country.
36745.m: The Security Council looks after peace in the world.

36746.q: How often does the presidency of the Security Council change?
36746.e: Each member holds the presidency for one month. The order follows the English alphabet.
36746.m: On the Security Council, the presidency changes every month.

36747.q: Which country in Asia is a permanent member of the Security Council?
36747.e: China is one of the five permanent members. Japan and India would also like a permanent seat.
36747.m: China has a permanent seat on the Security Council.

36748.q: What must all UN countries do with the decisions of the Security Council?
36748.e: Decisions of the Security Council are binding for all members. That is written in the UN Charter.
36748.m: All UN countries must follow the decisions of the Security Council.

36749.q: When are Blue Helmets allowed to use their weapons?
36749.e: Blue Helmets are not supposed to wage war. They may only use force to defend themselves and their mission.
36749.m: Blue Helmets only use their weapons in self-defence.

36750.q: Which big prize did the Blue Helmets receive in 1988?
36750.e: The UN peacekeeping forces received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1988. This honoured their dangerous work.
36750.m: The Blue Helmets received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1988.

36751.q: Where do the Blue Helmet soldiers come from?
36751.e: The UN does not have its own army. Member countries send soldiers and police officers voluntarily.
36751.m: The Blue Helmets are provided by the member countries.

36752.q: Who usually decides whether Blue Helmets are sent to a country?
36752.e: The Security Council decides on the UN’s peace missions. It also decides what the Blue Helmets should do.
36752.m: The Security Council sends out the Blue Helmets.

36753.q: In which year did the first UN peace mission begin?
36753.e: In 1948 the UN sent observers to the Middle East for the first time. They were to monitor a ceasefire.
36753.m: The UN has been sending peace missions around the world since 1948.

36754.q: What colour are the vehicles of the UN peacekeeping forces usually?
36754.e: UN vehicles are white and have the black letters “UN” on them. That way you can recognise them from far away.
36754.m: Vehicles of the UN peacekeeping forces are usually white.

36755.q: Does Switzerland also send people on UN peace missions?
36755.e: The Swiss Army sends unarmed military observers and experts on UN missions. They help to monitor the peace.
36755.m: Swiss people also help with UN peace missions.

36756.q: What colour are the caps and helmets of the peacekeeping forces?
36756.e: The helmets and caps are light blue. That is where the name Blue Helmets comes from.
36756.m: UN peacekeeping forces wear light blue helmets.

36757.q: What is shown in the middle of the UN flag?
36757.e: A map of the world can be seen in the middle. It shows that the UN is there for all countries.
36757.m: The UN flag shows a map of the world.

36758.q: Is a company allowed to use the UN flag in its advertising?
36758.e: The UN flag rules forbid using the flag for advertising or to make money. It is only a sign of the UN.
36758.m: The UN flag must not be used for advertising.

36759.q: What colour is the emblem on the UN flag?
36759.e: The map of the world and the branches are white. They are on a light blue background.
36759.m: The emblem on the UN flag is white.

36760.q: What do the olive branches on the UN flag stand for?
36760.e: Olive branches have been a sign of peace for a long time. They frame the map of the world.
36760.m: The olive branches on the UN flag mean peace.

36761.q: Which point on Earth is in the middle of the world map on the UN flag?
36761.e: The world map shows the Earth from above the North Pole. That way all countries are arranged around the middle.
36761.m: The North Pole is in the middle of the UN flag.

36762.q: What colour is the background of the UN flag?
36762.e: The UN flag shows a white emblem on a light blue background. Light blue is the colour of the UN.
36762.m: The UN flag is light blue.

36763.q: Which continent is missing from the world map on the UN flag?
36763.e: The map shows the Earth from the North Pole down to about 60 degrees south. So Antarctica, right in the south, cannot be seen.
36763.m: Antarctica is missing from the UN flag.

36764.q: What does the UN flag on a car or a tent show?
36764.e: The UN flag is the identifying sign of the United Nations. UN vehicles and camps are marked with it.
36764.m: The UN flag shows what belongs to the UN.

36765.q: How was the decision on joining the UN made in Switzerland?
36765.e: In March 2002, the people and the cantons voted on joining and narrowly said yes. In September 2002, Switzerland was admitted.
36765.m: In 2002 the Swiss people decided on joining the UN.

36766.q: Which number member of the UN did Switzerland become?
36766.e: Switzerland was admitted in 2002 as the 190th country. Shortly afterwards East Timor followed.
36766.m: Switzerland is the 190th member of the UN.

36767.q: What was the result of the first vote on joining the UN in 1986?
36767.e: In 1986, about three quarters of voters said no. Only at the second vote in 2002 was there a yes.
36767.m: In 1986, Switzerland first said no to the UN.

36768.q: In which building in Geneva did the League of Nations work?
36768.e: The League of Nations built the Palais des Nations in Geneva. Today the large UN office in Europe is there.
36768.m: The League of Nations used to work in the Palais des Nations in Geneva.

36769.q: In which years did Switzerland sit on the UN Security Council for the first time?
36769.e: Switzerland was elected by the General Assembly in 2022. It was on the Council in 2023 and 2024 as a non-permanent member.
36769.m: Switzerland was on the UN Security Council in 2023 and 2024.

36770.q: What is special about the giant wooden chair in front of the UN in Geneva?
36770.e: The sculpture “Broken Chair” has a broken leg. It is a reminder of people injured by landmines.
36770.m: The Broken Chair in Geneva remembers the victims of landmines.

36771.q: Roughly how many voters said yes to joining the UN in 2002?
36771.e: About 55 per cent of voters said yes. Among the cantons, too, it was very close.
36771.m: In 2002, Switzerland narrowly said yes to the UN.

36772.q: What are the Swiss troops serving for peace in Kosovo called?
36772.e: Swisscoy has been helping in Kosovo since 1999. It is based on a decision of the UN Security Council.
36772.m: Swisscoy is a Swiss Army peace mission in Kosovo.

36773.q: Which language is an official language of the UN?
36773.e: Spanish is one of the six official languages. It is spoken in Spain and in many countries in the Americas.
36773.m: Spanish is an official language of the UN.

36774.q: Which Swiss national language is also an official language of the UN?
36774.e: French is one of the six official languages of the UN. The other Swiss national languages are not.
36774.m: Of our national languages, only French is an official UN language.

36776.q: Which language from Asia is an official language of the UN?
36776.e: Chinese is one of the six official languages. Hindi, Korean and Thai are not.
36776.m: Chinese is an official language of the UN.

36777.q: Who makes sure that everyone at the UN understands a speech?
36777.e: Interpreters translate every speech straight away into the other official languages. The listeners wear headphones for this.
36777.m: At the UN, interpreters translate the speeches into all the official languages.

36778.q: Which language from Eastern Europe is an official language of the UN?
36778.e: Russian is one of the six official languages of the UN. Polish, Ukrainian and Czech are not.
36778.m: Russian is an official language of the UN.

36779.q: Which two languages are used most in the UN Secretariat for daily work?
36779.e: English and French are the working languages of the Secretariat. The staff usually write their texts in them.
36779.m: The working languages of the UN Secretariat are English and French.

36780.q: What is the Spanish abbreviation for the UN?
36780.e: In Spanish the UN is called “Organización de las Naciones Unidas”. The first letters make ONU.
36780.m: In Spanish the UN is abbreviated to ONU.

36781.q: On which date is United Nations Day?
36781.e: On this day in 1945, the UN was officially founded.
36781.m: United Nations Day is on 24 October.

36782.q: What did the UN recommend to its member countries in 1971 for United Nations Day?
a: To make it a public holiday
To move it to the summer
To celebrate it only in New York
To celebrate it only every ten years
36782.e: In 1971 the General Assembly recommended that countries make this day a public holiday. Not all countries do so.
36782.m: The UN recommended celebrating United Nations Day as a public holiday.

36783.q: What is celebrated on United Nations Day?
36783.e: On 24 October 1945, the UN officially began its work. That is why this day is like the UN’s birthday.
36783.m: On United Nations Day, people celebrate the UN’s birthday.

36784.q: Since which year has United Nations Day existed?
36784.e: The General Assembly decided in 1947 to celebrate this day. From 1948 it was marked every year.
36784.m: United Nations Day has existed since 1948.

36785.q: In which colour are famous buildings often lit up on 24 October?
36785.e: For United Nations Day, many buildings are lit up in UN blue. This shows their support for the UN.
36785.m: On United Nations Day, many buildings light up blue.

36786.q: What does the UN Secretary-General publish every year for United Nations Day?
36786.e: Every year the Secretary-General writes a message for this day. In it he reminds people of the goals of the UN.
36786.m: For United Nations Day there is a message from the Secretary-General.

36787.q: What came into force on 24 October 1945?
36787.e: On this day, enough countries had signed and confirmed the Charter. With that, the UN was officially founded.
36787.m: The UN Charter has been in force since 24 October 1945.

36788.q: What do the United Nations mainly want to achieve?
36788.e: In the United Nations, or UN for short, almost all the countries of the world work together. They want to prevent wars and protect peace.
36788.m: The United Nations work for peace.

a: The founding treaty of the UN
36789.e: The Charter is like the constitution of the UN. It contains the goals and rules of the organisation.
36789.m: The UN Charter is the founding treaty of the United Nations.

36790.q: In which city was the UN Charter signed in 1945?
36790.e: Many countries had met there for a big conference. At the end they signed the Charter.
36790.m: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco.

36791.q: In which year was the UN Charter signed and the UN founded?
36791.e: The UN Charter was signed in 1945, shortly after the end of the Second World War. It came into force in October 1945.

36792.q: With which words does the UN Charter begin?
a: In the name of the King
36792.e: The Charter begins with “We the peoples of the United Nations”. This is meant to show that it applies to all people.
36792.m: The UN Charter begins with the words “We the peoples”.

36793.q: Which goal comes first in the UN Charter?
36793.e: The first goal of the UN is to maintain peace and security in the world. Other goals are friendship and cooperation between countries.
36793.m: The first goal of the UN Charter is world peace.

36794.q: According to the Charter, how should UN countries settle disputes?
36794.e: The Charter requires countries to settle disputes by peaceful means. Using force against other countries is forbidden.
36794.m: According to the UN Charter, countries should settle their disputes peacefully.

36795.q: What does the UN Charter allow a country to do if it is attacked?
36795.e: Article 51 of the Charter allows an attacked country to defend itself. Then the Security Council is supposed to restore peace.
36795.m: According to the UN Charter, an attacked country may defend itself.

36796.q: Who is expressly named in the UN Charter as having equal rights alongside men?
36796.e: The equal rights of men and women are already mentioned in the introduction to the Charter. That was something special in 1945.
36796.m: The UN Charter says women and men have equal rights.

36797.q: What is the series of speeches by heads of state in September called?
36797.e: In the General Debate, each country speaks to the General Assembly. Many heads of state travel to New York for it.
36797.m: In the General Debate, countries speak to the whole world.

36798.q: What does the “C” in UNICEF stand for?
36798.e: At the beginning, UNICEF was called the “United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund”.
36798.m: The name UNICEF contains the word children.

36799.q: In which city does UNICEF have its headquarters?
36799.e: UNICEF’s headquarters is in New York, near the UN headquarters.
36799.m: UNICEF has its headquarters in New York.

36800.q: Which famous prize did UNICEF receive in 1965?
36800.e: UNICEF received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965 for its help for children.
36800.m: UNICEF received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.

36801.q: What does the UNICEF logo show?
36801.e: The logo shows a mother holding up her child in front of a globe. It stands for protecting children.
36801.m: In the UNICEF logo, a mother holds up her child.

36802.q: Which award does UNICEF Switzerland give to municipalities that do a lot for children?
36802.e: Municipalities can receive the label “Child-Friendly Municipality” from UNICEF Switzerland and Liechtenstein. To get it, they must take children’s opinions seriously.
36802.m: Child-friendly municipalities get a label from UNICEF.

36803.q: Which UN agreement on children’s rights is especially important for UNICEF?
a: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
36803.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child sets out children’s rights. UNICEF works all over the world to make sure they are respected.
36803.m: UNICEF fights for the rights in the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

36804.q: What does UNICEF bring to villages without clean water, for example?
36804.e: UNICEF builds wells and hands out water filters and tablets so that children have clean drinking water. Dirty water makes people ill.
36804.m: Clean water protects children from diseases.

36805.q: What is the most important yearly meeting of all WHO countries called?
36805.e: Once a year, the WHO countries meet in Geneva for the World Health Assembly. There they decide on the most important tasks.
36805.m: The WHO countries meet every year at the World Health Assembly.

36806.q: In which Swiss city is the WHO headquarters?
36806.e: The WHO has its headquarters in Geneva. Many international organisations work in Geneva.
36806.m: The WHO has its seat in Geneva.

36807.q: In which year was the WHO founded?
36807.e: The WHO was founded in 1948, shortly after the UN. It belongs to the United Nations family.

36808.q: On which day is World Health Day every year?
36808.e: World Health Day marks the founding of the WHO every year. Each year it has a different theme.
36808.m: World Health Day is on 7 April.

36809.q: Which animal can be seen in the WHO logo?
36809.e: In the logo, a snake winds around a staff. This Rod of Asclepius is an ancient sign of the art of healing.
36809.m: The snake on a staff is a sign of medicine.

36810.q: What does the WHO do when a dangerous disease spreads around the world?
36810.e: The WHO watches diseases all over the world. It warns countries and gives advice on how to protect yourself.
36810.m: The WHO warns the world about dangerous diseases.

36811.q: What does the WHO draw attention to on World No Tobacco Day on 31 May?
36811.e: Smoking is very bad for your health. Since 1988, the WHO has drawn attention to this every year on 31 May.
36811.m: On World No Tobacco Day, the WHO warns about smoking.

36812.q: What is the title of the person who leads the WHO?
36812.e: The WHO is led by a Director-General. Since 2017 this has been Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus from Ethiopia.
36812.m: The WHO is led by a Director-General.

36813.q: According to the WHO, roughly how long should children be active every day?
36813.e: The WHO recommends that children and teenagers are active for at least 60 minutes a day on average. Running around, cycling and sport all count.
36813.m: Children should be active for about an hour every day.

36814.q: In which city does UNESCO have its headquarters?
36814.e: UNESCO has its headquarters in Paris, the capital of France.
36814.m: UNESCO has its seat in Paris.

36815.q: In which year was UNESCO founded?
36815.e: UNESCO was founded in London in November 1945. Its aim is peace through education, science and culture.

36816.q: What does the “E” in UNESCO stand for?
36816.e: UNESCO stands for “United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization”. The “E” stands for education.
36816.m: The E in UNESCO stands for education.

36817.q: Which Swiss custom has been on a UNESCO list of living traditions since 2017?
36817.e: Basel Carnival was added to the UNESCO list of intangible cultural heritage in 2017. This list protects customs and traditions.
36817.m: Basel Carnival is UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.

36818.q: Which Swiss craft has been UNESCO intangible cultural heritage since 2020?
36818.e: The craft of watchmaking in the Jura Arc of Switzerland and France was recognised by UNESCO in 2020.
36818.m: Watchmaking is part of UNESCO’s cultural heritage.

36819.q: Which day about languages does UNESCO celebrate every year on 21 February?
36819.e: UNESCO introduced this day in 1999. It reminds us how valuable the world’s many languages are.
36819.m: 21 February is International Mother Language Day.

36820.q: What is a UNESCO protected area where people and nature should live well together called?
36820.e: In a biosphere reserve, nature is protected, and at the same time people may live and work there. There are such areas in Switzerland too.
36820.m: In a biosphere reserve, people and nature live together.

36821.q: Which UNESCO biosphere reserve is in the canton of Lucerne?
36821.e: The UNESCO Biosphere Entlebuch in the canton of Lucerne was recognised in 2001. There are many moors there.
36821.m: The Entlebuch is a UNESCO biosphere.

36822.q: What does the WFP give some families instead of sacks of food?
36822.e: Where there is enough food at the market, families get money or vouchers. That way they can buy food themselves, and local traders earn money too.
36822.m: The WFP also helps with money and vouchers for food.

36823.q: In which city does the World Food Programme have its headquarters?
36823.e: The WFP has its headquarters in Rome, the capital of Italy.
36823.m: The World Food Programme is based in Rome.

36824.q: Which prize did the World Food Programme receive in 2020?
36824.e: The WFP received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for its work against hunger.
36824.m: The WFP won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020.

36825.q: In which year was the World Food Programme founded?
36825.e: The WFP was founded in 1961. Two years later it began its work.
36825.m: The World Food Programme has existed since 1961.

36826.q: How does the WFP get food to areas without roads?
36826.e: If no roads lead there, the WFP flies in aid. Sometimes sacks of food are even dropped from the aeroplane.
36826.m: The WFP also flies food to remote areas.

36827.q: When does the World Food Programme help especially quickly?
36827.e: After earthquakes, floods or in wars, people often suddenly have nothing left to eat. Then the WFP quickly brings food.
36827.m: After disasters, the WFP quickly brings food.

36828.q: What colour are many of the World Food Programme’s sacks and lorries?
36828.e: The WFP’s aid supplies and vehicles are usually white and carry the organisation’s blue logo. That makes them easy to recognise.
36828.m: You can recognise the WFP by its blue logo on white.

36829.q: What do hungry young children often get from the WFP?
36829.e: For young children there is enriched special food with lots of vitamins and minerals. This helps them grow up healthy.
36829.m: Special food helps hungry young children to grow.

36830.q: What title does the person at the head of the UNHCR have?
36830.e: The UNHCR is headed by a High Commissioner for Refugees. This person is elected by the UN General Assembly.
36830.m: The UNHCR is led by a High Commissioner.

36831.q: What is the prize that the UNHCR gives every year to people who help refugees called?
36831.e: The prize is named after the Norwegian Fridtjof Nansen, who worked for refugees early on. The UNHCR has awarded it since 1954.
36831.m: The Nansen Refugee Award honours people who help refugees.

36832.q: In which year was the UNHCR founded?
36832.e: The UNHCR was founded in December 1950. After the Second World War there were millions of refugees in Europe.

36833.q: Which important prize has the UNHCR received twice?
36833.e: The UNHCR received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981 for its help for refugees.
36833.m: The UNHCR has received the Nobel Peace Prize twice.

36834.q: What does the UNHCR logo show?
36834.e: In the blue UNHCR logo, two hands surround a small figure. This shows that refugees are given protection.
36834.m: The UNHCR logo stands for protecting refugees.

36835.q: What does the UNHCR hand out to families who have no roof over their heads?
36835.e: Refugee families get tents, blankets, mats and cooking pots from the UNHCR. That way they have the bare essentials.
36835.m: The UNHCR gives refugees tents and blankets.

36836.q: What does the “R” in UNHCR stand for?
36836.e: UNHCR stands for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. The UNHCR is the UN Refugee Agency.
36836.m: The R in UNHCR stands for refugees.

36837.q: Who does the UN Refugee Agency help?
a: People who have fled their homes
36837.e: The UN Refugee Agency is called UNHCR for short. It helps people who have had to leave their homes because of war or danger.
36837.m: The UNHCR helps people who have fled their homes.

36838.q: According to the FAO, why are bees so important for our food?
36838.e: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower. Without this pollination there would be much less fruit and vegetables.
36838.m: Bees pollinate many plants that feed us.

36839.q: In which city does the FAO have its headquarters?
36839.e: The FAO has had its headquarters in Rome since 1951.
36839.m: The FAO has its seat in Rome.

36840.q: In which year was the FAO founded?
36840.e: The FAO was founded in Canada on 16 October 1945.

36841.q: Which world day on 16 October each year marks the founding of the FAO?
36841.e: 16 October is World Food Day. It reminds us that not everyone has enough to eat.

36842.q: Which food is shown in the FAO logo?
36842.e: The FAO logo shows an ear of wheat and the Latin words “Fiat panis”. That means “Let there be bread”.
36842.m: The ear of wheat in the FAO logo stands for bread for everyone.

36843.q: What does the FAO show farmers in poor countries, for example?
36843.e: The FAO teaches farmers better growing methods, for example for watering, seeds and protection against pests.
36843.m: With good irrigation, more food grows.

36844.q: Which areas does the FAO also look after, besides fields?
36844.e: The FAO’s work also includes fishing and forests. They provide food too and are important for many people.
36844.m: The FAO also protects fish stocks and forests.

36845.q: What does the “F” in FAO stand for?
36845.e: FAO stands for “Food and Agriculture Organization”.
36845.m: FAO stands for Food and Agriculture Organization.

36846.q: What does the WMO keep about the weather all over the world, for example?
a: A list of the highest mountains
A list of the biggest cities
36846.e: The WMO collects the hottest, coldest and wettest measurements in the world. Experts check carefully whether a new record is correct.
36846.m: The WMO checks and collects weather records.

36847.q: What do weather stations all over the world measure for the WMO, for example?
36847.e: Thousands of weather stations measure temperature, rain, wind and air pressure. The data is shared through the WMO.
36847.m: Weather stations measure temperature, wind and rain.

36848.q: Which day does the WMO celebrate every year on 23 March?
36848.e: On this day the WMO’s founding agreement came into force. That is why it is World Meteorological Day.

36849.q: In which year was the World Meteorological Organization founded?
36849.e: The WMO has existed since 1950. It replaced an older weather organisation from 1873.

36850.q: What does the WMO decide for tropical storms?
36850.e: The WMO keeps lists of names for hurricanes and other tropical storms. That way everyone knows which storm is meant. Nobody can decide where a storm goes.
36850.m: Tropical storms get their names from WMO lists.

36851.q: Which Swiss office works with the WMO on the weather?
36851.e: MeteoSwiss is the federal weather service. It shares weather data with the WMO and other countries.

36852.q: Why do countries share weather data through the WMO?
a: Because they want to save money
36852.e: Clouds and storms move across national borders. For good forecasts, you need measurements from all over the world.
36852.m: Good weather forecasts need data from all over the world.

36853.q: Which climate panel did the WMO set up in 1988 together with the UN Environment Programme?
a: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
36853.e: The IPCC gathers what research knows about climate change. It was set up in 1988 by the WMO and the UN Environment Programme.
36853.m: The IPCC explains the state of climate research.

36854.q: What is the UN Environment Programme’s award for people who protect the environment called?
36854.e: Since 2005, UNEP has honoured people and groups every year with the “Champions of the Earth” award.
36854.m: The “Champions of the Earth” award honours people who protect the environment.

36855.q: For which animals is there a special protection agreement under the UN Environment Programme?
a: For migratory animals such as migrating birds
36855.e: Many animals migrate across many national borders. An agreement from 1979 makes sure that countries protect them together.
36855.m: Migratory animals need protection in many countries.

36856.q: In which city did the big environmental conference take place in 1972 that led to UNEP?
36856.e: In June 1972, many countries met in Stockholm in Sweden for the first big UN environmental conference. Afterwards UNEP was founded.
36856.m: UNEP came about after the Stockholm environmental conference.

36857.q: In which year was the UN Environment Programme founded?
36857.e: UNEP was founded in 1972 after the first big UN environmental conference.
36857.m: The UN Environment Programme has existed since 1972.

36858.q: According to the UN Environment Programme, what is thrown away far too often in the world?
36858.e: UNEP measures how much food ends up in the rubbish in homes, shops and restaurants. Throwing away less food is good for the environment.
36858.m: If you don’t throw food away, you protect the environment.

36859.q: Which rubbish in the sea does the UN Environment Programme especially fight against?
36859.e: Plastic breaks down only very slowly in the sea and harms fish, birds and turtles. That is why UNEP calls for a fight against plastic waste.
36859.m: Plastic rubbish in the sea harms many animals.

36860.q: Which protective layer of the Earth is the UN Environment Programme helping to save?
36860.e: The ozone layer protects us from dangerous rays from the sun. Thanks to an agreement from 1987, it is slowly recovering.
36860.m: The ozone layer protects us from strong sun rays.

36861.q: What is the 1987 agreement that protects the ozone layer called?
36861.e: In the Montreal Protocol, countries agreed to ban substances that destroy the ozone layer.
36861.m: The Montreal Protocol protects the ozone layer.

36862.q: According to the ILO’s first agreement from 1919, what was the maximum number of hours a day people should work?
36862.e: The very first ILO agreement set the eight-hour day and a maximum of 48 hours a week for factories.
36862.m: The ILO worked for the eight-hour day early on.

36863.q: In which year was the International Labour Organization founded?
36863.e: The ILO was founded in 1919 after the First World War. That makes it older than the UN itself.

36864.q: What does the ILO especially fight against, so that children can go to school?
36864.e: Many children in the world have to work instead of going to school. The ILO works to get rid of child labour.
36864.m: Children should learn and play instead of working.

36865.q: Which prize did the International Labour Organization receive in 1969?
36865.e: For its 50th birthday in 1969, the ILO received the Nobel Peace Prize.
36865.m: The ILO received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969.

36866.q: Who sits at the table at the ILO alongside governments?
36866.e: At the ILO, governments, employers and workers talk together. This is meant to create fair rules for work.
36866.m: At the ILO, three groups decide together.

36867.q: What does the letter “L” in ILO stand for?
36867.e: ILO stands for “International Labour Organization”. The word “labour” means work.
36867.m: ILO stands for International Labour Organization.

36868.q: What is one aim of the International Labour Organization?
36868.e: The ILO wants people to work safely, be paid fairly and have enough time to rest.
36868.m: Good work is safe and fairly paid.

36869.q: Which Swiss city has an old town that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
36869.e: The old town of Bern with its arcades and fountains has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
36869.m: Bern’s old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

36870.q: Which abbey in eastern Switzerland with a famous library is a World Heritage Site?
36870.e: The Abbey precinct of St Gallen with its Abbey Library has been on the World Heritage list since 1983.
36870.m: The Abbey of St Gallen is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

36871.q: Which glacier area in the Swiss Alps is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
36871.e: The Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch area with the great Aletsch Glacier became a World Heritage Site in 2001.
36871.m: Jungfrau-Aletsch is a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site.

36872.q: Which railway lines in the Grisons are UNESCO World Heritage?
36872.e: The Albula and Bernina lines of the Rhaetian Railway have been World Heritage since 2008. They cross many viaducts and run through spiral tunnels.
36872.m: The Albula and Bernina lines are UNESCO World Heritage.

36873.q: Which castles in Ticino are World Heritage?
36873.e: The three castles of Bellinzona and the town wall have been on the World Heritage list since 2000.
36873.m: The castles of Bellinzona are UNESCO World Heritage.

36874.q: Which vineyards on Lake Geneva are a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
36874.e: The vineyard terraces of Lavaux between Lausanne and Montreux have been World Heritage since 2007.
36874.m: The vineyard terraces of Lavaux are UNESCO World Heritage.

36875.q: Which buildings in Egypt are famous World Heritage?
36875.e: The Pyramids of Giza are over 4,000 years old. They have been UNESCO World Heritage since 1979.
36875.m: The Pyramids of Giza are World Heritage in Egypt.

36876.q: Which very long wall in Asia is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
36876.e: The Great Wall of China is thousands of kilometres long. It has been on the World Heritage list since 1987.
36876.m: The Great Wall of China is UNESCO World Heritage.

36877.q: Which coral reef off Australia is World Natural Heritage?
36877.e: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef on Earth. It has been World Natural Heritage since 1981.
36877.m: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world.

36878.q: What does a vaccination protect you from?
36878.e: A vaccination trains the body to fight a particular germ. That way you do not get ill, or not as badly.
36878.m: A vaccination trains the body against diseases.

36879.q: Which two UN organisations work closely together on vaccination campaigns for children?
36879.e: The WHO gives the recommendations, and UNICEF buys and distributes many of the vaccines for children.
36879.m: WHO and UNICEF vaccinate children around the world together.

36880.q: What is another name for the disease polio?
36880.e: Polio is also called infantile paralysis. The disease can paralyse arms and legs and has almost been wiped out with vaccinations.
36880.m: Polio is also called infantile paralysis.

36881.q: How did children in Switzerland get the polio vaccine in the past?
36881.e: The oral polio vaccine used to be dripped onto a piece of sugar. Today in Switzerland it is given with an injection.
36881.m: The oral vaccine used to be given on a sugar cube.

36882.q: Why must vaccines stay cold on the way to faraway villages?
a: Because otherwise they no longer work
Because otherwise they turn to ice
36882.e: Many vaccines go off in the heat. That is why they are transported in fridges and cool boxes. This is called the cold chain.
36882.m: Vaccines need an unbroken cold chain.

36883.q: Who carried out one of the first vaccinations against smallpox in 1796?
36883.e: The English doctor Edward Jenner vaccinated a boy with cowpox in 1796. Afterwards the boy was protected against real smallpox.
36883.m: Edward Jenner is seen as the father of the smallpox vaccine.

36884.q: Who usually gives children in Switzerland their vaccinations?
36884.e: Children are usually vaccinated by their paediatrician. Sometimes the school doctor gives vaccinations too.
36884.m: Children usually get their vaccinations from the paediatrician.

36885.q: In which booklet are all vaccinations recorded in Switzerland?
36885.e: The vaccination record shows which vaccinations you have had and when. That way you know whether you are protected.
36885.m: The vaccination record shows all your vaccinations.

36886.q: Against which infectious disease with red spots on the skin do the WHO and UNICEF vaccinate children worldwide?
36886.e: Measles is very infectious and can be dangerous. Every year, millions of children are protected with the measles vaccine.
36886.m: The measles vaccine protects children from a dangerous disease.

36887.q: Which UN organisation provides meals in schools in many countries?
36887.e: The WFP gives schoolchildren a meal in many poor countries. It is one of the largest providers of school meals in the world.
36887.m: The WFP brings school meals to many poor countries.

36888.q: Why do more children come to school when there is food there?
a: Because they can be sure of getting enough to eat there
36888.e: In poor families there is often not enough food. If the school gives a meal, parents are more willing to send their children to school.
36888.m: A school meal attracts children to school.

36889.q: What happens when children are hungry at school?
a: They find it hard to concentrate
36889.e: It is hard to think on an empty stomach. A school meal gives you energy for learning.
36889.m: You learn better with a full tummy.

36890.q: Who else does it help when a school buys its food from local farmers?
36890.e: When schools buy food from farmers nearby, the farmers earn money too. So a school meal helps twice over.
36890.m: Local school food helps the farmers too.

36891.q: In some programmes, what do children take home in addition to their school meal?
36891.e: Some programmes give children, often girls, food to take home for the family. That makes it worthwhile for parents to send their children to school.
36891.m: Take-home food helps the whole family.

36892.q: What is the lunchtime care with a meal at school called in Switzerland?
36892.e: Many Swiss schools offer a Mittagstisch. There, children eat together if they do not go home at lunchtime.
36892.m: At the Mittagstisch, schoolchildren eat together.

36893.q: What do Swiss children call the snack they often eat at morning break?
36893.e: The Znüni is eaten in the morning, at about nine o’clock. The Zvieri is eaten in the afternoon.
36893.m: The Znüni is eaten at morning break.

36894.q: What should a healthy school meal contain?
36894.e: A healthy meal is varied. Vegetables, grains and foods rich in protein such as beans give you strength for learning.
36894.m: Varied food gives you strength for learning.

36895.q: In which city is the Palais des Nations?
36895.e: The Palais des Nations is in Geneva. It is the most important seat of the UN in Europe.
36895.m: The Palais des Nations is in Geneva.

36896.q: Which big organisation works in the Palais des Nations today?
36896.e: Since 1946 the Palais des Nations has belonged to the UN. It is its most important seat after New York.
36896.m: The UN works in the Palais des Nations.

36897.q: For which organisation was the Palais des Nations originally built?
36897.e: The Palais des Nations was built for the League of Nations. The League of Nations moved into the new building in 1936.
36897.m: The Palais des Nations was first the home of the League of Nations.

36898.q: Why do representatives of many countries meet in the Palais des Nations?
a: For sessions of the Swiss parliament
36898.e: Thousands of meetings and conferences take place in the Palais des Nations every year. Countries look for solutions to problems together there.
36898.m: In the Palais des Nations, countries negotiate with each other.

36899.q: In which Swiss city is the UN’s Palais des Nations?
36899.e: The Palais des Nations is in Geneva. Peacocks even walk around freely in the park around it.
36899.m: The Palais des Nations is in Geneva.

36900.q: Roughly how long is the Palais des Nations?
36900.e: The Palais des Nations is about 600 metres long. That makes it one of the largest buildings in Europe.
36900.m: The Palais des Nations is about 600 metres long.

36901.q: What can you see in a long row in front of the Palais des Nations?
a: The flags of the UN member states
The coats of arms of all Swiss cantons
The flags of all football clubs
36901.e: The flags of the UN member states fly in front of the entrance. They show that countries from all over the world work together here.
36901.m: The flags of the UN countries fly in front of the Palais des Nations.

36902.q: What can school classes do at the Palais des Nations?
36902.e: Every year about 100,000 people visit the Palais des Nations on a guided tour. You get to see large halls.
36902.m: You can go on a guided tour of the Palais des Nations.

36903.q: Which UN body meets regularly in the Palais des Nations?
36903.e: The UN Human Rights Council meets in the Human Rights Room in Geneva. This room has a famous colourful ceiling by the artist Miquel Barceló.
36903.m: The UN Human Rights Council meets in Geneva.

36904.q: What is the “Broken Chair” in Geneva?
36904.e: The Broken Chair is a giant wooden chair. It stands in front of the Palais des Nations.
36904.m: The Broken Chair is a giant chair in Geneva.

36905.q: What is broken on the Broken Chair?
36905.e: Part of one leg is missing from the chair. That is why it is called the “Broken Chair”.
36905.m: Part of one leg is missing from the Broken Chair.

36906.q: What is the Broken Chair made of?
36906.e: The Broken Chair is a wooden sculpture. A carpenter built it.
36906.m: The Broken Chair is made of wood.

36907.q: Roughly how tall is the Broken Chair?
36907.e: The Broken Chair is about 12 metres tall. That is as tall as a house with four floors.
36907.m: The Broken Chair is about 12 metres tall.

36908.q: What does the Broken Chair remind us of?
36908.e: Landmines are weapons hidden in the ground. Many people lose a leg because of them. The broken chair leg reminds us of these victims.
36908.m: The Broken Chair remembers the victims of landmines.

36909.q: Where is the Broken Chair sculpture?
a: In front of the UN seat in Geneva
In front of the Federal Palace in Bern
In front of the UN headquarters in New York
36909.e: The Broken Chair stands on the Place des Nations in front of the Palais des Nations in Geneva. It was designed by the Geneva artist Daniel Berset.
36909.m: The Broken Chair stands in front of the UN in Geneva.

36910.q: On which square in Geneva is the Broken Chair?
36910.e: The Broken Chair stands on the Place des Nations, opposite the Palais des Nations.
36910.m: The Broken Chair stands on the Place des Nations.

36912.q: How many whole legs does the Broken Chair in Geneva have?
36912.e: The giant wooden chair has three whole legs, and the fourth is broken off. It was put up in 1997.
36912.m: The Broken Chair is missing a leg.

36913.q: In which year was the Red Cross founded in Geneva?
36913.e: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863. Henry Dunant and four other men from Geneva were there at the start.
36913.m: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863.

36914.q: How many men founded the committee in Geneva that became the Red Cross?
36914.e: The committee was made up of five men from Geneva, including Henry Dunant and General Dufour. That is why it is also called the Committee of Five.
36914.m: Five men from Geneva founded the Red Cross committee in 1863.

36915.q: Which flag does the Red Cross emblem come from?
36915.e: The colours of the Swiss flag were swapped. The white cross on red became a red cross on white.
36915.m: The Red Cross emblem is the Swiss flag with the colours swapped.

36916.q: Which emblem do many countries use instead of the Red Cross?
36916.e: In many countries the organisation is called the Red Crescent. It helps just like the Red Cross.
36916.m: Many countries use the Red Crescent as their emblem.

36917.q: Who does the Red Cross especially help in war?
36917.e: The Red Cross helps all the wounded and prisoners. It does not matter which side they are on.
36917.m: The Red Cross helps all the wounded, whatever side they are on.

36918.q: What is the Red Cross called in Switzerland?
36918.e: The Swiss Red Cross, SRC for short, helps in Switzerland, for example with blood donations and transport services.
36918.m: In Switzerland there is the Swiss Red Cross.

36919.q: What does the Swiss Red Cross help with, for example?
36919.e: The Swiss Red Cross blood donation service collects blood. It helps people who are ill or injured.
36919.m: Giving blood can help people who are ill.

36920.q: Which third protective emblem has existed since 2005 alongside the Red Cross and Red Crescent?
36920.e: The Red Crystal is a red square standing on one corner. It was agreed in 2005 as the third protective emblem.
36920.m: The Red Crystal is the third protective emblem.

36921.q: What is the abbreviation for the Red Cross committee based in Geneva?
36921.e: ICRC stands for International Committee of the Red Cross. It helps mainly in wars.
36921.m: The International Committee of the Red Cross is called the ICRC for short.

36922.q: Where did Henry Dunant see a great battle with many wounded in 1859?
36922.e: After the Battle of Solferino, thousands of wounded lay on the ground. Dunant helped them together with women from the area.
36922.m: At Solferino, Henry Dunant saw the suffering of the wounded.

36924.q: What is the title of the book Henry Dunant wrote?
36924.e: In the book “A Memory of Solferino”, Dunant describes the suffering of the wounded. The book made many people think.
36924.m: Henry Dunant wrote the book “A Memory of Solferino”.

36926.q: In which village in Appenzell did Henry Dunant spend the last years of his life?
36926.e: Henry Dunant lived last in the hospital in Heiden in the Appenzell region. He died there in 1910.
36926.m: Henry Dunant died in Heiden in 1910.

36927.q: On which day is World Red Cross Day, Henry Dunant’s birthday?
36927.e: Henry Dunant was born on 8 May 1828. That is why World Red Cross Day is celebrated on 8 May.
36927.m: World Red Cross Day is on 8 May.

36928.q: What was Henry Dunant’s job before he founded the Red Cross?
36928.e: Henry Dunant was a businessman. He travelled to Italy because he was looking for help with his business.
36928.m: Henry Dunant was a businessman by profession.

36929.q: In which city is the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum?
36929.e: The museum is in Geneva, right next to the headquarters of the ICRC.
36929.m: The Red Cross Museum is in Geneva.

36930.q: What does the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum in Geneva show?
36930.e: The museum opened in 1988. It shows how people are helped in wars and disasters.
36930.m: The Red Cross Museum shows the history of humanitarian aid.

36931.q: What does the Red Cross Museum in Geneva tell you about?
36931.e: The museum shows how people are helped in wars and disasters.
36931.m: The Red Cross Museum shows help for people in need.

36932.q: Which famous medal does the Red Cross Museum own?
a: The first Nobel Peace Prize medal
The first football World Cup medal
36932.e: The museum owns the medal of the first Nobel Peace Prize from 1901. Henry Dunant had received this prize.
36932.m: The Red Cross Museum owns the first Nobel Peace Prize medal.

36933.q: What does the Red Cross Museum show from the time of the First World War?
a: Index cards about prisoners of war
36933.e: In the First World War, millions of index cards were written about prisoners. That way families found their relatives again.
36933.m: Index cards helped families find prisoners again.

36935.q: Which emblems can you see at the Red Cross Museum in Geneva?
a: A red cross and a red crescent
A white cross on a red background
36935.e: The museum is called the Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum. That is why it shows both emblems of the helpers: the red cross and the red crescent.
36935.m: The Red Cross Museum shows the red cross and the red crescent.

36936.q: What is part of the Red Cross Museum’s collection?
36936.e: The collection includes about 30,000 objects, for example photos, posters and letters from the history of humanitarian aid.
36936.m: The Red Cross Museum collects photos, posters and letters.

36937.q: Who do the Geneva Conventions protect at sea?
36937.e: A separate agreement protects the wounded and shipwrecked at sea. They must be rescued and cared for.
36937.m: The Geneva Conventions also protect shipwrecked people.

36938.q: In which year was the first Geneva Convention signed?
36938.e: The first Geneva Convention was signed in Geneva in 1864. Twelve states took part at the beginning.
36938.m: The first Geneva Convention dates from 1864.

36939.q: Who did the very first Geneva Convention protect?
36939.e: The first Geneva Convention protected wounded soldiers and the helpers who cared for them.
36939.m: The first Geneva Convention protected wounded soldiers.

36940.q: In which year were today’s Geneva Conventions agreed?
36940.e: After the Second World War, the Geneva Conventions were rewritten in 1949. They still apply today.

36941.q: Who do the Geneva Conventions protect, for example?
36941.e: Prisoners of war must be treated well. They must not be tortured and must be given food.
36941.m: Prisoners of war must be treated well.

36942.q: Which country keeps the original documents of the Geneva Conventions?
36942.e: Switzerland is the depositary state. It keeps the treaties and invites countries to conferences.

36943.q: How many states have accepted the Geneva Conventions of 1949?
a: All the states in the world
36943.e: All the states in the world have accepted the Geneva Conventions of 1949. That is true of hardly any other treaty.
36943.m: All the states in the world have accepted the Geneva Conventions.

36944.q: According to the Geneva Conventions, what must not be attacked in war?
36944.e: Hospitals with the protective emblem must not be attacked. The wounded are cared for there.
36944.m: Hospitals must not be attacked in war.

36945.q: What do you call a country’s representation at the UN in Geneva?
36945.e: Almost every country has a Permanent Mission in Geneva. Diplomats work there.
36945.m: A country has a Permanent Mission at the UN in Geneva.

36946.q: Which languages do you hear especially often among diplomats in Geneva?
36946.e: English and French are the most important working languages at the UN in Geneva. French is also the language of the city.
36946.m: In international Geneva, people often speak English and French.

36947.q: Roughly how many international organisations have their seat in Geneva (as of 2023)?
36947.e: At the end of 2023 there were 38 international organisations in Geneva. There are also hundreds of aid organisations.
36947.m: About 40 international organisations have their seat in Geneva.

36948.q: Which organisation in Geneva looks after the weather worldwide?
36948.e: The World Meteorological Organization, WMO for short, has its seat in Geneva. It collects weather data from all over the world.
36948.m: The World Meteorological Organization in Geneva looks after the weather.

36949.q: What is Switzerland called when it welcomes international organisations?
36949.e: Switzerland is the host state. For example, it provides security and helps with building offices.
36949.m: Switzerland is the host state for many organisations.

36950.q: Roughly how many people work for international organisations in Geneva (as of 2023)?
36950.e: In 2023, about 28,700 people worked for international organisations in Geneva.
36950.m: Almost 30,000 people work for international organisations in Geneva.

36951.q: Which organisation based in Geneva looks after refugees?
36951.e: The UNHCR is the UN Refugee Agency. It has its headquarters in Geneva.
36951.m: The UN Refugee Agency UNHCR has its seat in Geneva.

36952.q: Which organisation based in Geneva works for good working conditions?
36952.e: The International Labour Organization ILO works for fair work. It also fights against child labour.
36952.m: The International Labour Organization is based in Geneva.

36953.q: Why is Geneva often called the “city of peace”?
a: Because peace is often negotiated there
36953.e: Countries that are in dispute often meet in Geneva. They talk about peace there.
36953.m: Geneva is a city where peace is often negotiated.

36954.q: What is Switzerland’s help called when it brings opposing sides to the table?
36954.e: Switzerland offers what are called good offices. It organises meetings and mediates between countries.
36954.m: Switzerland offers good offices to opposing sides.

36955.q: In which year did the leaders of four great powers meet in Geneva for the first big summit after the Second World War?
36955.e: In 1955, the leaders of the USA, the Soviet Union, Great Britain and France met in Geneva. They talked about peace in Europe.
36955.m: In 1955, a big summit of four great powers took place in Geneva.

36956.q: Why do peace talks take place in Geneva especially often?
a: Switzerland is neutral and there are many international organisations in Geneva
Geneva is the capital of Switzerland
Most of the world’s presidents live in Geneva
Geneva does not belong to any country
36956.e: Switzerland does not take sides and is seen as a reliable host. The UN and many other organisations also have a seat in Geneva. That is why countries that are in dispute often meet there.
36956.m: Thanks to neutral Switzerland, Geneva is a popular place for peace talks.

36957.q: Which countries negotiated in Geneva in 2013 about one country’s nuclear programme?
36957.e: In November 2013, Iran and six great powers agreed on a first plan for Iran’s nuclear programme in Geneva.
36957.m: In 2013, Iran’s nuclear programme was negotiated in Geneva.

36958.q: Which war in Southeast Asia was negotiated in Geneva in 1954?
36958.e: At the Geneva Conference on Indochina in 1954, the end of the Indochina War was negotiated.
36958.m: In 1954, the Indochina War was negotiated in Geneva.

36959.q: About which country in the Middle East were peace talks held in Geneva from 2012?
36959.e: Because of the civil war in Syria, representatives met again and again in Geneva from 2012 to talk about peace.
36959.m: Peace in Syria was negotiated in Geneva.

36960.q: What does a mediator do in peace talks?
a: Helps both sides to reach an agreement
36960.e: A mediator does not take sides. She helps both sides to find a solution.
36960.m: A mediator helps two sides to reach an agreement.

36961.q: What is the Jet d’Eau in Geneva?
36961.e: The Jet d’Eau is a huge jet of water in Lake Geneva. It is the landmark of Geneva.
36961.m: The Jet d’Eau is a tall jet of water in Geneva.

36962.q: Roughly how high does the Jet d’Eau shoot?
36962.e: The Jet d’Eau shoots water about 140 metres into the air. That is higher than a church tower.
36962.m: The Jet d’Eau shoots about 140 metres high.

36963.q: In which lake is the Jet d’Eau?
36963.e: The Jet d’Eau is in Lake Geneva, where the Rhône flows out of the lake.
36963.m: The Jet d’Eau is in Lake Geneva.

36964.q: How many litres of water does the Jet d’Eau pump per second?
36964.e: The Jet d’Eau pumps about 500 litres of water per second. That is about three full bathtubs.
36964.m: The Jet d’Eau pumps about 500 litres per second.

36965.q: How fast does the water shoot out of the nozzle of the Jet d’Eau?
36965.e: The water leaves the nozzle at about 200 kilometres per hour. That is faster than a car on the motorway.
36965.m: The water of the Jet d’Eau travels at about 200 km/h.

36966.q: Where does the water for the Jet d’Eau come from today?
36966.e: Since 1951, the Jet d’Eau has pumped water from Lake Geneva. The water falls back into the lake.
36966.m: The Jet d’Eau gets its water from Lake Geneva.

36967.q: When is the Jet d’Eau switched off?
a: When there is frost or strong wind
36967.e: When there is frost or strong wind, the Jet d’Eau is switched off. Otherwise the water would freeze or soak people.
36967.m: In frost and strong wind, the Jet d’Eau is off.

36968.q: Why was there a first Jet d’Eau in 1886?
a: As a safety valve for water pipes
As a clock for the city
36968.e: The first Jet d’Eau was a safety valve. It let excess pressure out of the water pipes.
36968.m: The first Jet d’Eau was a safety valve.

36969.q: What colour is the Jet d’Eau usually when it is lit up at night?
36969.e: At night the Jet d’Eau is usually lit up in white. On special days it also shines in other colours.
36969.m: At night the Jet d’Eau usually shines white.

36970.q: What is the abbreviation for the World Health Organization?
36970.m: The World Health Organization is called WHO for short.

36971.q: Which childhood disease does the WHO fight with an oral vaccine?
36971.e: Polio is also called infantile paralysis. Thanks to vaccinations, it hardly exists anywhere in the world any more.

36972.q: Which disease spread by mosquitoes does the WHO fight especially in Africa?
36972.e: Malaria is spread by certain mosquitoes. The WHO helps with mosquito nets, medicines and vaccines.

36973.q: Because of which disease did the WHO declare a pandemic in 2020?
36973.e: In March 2020, the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic. A pandemic is a disease that spreads all over the world.
36973.m: In 2020, the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic.

36974.q: Which dangerous disease has the WHO defeated completely with vaccinations?
36974.e: Thanks to vaccinations around the world, smallpox no longer exists. The WHO announced this in 1980.

36975.q: What does the World Health Organization work for?
36975.e: The WHO wants all people to be able to live as healthily as possible. For example, it helps with vaccinations.
36975.m: The WHO works for the health of all people.

36976.q: Which big organisation does the World Health Organization belong to?
36976.e: The WHO is a specialised agency of the UN. It only deals with health.
36976.m: The WHO belongs to the UN.

36977.q: What does the WHO recommend so that diseases spread less?
36977.e: Soap and water wash away many germs. That is why the WHO recommends washing your hands often.
36977.m: Washing your hands often protects you from diseases.

36978.q: Who has led the World Health Organization since 2017 (as of 2026)?
36978.e: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus from Ethiopia has been Director-General of the WHO since 2017 (as of 2026).
36978.m: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has led the WHO since 2017.

36979.q: What is special about an international school?
a: Children from many countries learn together
36979.e: At an international school, children from many countries learn together. Their parents often work for international organisations.
36979.m: At international schools, children from many countries learn together.

36980.q: Who was the International School of Geneva founded for in 1924?
a: For children of League of Nations staff
36980.e: The International School of Geneva was founded in 1924. It was meant for the children of people working for the League of Nations.
36980.m: The International School of Geneva began for the children of League of Nations staff.

36981.q: In which city is the oldest international school in the world?
36981.e: The International School of Geneva was founded in 1924. It is considered the oldest international school in the world.
36981.m: The oldest international school is in Geneva.

36982.q: In which two languages is teaching mainly done at the International School of Geneva?
36982.e: At the International School of Geneva, children learn mainly in English and French.
36982.m: The International School of Geneva teaches in English and French.

36983.q: Which school qualification was invented in Geneva and is recognised almost everywhere in the world?
36983.e: Teachers at the International School of Geneva developed the International Baccalaureate in the 1960s.
36983.m: The International Baccalaureate was developed in Geneva.

36984.q: In which language do children often learn at international schools?
36984.e: At international schools, lessons are often in English. That way children from many countries can learn together.
36984.m: At international schools, you often learn in English.

36985.q: Why are there many international schools in Geneva?
a: Because many families from all over the world work there
Because Geneva is the largest city in Switzerland
Because Geneva is high up in the mountains
Because Geneva is by the sea
36985.e: Many people in Geneva work for the UN and other organisations. Their children often go to international schools.
36985.m: Geneva has many international schools because families from all over the world live there.

36986.q: Who goes to the International School of Geneva?
36986.e: Children from over a hundred countries learn at the International School of Geneva. Many parents work for international organisations.
36986.m: Children from all over the world learn at the International School of Geneva.

36987.q: What stands in a long row in front of the big UN building in Geneva?
36987.e: In front of the UN building in Geneva, the flags of many countries fly side by side. This path is called the Alley of Flags.
36987.m: The flags of the UN countries fly in the Alley of Flags in Geneva.

36988.q: What is the Alley of Flags at the Palais des Nations called in French?
36988.e: “Drapeau” is the French word for flag. That is why the Alley of Flags in Geneva is called the “Allée des Drapeaux”.
36988.m: In French, the Alley of Flags is called the “Allée des Drapeaux”.

36989.q: Which flags fly in the Alley of Flags in front of the Palais des Nations in Geneva?
a: The flags of the UN member states
The flags of the Swiss cantons
Only the flags of the EU countries
36989.e: The flags of the UN member states fly in front of the Palais des Nations in Geneva. The Palais is the UN’s European seat.
36989.m: The flags of the UN countries fly in the Alley of Flags in Geneva.

36990.q: Why is every flag in the Alley of Flags equally important?
a: Because every country counts the same in the UN
Because all countries are the same size
Because all countries are equally rich
Because all countries are the same age
36990.e: In the UN, every country has one vote. Small and large countries count the same.
36990.m: In the UN, every country counts the same.

36991.q: Roughly how heavy is the Broken Chair?
36991.e: About 5.5 tonnes of wood were used for the Broken Chair. That is as heavy as an elephant.
36991.m: The Broken Chair weighs about 5.5 tonnes.

36992.q: How much water is in the air at the same time at the Jet d’Eau?
36992.e: There are always about 7,000 litres of water in the air at the same time at the Jet d’Eau. That is about 50 full bathtubs.
36992.m: About 7,000 litres of water are in the air at the same time at the Jet d’Eau.

36993.q: Which country became the most recent to join the EU so far, in 2013 (as of 2026)?
36993.e: Croatia became a member of the EU on 1 July 2013. Since then no other country has joined.

36994.q: In which city were the treaties for the European Community signed in 1957?
36994.e: The treaties were signed in Rome in 1957. That is why they are called the Treaties of Rome.
36994.m: The Treaties of Rome were signed in Rome in 1957.

36995.q: How many countries are members of the EU (as of 2026)?
36995.e: The European Union has 27 member states (as of 2026).

36996.q: Which country left the EU in 2020?
36996.e: Great Britain left the EU in 2020. This is called “Brexit”.
36996.m: Great Britain left the EU with Brexit.

36997.q: What do the countries of the EU do together?
36997.e: The countries of the EU work together, for example on trade and protecting the environment. But each country still has its own language.
36997.m: In the EU, many countries work together.

36998.q: What is the parliament of the European Union called?
36998.e: Members from all EU countries sit in the European Parliament. They are elected by the people in the EU.
36998.m: The EU has the European Parliament.

36999.q: Which country is the largest in the EU by area?
36999.e: France has the largest area of all the EU countries.
36999.m: France is the largest EU country by area.

37000.q: Which is the smallest country in the EU?
37000.e: Malta is a small group of islands in the Mediterranean Sea. It is the smallest country in the EU.
37000.m: Malta is the smallest country in the EU.

37001.q: How many countries founded the European Community in 1957?
37001.e: In 1957, six countries started: Germany, France, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. Later this became the EU.
37001.m: The cooperation began in 1957 with six countries.

37002.q: In how many EU countries do people pay with the euro (as of 2026)?
37002.e: 21 EU countries pay with the euro (as of 2026). The others still have their own money.
37002.m: In 2026, 21 EU countries have the euro.

37003.q: Which EU country does not pay with the euro?
37003.e: Sweden is in the EU but has its own currency, the krona.
37003.m: Sweden pays with the krona instead of the euro.

37004.q: Which euro coin has the lowest value?
37004.e: The smallest euro coin is the 1-cent piece. It is copper-coloured.
37004.m: The euro coin with the lowest value is 1 cent.

37005.q: What is the same on one side of every euro coin?
a: The value and a map of Europe
37005.e: One side of every euro coin shows the value and a map of Europe. Each country designs the other side itself.
37005.m: One side of every euro coin shows the value and Europe.

37006.q: Which country introduced the euro on 1 January 2026?
37006.e: Bulgaria got the euro on 1 January 2026. Before that its money was called the lev.
37006.m: Bulgaria has paid with the euro since 2026.

37007.q: Which is the highest-value euro coin?
37007.e: Euro coins go from 1 cent to 2 euros. From 5 euros upwards there are notes.
37007.m: The most valuable euro coin is the 2-euro piece.

37008.q: What is shown on euro banknotes?
37008.e: Euro banknotes show windows, gateways and bridges. They stand for openness and connections in Europe.
37008.m: Euro banknotes show windows, gateways and bridges.

37009.q: What colour is the background of the European flag?
37009.e: The European flag has a blue background. Blue stands for the sky.

37010.q: Where do you see a blue strip with the circle of stars in many EU countries?
37010.e: Many number plates in EU countries have a blue strip on the left with the stars of the European flag.
37010.m: The circle of stars can be seen on many EU number plates.

37011.q: What colour are the stars on the European flag?
37011.e: The twelve stars are golden yellow and shine on the blue background.
37011.m: The stars of the European flag are golden.

37012.q: How are the stars arranged on the European flag?
37012.e: The twelve stars form a circle, a bit like the numbers on a clock face.
37012.m: The stars of the European flag form a circle.

37013.q: What do the twelve stars of the European flag stand for?
37013.e: The number twelve is a sign of completeness and unity. It does not show the number of countries.
37013.m: The twelve stars stand for unity.

37014.q: How many points does each star on the European flag have?
37014.e: Each star on the European flag has five points.
37014.m: Each star on the European flag has five points.

37015.q: Who used the European flag first?
37015.e: The Council of Europe introduced the flag in 1955. Later, in 1985, the EU adopted it too.
37015.m: The European flag comes from the Council of Europe.

37016.q: Does the European flag change when a new country joins the EU?
37016.e: The flag always stays the same with twelve stars. No star is added.
37016.m: The European flag always keeps twelve stars.

37017.q: In which country is the city of Brussels?
37017.e: Brussels is the capital of Belgium.
37017.m: Brussels is the capital of Belgium.

37018.q: Why is Brussels often called the capital of Europe?
37018.e: Important parts of the EU work in Brussels, for example the European Commission.

37019.q: What is the large structure made of shiny spheres in Brussels called?
37019.e: The Atomium was built for the 1958 World’s Fair. It looks like a giant particle made of spheres.
37019.m: The Atomium is a landmark of Brussels.

37020.q: What is the small fountain statue of a boy in Brussels called?
37020.e: The Manneken Pis is a small bronze statue. It is often dressed in different costumes.
37020.m: The Manneken Pis is a famous statue in Brussels.

37021.q: Which sweet treat is famous in Brussels and all of Belgium?
37021.e: Belgium is known for pralines and chocolate, as well as for waffles.
37021.m: Belgium is known for its chocolate.

37022.q: Which languages are mainly spoken in Brussels?
37022.e: In Brussels, French and Dutch are the official languages. Most people speak French.
37022.m: In Brussels, people speak French and Dutch.

37023.q: Which vegetable is named after the city of Brussels?
37023.e: In French, Brussels sprouts are called “choux de Bruxelles”, which means cabbages of Brussels.
37023.m: Brussels sprouts are named after Brussels.

37025.q: In which city does the Council of Europe have its seat?
37025.e: The Council of Europe has its seat in Strasbourg.
37025.m: The Council of Europe is based in Strasbourg.

37026.e: Strasbourg is in Alsace in France, very close to the border with Germany.

37027.q: Is the Council of Europe the same as the EU?
37027.e: The Council of Europe is a separate organisation. It has more members than the EU.
37027.m: The Council of Europe and the EU are two different organisations.

37028.q: Is Switzerland a member of the Council of Europe?
a: No, it is only an observer
37028.e: Switzerland has been a member of the Council of Europe since 1963.
37028.m: Switzerland is a member of the Council of Europe.

37029.q: What does the Council of Europe mainly work for?
37029.e: The Council of Europe protects human rights, democracy and the rule of law in Europe.
37029.m: The Council of Europe protects human rights.

37030.q: In which year was the Council of Europe founded?
37030.e: The Council of Europe was founded in 1949, shortly after the Second World War.
37030.m: The Council of Europe has existed since 1949.

37031.q: Which important court is also in Strasbourg?
a: Court of Justice of the EU
37031.e: The European Court of Human Rights is in Strasbourg. It belongs to the Council of Europe.
37031.m: The Court of Human Rights is in Strasbourg.

37032.q: On which big river is Strasbourg?
37032.e: Strasbourg is on the Rhine. The same river flows through Basel first.

37033.q: What is the piece of music that is the European anthem called?
37033.e: The European anthem is the tune “Ode to Joy”.
37033.m: The European anthem is called “Ode to Joy”.

37034.q: Which famous composer wrote the tune of the European anthem?
37034.e: The tune is by Ludwig van Beethoven, a famous composer from Bonn.
37034.m: Beethoven wrote the tune of the European anthem.

37035.q: Which of Beethoven’s works does the European anthem come from?
37035.e: The “Ode to Joy” is the last part of Beethoven’s 9th Symphony.
37035.m: The European anthem comes from Beethoven’s 9th Symphony.

37036.q: Which poet wrote the poem “Ode to Joy”?
37036.e: The poem “Ode to Joy” is by Friedrich Schiller. Beethoven set it to music.
37036.m: Friedrich Schiller wrote the poem “Ode to Joy”.

37037.q: Is the European anthem officially sung with words?
37037.e: The official European anthem has no words. That way it suits all the languages in Europe.
37037.m: The European anthem is a tune without official words.

37038.q: Which feeling appears in the title of the European anthem?
37038.e: The anthem is called “Ode to Joy”. It is meant to express joy and friendship.
37038.m: The European anthem is about joy.

37039.q: Who was the first to choose the European anthem?
37039.e: The Council of Europe chose the tune in 1972. The EU adopted it in 1985.
37039.m: The Council of Europe chose the European anthem.

37040.q: What was special about Beethoven when he wrote the 9th Symphony?
a: He was only ten years old
37040.e: At that time Beethoven could hardly hear anything. Even so, he wrote this famous music.
37040.m: Beethoven was almost deaf when he wrote the 9th Symphony.

37042.q: Who gave an important speech for Europe on 9 May 1950?
37042.e: On 9 May 1950, Robert Schuman proposed that countries in Europe should work together.
37042.m: Robert Schuman got Europe started on 9 May 1950.

37043.q: Which country did Robert Schuman come from?
37043.e: Robert Schuman was Foreign Minister of France.
37043.m: Robert Schuman was a politician from France.

37044.q: What do many EU buildings do around Europe Day?
a: They open their doors to visitors
They stay closed for a week
They take down all the flags
They hand out free euro coins
37044.e: Around Europe Day, the EU institutions hold open days. Then you can look around them.
37044.m: On Europe Day you can visit many EU buildings.

37045.q: According to Robert Schuman, what should France and Germany manage together?
37045.e: In 1950, Schuman proposed managing coal and steel together. This was meant to stop a new war from starting.
37045.m: The cooperation began with coal and steel.

37046.q: After Schuman’s speech, what was the cooperation mainly meant to achieve?
37046.e: After the Second World War, people wanted the countries of Europe to live in peace.
37046.m: Cooperation in Europe is meant to secure peace.

37048.q: What is usually no longer needed when travelling in the Schengen Area?
37048.e: In the Schengen Area there are usually no fixed checks at the borders between countries any more.
37048.m: In the Schengen Area you usually travel without border checks.

37049.q: In which country is the village of Schengen?
37049.e: Schengen is a small wine village in Luxembourg.
37049.m: Schengen is a village in Luxembourg.

37050.q: Is Switzerland part of the Schengen Area?
a: Yes, even though it is not in the EU
No, because it is not in the EU
37050.e: Switzerland takes part in the Schengen Area even though it is not in the EU.
37050.m: Switzerland is part of the Schengen Area.

37051.q: In which year was the Schengen Agreement signed?
37051.e: The Schengen Agreement was signed in 1985 in Schengen in Luxembourg. Switzerland has taken part since 2008.

37052.q: Why is the Schengen Agreement called that?
a: It was signed near the village of Schengen
It is named after a river
37052.e: The agreement was signed in 1985 near the small village of Schengen in Luxembourg. That is why it has this name.
37052.m: The agreement is named after the village of Schengen.

37053.q: What must you still carry with you when travelling in the Schengen Area?
37053.e: Even without fixed border checks, you can be checked. That is why you must always carry a valid ID.
37053.m: You need ID in the Schengen Area too.

37054.q: Which country is in the Schengen Area but not in the EU?
37054.e: Norway is not an EU country, but it takes part in Schengen. The same is true for Iceland.
37054.m: Norway is in Schengen but not in the EU.

37055.q: Since which year has Switzerland taken part in Schengen?
37055.e: Switzerland has been in the Schengen Area since December 2008. For airports it has applied since March 2009.
37055.m: Switzerland has been in the Schengen Area since 2008.

37056.q: How did the Swiss people vote on the initiative “Yes to Europe!” in 2001?
37056.e: On 4 March 2001, about 77 per cent said no. The initiative wanted quick negotiations on joining the EU.
37056.m: In 2001 the people clearly rejected the initiative “Yes to Europe!”.

37057.q: Who has the final say on important questions about the EU in Switzerland?
37057.e: In Switzerland, the people can vote on important treaties.
37057.m: In Switzerland, the people vote on important questions.

37058.q: What did the Swiss people vote on in the big Europe vote of 1992?
37058.e: In 1992, the Swiss people voted on the European Economic Area, EEA for short.
37058.m: In 1992, Switzerland voted on the EEA.
