37059.q: What was the result of the 1992 EEA vote in Switzerland?
37059.e: On 6 December 1992, the people narrowly said no to the EEA, with about 50.3 per cent voting no.
37059.m: In 1992, Switzerland narrowly said no to the EEA.

37060.q: Which of Switzerland’s neighbours is also not in the EU?
37060.e: Liechtenstein is not a member of the EU. All of Switzerland’s other neighbours are in the EU.
37060.m: Like Switzerland, Liechtenstein is not in the EU.

37061.e: Switzerland borders Germany, France, Italy and Austria. These countries are all in the EU.
37061.m: Four of Switzerland’s neighbours are in the EU.

37062.q: Who does Switzerland trade with the most?
37062.e: The EU is Switzerland’s most important trading partner. Many goods go to EU countries or come from there.
37062.m: The EU is Switzerland’s most important trading partner.

37063.q: Which country, like Switzerland, is also not in the EU?
37063.e: Norway has said no to the EU twice in votes. That is why it is not a member.
37063.m: Like Switzerland, Norway is not in the EU.

37064.q: Can you go on holiday from Switzerland to an EU country?
a: Only with permission from the EU
37064.e: Swiss people can travel to EU countries without any problems, for example to Italy.
37064.m: You can easily travel from Switzerland to EU countries.

37065.q: What are the treaties between Switzerland and the EU called?
37065.e: Switzerland and the EU have made many separate treaties. They are called the bilateral agreements.
37065.m: Switzerland and the EU have bilateral agreements.

37066.e: “Bi” means two. Bilateral means that two sides do something together, here Switzerland and the EU.

37067.q: Who makes the bilateral agreements with each other?
37067.e: In the bilateral agreements, Switzerland and the EU are the two partners.
37067.m: The bilateral agreements are treaties between Switzerland and the EU.

37068.q: What does the free movement of persons allow?
a: Living and working in the EU
Travelling by train in the EU for free
Living in the EU without taxes
Voting in elections in the EU
37068.e: Thanks to the free movement of persons, Swiss people may live and work in EU countries. The same applies the other way round.
37068.m: Free movement of persons allows people to live and work in the other country.

37069.q: In which year did the Swiss people approve the first bilateral agreements?
37069.e: On 21 May 2000, about two thirds of voters said yes to the first package of bilateral agreements.
37069.m: In 2000 the people said yes to the Bilaterals I.

37070.q: Which package of bilateral agreements came first?
a: They all came at the same time
37070.e: The first package is called Bilaterals I and was signed in 1999. Later the Bilaterals II and III followed.
37070.m: The first package of treaties is called Bilaterals I.

37071.q: What is the Land Transport Agreement with the EU about?
37071.e: The Land Transport Agreement regulates traffic with lorries and trains through Switzerland.
37071.m: The Land Transport Agreement regulates lorries and trains.

37072.q: Why does Switzerland make treaties with the EU?
a: To work well together without being a member
To become a member of the EU
37072.e: With the treaties, Switzerland and the EU can work well together in many areas, for example trade. Switzerland stays outside the EU.
37072.m: The treaties help Switzerland and the EU to work together.

37073.q: What do students do with the Erasmus programme?
37073.e: With Erasmus, students can study for a while at a university in another country.
37073.m: With Erasmus you study abroad for a while.

37074.q: Who is the Erasmus programme named after?
37074.e: It is named after Erasmus of Rotterdam, a famous scholar who travelled a lot in Europe.

37075.q: Which city did the scholar Erasmus come from?
37075.e: He was called Erasmus of Rotterdam because he came from Rotterdam in the Netherlands.

37076.q: In which Swiss city is Erasmus of Rotterdam buried?
37076.e: Erasmus died in Basel in 1536. He is buried in Basel Minster.
37076.m: Erasmus of Rotterdam is buried in Basel.

37077.q: In which year did the Erasmus programme begin?
37077.e: The Erasmus programme started in 1987 with just over 3,000 students. Today millions of young people have studied abroad with it.

37078.q: What do you often learn along the way on an Erasmus exchange abroad?
37078.e: People who live abroad often learn a new language and make new friends.
37078.m: On an exchange you often learn a new language.

37079.q: What is today’s programme that Erasmus belongs to called?
37079.e: Since 2014, the big EU programme for education and exchange has been called Erasmus+.
37079.m: Today the programme is called Erasmus+.

37080.q: Besides students, who else can take part in Erasmus+?
37080.e: Erasmus+ is also for apprentices, school pupils and teachers.
37080.m: Apprentices can take part in Erasmus+ too.

37081.q: What is the Eurovision Song Contest?
37081.e: In the Eurovision Song Contest, artists from many countries sing to win.
37081.m: The Eurovision Song Contest is a singing competition.

37082.q: In which Swiss city did the first Eurovision Song Contest take place?
37082.e: The very first Eurovision Song Contest took place in 1956 in Lugano in Ticino.
37082.m: The first Eurovision Song Contest was in Lugano.

37083.q: Which country won the very first Eurovision Song Contest in 1956?
37083.e: Lys Assia won for Switzerland in 1956 with the song “Refrain”.
37083.m: Switzerland won the first Eurovision Song Contest.

37084.q: Who won the Eurovision Song Contest for Switzerland in 2024?
37084.e: Nemo from Biel won in 2024 with the song “The Code”.

37085.q: Which famous band from Sweden won in 1974 with “Waterloo”?
37085.e: ABBA won in 1974 with “Waterloo” and then became world-famous.

37086.q: Which singer won for Switzerland in 1988?
37086.e: In 1988, Céline Dion sang the song “Ne partez pas sans moi” for Switzerland and won.
37086.m: Céline Dion won for Switzerland in 1988.

37087.q: In which Swiss city is the European Broadcasting Union, which organises the contest, based?
37087.e: The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) has its seat in Geneva. It organises the Eurovision Song Contest.
37087.m: The Eurovision Song Contest is organised from Geneva.

37088.q: What is the Eurovision contest for children called?
37088.e: In the Junior Eurovision Song Contest, children and young teenagers sing for their country.
37088.m: For children there is the Junior Eurovision Song Contest.

37090.q: What colour is the dove of peace usually?
37090.e: The dove of peace is almost always drawn white. White often stands for calm and purity.
37090.m: The dove of peace is usually white.

37091.q: What does the dove of peace often carry in its beak?
37091.e: The dove of peace is often shown with an olive branch in its beak. The olive branch is a sign of peace too.
37091.m: The dove of peace often carries an olive branch.

37092.q: Which old story does the dove with the branch come from?
37092.e: The Bible tells the story of Noah and the great flood. In it, a dove returns to the ark with a branch in its beak.
37092.m: The dove with a branch comes from the story of Noah.

37093.q: Which famous painter drew a dove of peace in 1949?
37093.e: Pablo Picasso painted a dove for a big peace congress in 1949. Since then it has been known all over the world.
37093.m: Picasso made the dove of peace famous.

37094.q: Where do you often see the dove of peace?
37094.e: At peace celebrations and demonstrations, you often see the dove on posters and flags. It is easy to recognise.
37094.m: The dove of peace is on many peace posters.

37095.q: What did the dove with the branch show Noah?
37095.e: The dove brought back a fresh branch from an olive tree. From this Noah knew that the water was going down and the flood was over.
37095.m: The dove’s branch showed Noah the end of the flood.

37096.q: What does it mean when people release a white dove?
37096.e: At some peace celebrations, white doves are released. This shows the wish for peace.
37096.m: Flying white doves stand for the wish for peace.

37097.q: Who gets the Nobel Peace Prize?
37097.e: The Nobel Peace Prize honours people or groups who have done a lot for peace. It is one of the best-known prizes in the world.
37097.m: The Nobel Peace Prize honours work for peace.

37098.q: Who is the Nobel Prize named after?
37098.e: Alfred Nobel became rich from his inventions, for example dynamite. In his will he decided that prizes should be awarded with his money.
37098.m: The Nobel Prize is named after Alfred Nobel.

37099.q: Which country did Alfred Nobel come from?
37099.e: Alfred Nobel was born in Stockholm in 1833. Stockholm is the capital of Sweden.

37100.q: In which city is the Nobel Peace Prize presented?
37100.e: The Nobel Peace Prize is presented in Oslo in Norway. The other Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
37100.m: The Nobel Peace Prize is presented in Oslo.

37101.q: Which Swiss man received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901?
37101.e: Henry Dunant from Geneva received the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901. He shared it with the Frenchman Frédéric Passy.
37101.m: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

37102.q: How often is the Nobel Peace Prize normally awarded?
37102.e: The Nobel Peace Prize is normally awarded once a year. In some years, for example in times of war, nobody got it.
37102.m: The Nobel Peace Prize is usually awarded once a year.

37103.q: In which month are the Nobel Prizes presented every year?
37103.e: The Nobel Prizes are presented on 10 December. Alfred Nobel died on that day in 1896.
37103.m: The Nobel Prizes are presented in December.

37104.q: Which girl received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 at the age of 17?
37104.e: Malala Yousafzai works so that all girls are allowed to go to school. At 17 she was the youngest prize winner.
37104.m: Malala is the youngest Nobel Peace Prize winner.

37105.q: What do Nobel Prize winners receive, among other things?
37105.e: Anyone who wins the Nobel Prize receives a medal, a diploma and prize money. The medal is made of gold.
37105.m: A gold medal is part of the Nobel Prize.

37106.e: A diplomat works for their country in another country. They talk to the government there and keep up good relations.
37106.m: A diplomat represents their country abroad.

37107.q: What is especially important for a diplomat?
37107.e: Diplomats solve problems through talks. That is why they must be good at speaking and listening.

37108.q: What are many diplomats good at?
37108.e: Diplomats work in foreign countries. That is why they often speak several languages, including the language of the host country.

37109.q: What is solving disputes between countries through talks called?
37109.e: Diplomacy means that countries talk and negotiate with each other. That way they want to settle disputes without violence.

37110.q: Which department do Swiss diplomats work for?
37110.e: The FDFA is the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs. It looks after Switzerland’s relations with other countries.
37110.m: Swiss diplomats work for the FDFA.

37111.q: Where do diplomats usually work in a foreign country?
37111.e: The embassy is a country’s representation abroad. The diplomats work there.
37111.m: Diplomats often work in an embassy.

37112.q: What often happens to diplomats after a few years?
a: They always stay in the same place
37112.e: Many diplomats change where they work every few years. Then they move to another country with their family.

37113.q: What does “being diplomatic” mean in everyday life?
37113.e: If you are diplomatic, you say things in a friendly and careful way. That leads to fewer arguments.
37113.m: Being diplomatic means speaking politely and tactfully.

37114.q: What is the house an ambassador lives in called?
37114.e: The ambassador’s home is called the residence. Receptions for guests are often held there too.
37114.m: The ambassador lives in the residence.

37115.q: In which city are most foreign embassies in Switzerland?
37115.e: Embassies are usually in a country’s capital. In Switzerland, that is the federal city of Bern.
37115.m: The embassies in Switzerland are in Bern.

37116.q: Which flag hangs at the Swiss embassy in a foreign country?
a: The flag of the foreign country
37116.e: An embassy flies the flag of the country it represents. So the Swiss cross hangs at the Swiss embassy.
37116.m: The Swiss flag flies at the Swiss embassy.

37117.q: In which city is the Swiss embassy in France?
37117.e: The Swiss embassy in France is in Paris, the capital. There are also consulates in other big cities.
37117.m: The Swiss embassy in France is in Paris.

37118.q: What are the people who work for their country in an embassy called?
37118.e: Diplomats work in an embassy. They look after relations with the country they live in.

37119.q: Can the police simply walk into a foreign embassy?
37119.e: Embassies are specially protected. The police of the host country may only go in with the ambassador’s permission.

37120.q: What does an embassy between two countries show?
a: That they are the same size
37120.e: When two countries have embassies in each other’s country, they have diplomatic relations. That way they can talk to each other directly.
37120.m: Embassies show that two countries have diplomatic relations.

37121.q: Roughly how many representations such as embassies and consulates does Switzerland have abroad (as of 2026)?
37121.e: According to the FDFA, Switzerland has about 170 representations abroad. These include embassies, consulates and cooperation offices.

37122.q: Which language was for a long time the most important language of diplomacy?
37122.e: For a long time, diplomats all over Europe negotiated in French. Today English is often spoken, but French is still important.
37122.m: French was long the language of diplomacy.

37123.e: In Switzerland, the Federal Council appoints the ambassadors. They then work for the FDFA.
37123.m: The Federal Council appoints Switzerland’s ambassadors.

37124.q: What does a new ambassador bring to the head of state of the host country?
37124.e: The letter of credence is an official letter. It confirms that the person really is the new ambassador.
37124.m: A new ambassador brings a letter of credence.

37125.q: To whom do foreign ambassadors in Switzerland hand over their letter of credence?
a: The President of the National Council
The President of the Federal Supreme Court
37125.e: Switzerland does not have a single head of state such as a king. That is why the President of the Confederation receives the letter.
37125.m: In Switzerland, the President of the Confederation receives new ambassadors.

37127.q: Where does an ambassador usually live?
37127.e: The ambassador lives in the host country while doing the job. There they are there for their country.
37127.m: An ambassador lives in the host country.

37128.q: What does an ambassador often do at celebrations in the host country?
37128.e: Ambassadors go to many events and celebrations. There they show that their country is friendly.
37128.m: An ambassador represents their country at celebrations too.

37129.q: How do you address an ambassador politely?
37129.e: Ambassadors are addressed as “Excellency”. This is an old, polite form of address in diplomacy.
37129.m: You address an ambassador as Excellency.

37130.q: Where do you go abroad if you have lost your Swiss passport?
37130.e: The consulate or embassy helps Swiss people abroad. There you can get a replacement passport.
37130.m: The consulate helps with lost passports.

37131.q: Where do Swiss people living abroad register?
37131.e: People who live abroad register with the responsible Swiss representation, which is an embassy or a consulate. That way it can help quickly in an emergency.
37131.m: Swiss people abroad register with the Swiss representation.

37132.q: Where is there often a consulate?
a: In big cities outside the capital
37132.e: There are often consulates in big cities that are not the capital. That way they are closer to the people.
37132.m: There are often consulates in big cities.

37133.q: What is the person who runs a consulate called?
37133.e: The head of a consulate is called the consul. They work for their own country abroad.
37133.m: A consulate is run by a consul.

37134.q: What can you apply for at some consulates in order to travel to a country?
37134.e: For some countries you need a visa to enter. You can apply for it at a consulate of that country.
37134.m: You often apply for a visa at the consulate.

37135.e: A consulate general is a large consulate. It is run by a consul general.
37135.m: A consulate general is a large consulate.

37136.q: Apart from Bern and Geneva, in which Swiss city are there many foreign consulates?
37136.e: Zurich is the largest city in Switzerland. That is why many countries have a consulate there for their citizens.
37136.m: There are many foreign consulates in Zurich.

37137.q: What can a consulate do if a Swiss person falls ill abroad?
37137.e: The consulate can help to find a doctor or let the family know. It gives advice in emergencies.
37137.m: The consulate also helps in emergencies.

37138.e: In a peace treaty, countries agree that the war is over. It also says what applies afterwards.
37138.m: A peace treaty ends a war.

37139.q: How does a peace treaty become valid?
37139.e: The representatives of the countries sign the treaty. With this they promise to keep to it.

37140.q: What is the 1648 peace treaty in which the Swiss Confederation was recognised as independent called?
37140.e: The Peace of Westphalia was made in Münster and Osnabrück in 1648. It recognised that the Swiss Confederation no longer belonged to the German Empire.
37140.m: In the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, the Swiss Confederation was recognised as independent.

37141.q: Which war did the Peace of Westphalia end?
37141.e: The Peace of Westphalia was made in 1648. It ended the Thirty Years’ War in Europe.
37141.m: The Peace of Westphalia ended the Thirty Years’ War.

37142.q: What is the 1919 treaty after the First World War called?
37142.e: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in France in 1919. It settled the peace with Germany after the First World War.
37142.m: The Treaty of Versailles followed the First World War.

37143.e: In a ceasefire, the fighting stops. A peace treaty often follows.
37143.m: A ceasefire is a pause in the fighting.

37144.q: What is often written in a peace treaty?
37144.e: Peace treaties often settle where the borders between countries run. They also settle other disputed questions.

37145.q: What do countries have to do before a peace treaty?
37145.e: Before a peace treaty is signed, countries often negotiate for a long time. They look for a solution that everyone accepts.
37145.m: There are long negotiations before a peace treaty.

37148.q: Was neutral Switzerland occupied by another country in the Second World War?
37148.e: Switzerland stayed neutral in the Second World War and was not occupied. Its army guarded the borders.
37148.m: Switzerland was not occupied in the Second World War.

37149.q: Which of these organisations is Switzerland NOT a member of?
37149.e: NATO is a military alliance. As a neutral country, Switzerland is not a member. But it does take part in the UN, the OSCE and the Council of Europe.
37149.m: Neutral Switzerland is not in NATO.

37150.q: Does neutral Switzerland still have its own army?
37150.e: Switzerland has armed neutrality. Its army is meant to defend the country, but not to attack others.
37150.m: Switzerland has an army for defence.

37151.q: How long is Switzerland’s neutrality meant to last?
37151.e: Switzerland is permanently neutral. That means it wants to be neutral not just in one war, but always.

37152.q: Which of Switzerland’s neighbours is also neutral?
37152.e: Austria has been neutral since 1955. Little Liechtenstein is neutral too.
37152.m: Austria is also a neutral country.

37153.q: What may neutral Switzerland still do in a war?
37153.e: Switzerland helps people in need, for example with food and medicine. This is called humanitarian aid.
37153.m: Neutral Switzerland may help war victims.

37154.q: What does Switzerland often provide for peace talks?
37154.e: Switzerland often invites opposing sides to talks and provides a safe, quiet place. There they can negotiate undisturbed.
37154.m: Switzerland often offers a safe place for talks.

37155.q: Which important organisation has a large seat in Geneva?
37155.e: The United Nations has its second-largest site in Geneva after New York. Many conferences take place there.
37155.m: The UN has a large seat in Geneva.

37156.q: In which Swiss city were talks held in 2015 on Iran’s nuclear programme?
37156.e: In spring 2015, several countries negotiated with Iran in Lausanne. Switzerland helped as host.
37156.m: Lausanne was the place of important talks with Iran in 2015.

37157.q: Why do opposing sides like to meet in Switzerland?
a: Because it is always summer there
37157.e: Switzerland does not take sides. That is why both sides trust it as a host.
37157.m: Neutral Switzerland is a popular host.

37158.q: What do you call someone who mediates in a dispute?
37158.e: A mediator helps two sides to find a solution. Switzerland often takes on this role.
37158.m: A mediator helps to settle a dispute.

37159.q: Which important rules for protecting people in war are named after a Swiss city?
37159.e: The Geneva Conventions protect the wounded, prisoners and civilians in war. They were agreed in Geneva.
37159.m: The Geneva Conventions protect people in war.

37160.q: On which Swiss mountain did a big conference on peace in Ukraine take place in June 2024?
37160.e: In June 2024, Switzerland invited representatives from many countries to the Bürgenstock on Lake Lucerne. There they talked about peace in Ukraine.
37160.m: The 2024 Ukraine peace conference took place on the Bürgenstock.

a: A country that represents another country
37161.e: When two countries do not talk to each other, a third country can help. It then represents the interests of one country to the other.
37161.m: A protecting power represents another country.

37162.q: When does a country need a protecting power?
a: When it has no embassy in the other country
When it elects a new government
When it holds a big celebration
When it gets a new flag
37162.e: Sometimes two countries break off relations. Then a protecting power takes on important tasks of the missing embassy.
37162.m: A protecting power helps when there is no embassy.

37163.q: What does a protecting power pass on between two countries in dispute?
37163.e: A protecting power passes on messages and letters. That way two countries in dispute can still stay in contact.
37163.m: A protecting power passes on messages.

37164.q: Which country did Switzerland represent in Cuba from 1961 to 2015?
37164.e: The USA and Cuba did not have embassies in each other’s country for a long time. Switzerland represented the USA in Cuba until both opened embassies again in 2015.
37164.m: Switzerland represented the USA in Cuba for a long time.

37165.q: Which two countries has Switzerland represented to each other since 2009?
37165.e: After a war in 2008, Russia and Georgia broke off relations. Since 2009, Switzerland has represented each country to the other.
37165.m: Switzerland represents Russia and Georgia to each other.

37166.q: When did Switzerland have especially many protecting power mandates?
37166.e: In the Second World War, Switzerland represented many countries that were at war with each other. That way they could still exchange messages.
37166.m: In the Second World War, Switzerland was often a protecting power.

37167.q: Which country has represented the interests of the USA in Iran since 1980?
37167.e: The USA and Iran do not have embassies in each other’s country. Switzerland takes on this task as protecting power.
37167.m: Switzerland is the USA’s protecting power in Iran.

37168.q: Why is Switzerland often chosen as a protecting power?
a: Because it is the largest country in Europe
Because it has the strongest army
Because it is in the EU
37168.e: Switzerland does not take sides. That is why both countries that no longer talk to each other trust it.
37168.m: Because of its neutrality, Switzerland is a sought-after protecting power.

37169.q: How often a year is the International Day of Peace?
37169.e: The International Day of Peace takes place once a year, always on the same date in September.
37169.m: The Day of Peace is once a year.

37170.q: Who introduced the International Day of Peace?
37170.e: The United Nations introduced this day. They want all countries to live in peace.
37170.m: The UN introduced the Day of Peace.

37171.q: What should stop everywhere in the world on this day?
37171.e: The UN calls for weapons to be laid down everywhere on the Day of Peace. It is meant to be a day without violence.
37171.m: On the Day of Peace, the fighting should stop.

37172.q: What is rung at the UN headquarters on the Day of Peace?
37172.e: A special Peace Bell hangs at the UN headquarters in New York. It is rung at the start of the Day of Peace.
37172.m: On the Day of Peace, the Peace Bell rings.

37173.q: Which country does the UN Peace Bell come from?
37173.e: The Peace Bell was a gift from Japan in 1954. It was cast from coins donated by people from many countries.
37173.m: The UN Peace Bell comes from Japan.

37174.q: Which bird is a sign of peace?
37174.e: The white dove is a sign of peace all over the world. On the Day of Peace you often see it in pictures.
37174.m: The dove is a sign of peace.

37175.q: What can school classes do on the Day of Peace, for example?
37175.e: Many schools make doves or paint pictures on the Day of Peace. That way the children think about peace.
37175.m: On the Day of Peace you can make peace doves.

37176.q: What is the International Day of Peace meant to promote?
37176.e: The day is meant to show how important a life without violence is. People all over the world work for it.
37176.m: The Day of Peace promotes a life without violence.

37177.q: What do two politicians show when they shake hands after negotiations?
37177.e: A handshake after a negotiation shows that an agreement has been found. It is a sign of trust.

37178.q: Which hand do people usually shake hands with?
37178.e: Here, people usually shake with the right hand. It is an old habit.
37178.m: People usually shake with the right hand.

37179.q: According to an old explanation, what did a handshake show in the past?
a: That you were not holding a weapon
37179.e: An old explanation says: if you offer an open hand, you show that you are not carrying a weapon. That creates trust.
37179.m: The open hand shows that you are not carrying a weapon.

37180.q: When do people often shake hands?
37180.e: In Switzerland, people often greet each other with a handshake. Sometimes they shake hands when saying goodbye too.
37180.m: People often shake hands when they greet each other.

37181.q: During the coronavirus period, what did many people greet each other with instead of their hand?
37181.e: During the coronavirus period, people wanted to avoid infections. That is why many greeted each other with their elbow instead of a handshake.
37181.m: During the coronavirus period, people often greeted each other with their elbow.

37182.q: What do you often do with your opponent after a fair game?
37182.e: After a game, players often shake hands. This shows respect, just as in negotiations between countries.

37183.q: In which country do people traditionally greet each other with a bow instead of a handshake?
37183.e: In Japan, people bow when they greet each other. The deeper the bow, the more respect you show.
37183.m: In Japan, people bow when they greet each other.

37184.q: What should you do during a polite handshake?
a: Look the other person in the eye
37184.e: During a polite handshake, you look the other person in the eye. This shows openness and respect.
37184.m: When you shake hands, you look each other in the eye.

37185.q: Which organisation has received the Nobel Peace Prize three times?
37185.e: The International Committee of the Red Cross received the prize in 1917, 1944 and 1963. No other organisation has received it so often.
37185.m: The ICRC received the Nobel Peace Prize three times.

37186.q: Which two presidents met in Geneva in 2021?
37186.e: In June 2021, US President Joe Biden and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Geneva. Switzerland was the host.
37186.m: Biden and Putin met in Geneva in 2021.

37187.q: What is a big meeting where diplomats from many countries negotiate called?
37187.e: At a conference, representatives of many countries meet. They discuss shared problems and look for solutions.
37187.m: At a conference, diplomats negotiate with each other.

37188.q: What is the aim of development cooperation?
a: To reduce poverty in poorer countries
37188.e: In development cooperation, rich countries help poorer countries. The aim is for fewer people to live in poverty.
37188.m: Development cooperation is meant to reduce poverty.

a: You pay for every bit of help
37189.e: People are meant to get knowledge and tools. That way they can carry on later without outside help.
37189.m: Help for self-help makes people independent.

37190.q: Why is a well often built in dry villages?
37190.e: Without clean water, people get ill. A well brings drinking water straight into the village.
37190.m: A well brings clean water into the village.

37191.q: In some villages without a well, who often has to walk a long way to fetch water?
37191.e: In many poor areas, women and girls carry water over long distances. Then the children have less time for school.
37191.m: A well saves children the long walk to fetch water.

37192.q: Why is a school so important for a poor village?
37192.e: If you can read, write and do sums, it is easier to find work. That is why education is an important way out of poverty.
37192.m: Education is a way out of poverty.

37193.q: What do farmers often learn in development cooperation projects?
37193.e: With better seeds and growing tricks, more plants grow. That way families have enough to eat.

37194.q: What are countries that are much poorer than Switzerland often called?
37194.e: Developing countries often have little money, few hospitals and few schools. Development cooperation supports them.
37194.m: Poorer countries are often called developing countries.

a: You are not allowed to sell anything
37195.e: With fair trade, farmers in poor countries get a fair wage for cocoa, coffee or bananas. They can live better on it.
37195.m: Fair trade pays farmers a fair price.

37196.q: What does the abbreviation SDC stand for?
a: Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation
37196.e: The SDC is responsible for Switzerland’s development cooperation and humanitarian aid abroad.
37196.m: SDC stands for Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation.

37197.q: Who does the SDC belong to?
37197.e: The SDC is an authority of the Swiss Confederation. It is not a private organisation.
37197.m: The SDC is an office of the Confederation.

37198.q: Which department does the SDC belong to?
37198.e: The SDC belongs to the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs, FDFA for short. It looks after relations with other countries.
37198.m: The SDC belongs to the foreign affairs department, the FDFA.

37199.q: What does the SDC pay for its help with?
37199.e: The SDC is part of the Confederation. Its money comes from the federal budget, so from taxes.
37199.m: The SDC helps with money from taxes.

37200.q: Where does the SDC mainly help?
37200.e: The SDC supports projects in poorer countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe.
37200.m: The SDC mainly helps in poorer countries.

37201.q: Which big organisation does the SDC often work with?
37201.e: The SDC works with United Nations organisations, for example UNICEF.
37201.m: The SDC often works with the UN.

37202.q: In which city does the SDC have its headquarters?
37202.e: The SDC has its headquarters in Bern, where the federal administration works too. It also has offices in many countries.
37202.m: The SDC has its seat in Bern.

37203.q: Which federal group of experts helps quickly after disasters abroad?
37203.e: The Swiss Humanitarian Aid Corps belongs to the SDC. Its experts travel abroad after disasters.
37203.m: The Humanitarian Aid Corps belongs to the SDC.

a: Help building houses for rich people
37204.e: Humanitarian aid saves lives and eases suffering. It helps after wars, disasters or famines.
37204.m: Humanitarian aid helps people in need.

37205.e: Humanitarian aid does not ask about origin, religion or opinion. It helps everyone who is in need.
37205.m: Humanitarian aid is for everyone in need.

37206.q: What does it mean that humanitarian helpers are neutral?
a: They do not take the side of any party in a war
37206.e: Neutral helpers do not take sides in a conflict. That is why both sides trust them and let them reach the victims.
37206.m: Humanitarian helpers do not take the side of any party in a war.

37207.q: Who is honoured on World Humanitarian Day?
a: People who help others in need
37207.e: World Humanitarian Day is on 19 August every year. It honours people who help others in need.
37207.m: World Humanitarian Day honours the helpers.

37208.q: What do you call people who help at an aid organisation without pay?
37208.e: Volunteers give their time without being paid for it. Many aid organisations could not work without them.

37209.q: After a war, what do helpers remove from the ground so that people can walk there safely?
37209.e: Landmines often stay hidden in the ground for many years and are very dangerous. Experts look for them and make them harmless.
37209.m: After a war, landmines must be removed.

37210.q: What is handed out first in a famine?
37210.e: People who are starving need food and clean water first. Only then does other help come.
37210.m: In a famine, food and water are needed first.

37211.q: What special food do severely malnourished children often receive?
37211.e: Aid organisations hand out a paste made of peanuts, milk powder and vitamins. It is very nutritious and keeps for a long time.
37211.m: A nutritious peanut paste helps starving children.

37212.q: Why must Red Cross helpers not be attacked in a war?
37212.e: The Red Cross emblem is protected by the Geneva Conventions. Anyone who wears it and helps must not be attacked.
37212.m: The Red Cross emblem protects the helpers.

a: It collects donations for people in need
37213.e: Swiss Solidarity calls for donations after disasters. The money goes to aid organisations that help on the spot.
37213.m: Swiss Solidarity collects donations for people in need.

37214.q: How did Swiss Solidarity (Glückskette) begin in 1946?
37214.e: Swiss Solidarity started in 1946 as a programme on French-speaking Swiss radio. Today it is a foundation.
37214.m: Swiss Solidarity began as a radio programme.

37215.q: Who does Swiss Solidarity work closely with?
37215.e: SRG radio and television make the collection days known. That way, many people hear about the appeal for donations.
37215.m: Swiss Solidarity works with the SRG.

37216.q: When does Swiss Solidarity usually call for a big collection?
37216.e: After earthquakes, floods or wars, a lot of money is needed quickly. Then Swiss Solidarity organises a collection day.
37216.m: Swiss Solidarity collects donations after disasters.

37217.q: Does Swiss Solidarity also help in Switzerland?
a: Only when there is too little snow
37217.e: Swiss Solidarity has also collected for victims of storms in Switzerland, for example in October 2000 in Valais and Ticino.
37217.m: Swiss Solidarity also helps in Switzerland.

37218.q: For which disaster has Swiss Solidarity collected the most money so far?
a: A forest fire in the Jura
37218.e: After the tsunami in Asia in December 2004, around 227 million francs were collected. That is still Swiss Solidarity's record (as of 2026).
37218.m: Swiss Solidarity collected the most money for the 2004 tsunami.

37219.q: Who passes Swiss Solidarity's money on to the people on the spot?
37219.e: Swiss Solidarity does not help on the spot itself. It gives the money to partner aid organisations, which carry out the projects.
37219.m: Swiss Solidarity passes the money on to aid organisations.

37220.q: What do you give Swiss Solidarity if you want to help people in need?
37220.e: A donation is money you give away to help. Swiss Solidarity collects donations and passes them on to aid organisations.
37220.m: A donation to Swiss Solidarity helps people in need.

37221.e: Earthquakes, floods and hurricanes are natural disasters. They can put many people in great need.
37221.m: Natural disasters are big catastrophes caused by nature.

37222.q: What do people need after an earthquake if their house has been destroyed?
37222.e: Anyone without a house needs a safe place to sleep. That is why aid organisations bring tents and blankets.
37222.m: After an earthquake, shelter comes first.

37223.e: A tsunami is often caused by an earthquake under the sea. The huge wave can flood entire coasts.
37223.m: A tsunami is a huge wave.

37224.q: What is the name of the Swiss group that searches for people buried after earthquakes abroad?
37224.e: Swiss Rescue is made up of experts, doctors and dogs. It can fly abroad within hours.
37224.m: Swiss Rescue searches for buried people abroad.

37225.q: Why does help after an earthquake have to be especially fast?
a: Buried people only survive a short time
37225.e: People trapped under rubble usually survive only a few days. That is why every hour counts.
37225.m: After an earthquake, every hour counts.

37226.q: What can become dangerous after a flood?
37226.e: After a flood, the water is often dirty. Anyone who drinks it can become ill.
37226.m: After floods, clean water is important.

37227.q: Which device helps aid workers make dirty water drinkable?
37227.e: A water filter holds back dirt and many germs. That turns dirty water into drinking water. A kitchen sieve only holds back large bits.
37227.m: A water filter makes water clean.

37228.q: Which vehicle gets relief supplies to distant countries fastest?
37228.e: Aeroplanes are the fastest over long distances. That is why relief supplies are often flown straight into the disaster area.
37228.m: Aeroplanes bring help quickly to distant countries.

37229.q: What does a rescue dog use to find buried people?
37229.e: Dogs can smell much better than people. They can pick up the scent of people under rubble or snow.
37229.m: Rescue dogs find people with their nose.

37230.q: What is a dog that searches for people under the snow called?
37230.e: Avalanche dogs search for buried people after an avalanche. They are often faster than people with equipment.
37230.m: An avalanche dog searches for people in the snow.

37231.q: How does a rescue dog usually show that it has found a person?
37231.e: The dog learns to bark or scratch at the spot where it found someone. Then the helpers know where to dig.
37231.m: A rescue dog barks when it finds someone.

37232.q: What do rescue dogs help with, for example after an earthquake?
37232.e: Rescue dogs can smell people under rubble. In Switzerland, the association REDOG trains such dogs.
37232.m: Rescue dogs find buried people with their nose.

37233.q: Which dog breed used to rescue people on the Great St Bernard Pass?
37233.e: The monks on the Great St Bernard kept large dogs. These helped find travellers who had lost their way in the snow.
37233.m: St Bernards used to rescue people on the pass.

37234.q: What was the name of the most famous rescue dog from the Great St Bernard?
37234.e: Barry is said to have saved about 40 people around 1800. He is on display in the Natural History Museum in Bern.
37234.m: Barry is the most famous St Bernard.

37235.q: What does a mantrailing dog do?
37235.e: A mantrailer sniffs a piece of clothing belonging to the missing person. Then it follows exactly that person's scent trail.
37235.m: A mantrailer follows a person's trail.

37236.q: Who works together with the rescue dog?
37236.e: Dog and handler form a team. They practise together for years.
37236.m: A rescue dog and its handler are a team.

37237.q: What is often in an aid package after a disaster?
37237.e: Aid packages contain what you need to survive. This includes blankets, food and things for personal hygiene.
37237.m: Aid packages contain the bare essentials for survival.

37238.q: What does a rescue dog often wear at work so that it can be seen easily?
37238.e: The coloured vest shows that the dog is on duty. That way the helpers can see it even among the rubble.
37238.m: Rescue dogs wear a vest when on duty.

37239.q: What do refugees often need first when they arrive in a safe country?
a: A place to sleep and food
37239.e: After a long escape, many people are tired and hungry. So they are first given a place to sleep and something to eat.
37239.m: Refugees first need a place to sleep and food.

37240.q: What do many people flee from?
37240.e: War is one of the most common reasons for fleeing. People want to bring themselves and their family to safety.

37241.q: What do you call a country that takes in and protects refugees?
37241.e: The host country gives refugees protection. The country they fled from is called the country of origin.

37242.q: In which city was the most important treaty for protecting refugees agreed in 1951?
37242.e: The 1951 Geneva Refugee Convention sets out who is a refugee. It also lays down their rights.
37242.m: The Geneva Refugee Convention protects refugees.

37243.q: What are countries not allowed to do under the Refugee Convention?
37243.e: Nobody may be sent back to a country where they are persecuted. This protection is at the heart of the Convention.
37243.m: Refugees must not be sent back into danger.

37244.q: What do people often take with them when they flee?
37244.e: Anyone who has to flee often has little time. That is why many take only the most important things.
37244.m: When fleeing, you take only a little with you.

37245.q: What do you call people who have to flee within their own country?
37245.e: Internally displaced people leave their homes but stay in their own country. There are a great many of them worldwide.
37245.m: Internally displaced people flee within their own country.

37246.q: What is especially important for refugee children in a new country?
a: Being able to go to school
37246.e: School helps children learn the language and make friends. That way they can settle into their new country.
37246.m: School helps refugee children settle in.

37247.e: Anyone who is persecuted in their home country can ask another country for protection. This protection is called asylum.
37247.m: Asylum means protection in another country.

37248.q: Why do some people ask for asylum in another country?
a: Because they are in danger in their home country
Because they have won a trip
Because they want to learn a language
37248.e: Some people are persecuted in their home country, or there is a war there. They flee and ask another country for protection.
37248.m: Anyone in danger in their home country can ask for asylum.

37249.q: Which federal office decides on asylum applications in Switzerland?
37249.e: The State Secretariat for Migration, SEM for short, examines every asylum application. It decides whether someone receives protection.
37249.m: The SEM decides on asylum applications.

37250.q: Where do asylum seekers in Switzerland live first?
a: In a hotel by the lake
37250.e: Newly arrived asylum seekers go to a federal asylum centre. Their application is examined there.
37250.m: Asylum seekers first live in a federal asylum centre.

37251.q: Which language do asylum seekers in German-speaking Switzerland often learn in courses?
37251.e: Anyone living in German-speaking Switzerland needs German for school, work and everyday life. That is why many asylum seekers attend German courses.
37251.m: Asylum seekers in German-speaking Switzerland learn German.

37252.q: What do you call someone who has been granted asylum in Switzerland?
37252.e: Anyone who is persecuted and receives asylum counts as a recognised refugee. They may stay in Switzerland.
37252.m: Anyone granted asylum is a recognised refugee.

37253.q: What do asylum seekers have to explain at their interview?
37253.e: At the interview, people talk about their escape. From this, it is checked whether they need protection.
37253.m: Asylum seekers explain why they fled.

37254.q: Who receives provisional admission in Switzerland?
a: People who are just on holiday
People who want to study here
37254.e: Some people are not granted asylum but cannot go back because it is too dangerous. They are provisionally admitted.
37254.m: Anyone who cannot safely return home is provisionally admitted.

37255.q: Which foods are often handed out in refugee camps?
37255.e: Aid organisations hand out staple foods that keep for a long time. With these, families can cook for themselves.
37255.m: In camps, families receive long-lasting staple foods.

37256.q: What do people live in at many refugee camps?
37256.e: Tents can be put up quickly. That is why many people in camps live in tents or simple huts.
37256.m: In refugee camps, people often live in tents.

37257.q: How does drinking water get to a camp if there is no well there?
37257.e: If there is no water source, lorries bring large tanks full of water. The water is then shared out among the families.
37257.m: Tanker lorries bring water to the camp.

37258.q: What is there often for children in large refugee camps too?
37258.e: Aid organisations set up schools in camps. That way children can keep learning despite having fled.
37258.m: Children can go to school even in a refugee camp.

37259.q: What problem is there often in refugee camps?
37259.e: In some camps, a great many people live in a small space. That makes life difficult.
37259.m: Refugee camps are often very crowded.

37260.q: Who helps in refugee camps with food, water and tents?
37260.e: Aid organisations bring food, water, tents and medicines to the camps. They are often paid for with donations.

37261.q: Why are toilets and washing areas so important in a camp?
a: They are nice to look at
37261.e: Where many people live close together, diseases spread quickly. Cleanliness protects against this.
37261.m: Cleanliness protects against diseases in the camp.

37262.q: How long do some people live in refugee camps?
37262.e: Camps are really meant to be temporary. Because wars often last a long time, some people stay for many years.
37262.m: Some people live in a camp for years.

37263.q: On which day is World Refugee Day?
37263.e: World Refugee Day is on 20 June every year. Before that, many countries already held an African Refugee Day on this date.
37263.m: World Refugee Day is on 20 June.

a: The Federal Council on its own
37264.e: The General Assembly of the United Nations decided on the day. It applies all over the world.
37264.m: The UN introduced World Refugee Day.

37265.q: What does World Refugee Day remind us of?
a: People who have had to flee
37265.e: The day draws attention to the fate of refugees. It reminds us of their courage and their hardship.
37265.m: World Refugee Day remembers people who have had to flee.

37266.q: What do many people want to show on World Refugee Day?
37266.e: Solidarity means sticking together and helping. On this day, many people show that they support refugees.
37266.m: On World Refugee Day, people show solidarity with refugees.

37267.q: Since which year has there been a World Refugee Day?
37267.e: In 2001, the Geneva Refugee Convention turned 50. To mark this, the first World Refugee Day was held.
37267.m: World Refugee Day has existed since 2001.

37268.q: Which organisation in Switzerland invites people every year to events around Refugee Day?
37268.e: The Swiss Refugee Council stands up for refugees. Around Refugee Day in June, it organises festivals and get-togethers with other groups.
37268.m: The Swiss Refugee Council organises events for Refugee Day.

37269.q: What can you do on World Refugee Day, for example?
37269.e: In many places there are festivals, exhibitions and get-togethers. That way people get to know each other better.
37269.m: On World Refugee Day you can get to know refugees.

37270.q: Which organisation publishes figures on displacement every year around World Refugee Day?
37270.e: Shortly before World Refugee Day, the UNHCR publishes a report. It says how many people worldwide have been forced to flee.
37270.m: The UNHCR counts the people who have fled every year.

37271.q: What is a sponsorship with an aid organisation?
a: You regularly support a child or project
37271.e: With a sponsorship, you donate money regularly. This helps a child, a village or a project.
37271.m: With a sponsorship, you help regularly.

37272.q: How often do you usually pay for a sponsorship?
37272.e: Sponsorships are meant to last. Usually you pay a fixed amount every month.
37272.m: Sponsorships are usually paid every month.

37273.q: Why is regular help good for projects?
a: You never have to say thank you
37273.e: When money comes in every month, the aid organisation knows what it can count on. That way projects can run for years.

37274.q: What do sponsors often receive from the aid organisation?
37274.e: Many aid organisations send letters, reports or photos. That way sponsors can see what happens with their money.
37274.m: Sponsors often receive reports about their project.

37275.q: Who often receives the help from a child sponsorship today?
37275.e: Many aid organisations help not just one child but the child's whole village. That way all the children there benefit.
37275.m: A child sponsorship often helps the whole village.

37276.q: Can you also sponsor an animal?
a: Yes, for example at the zoo
Only dogs in your own home
37276.e: Many zoos and animal welfare organisations offer animal sponsorships. The money helps pay for food and care.
37276.m: There are sponsorships for animals too.

37277.q: What should you check before taking on a sponsorship?
a: Whether the aid organisation is honest and helps well
37277.e: You should be sure that the money is used well. That is why you find out about the aid organisation carefully beforehand.
37277.m: Before donating, you check the aid organisation.

37278.q: What do you call someone who takes on a sponsorship?
37278.e: Someone who takes on a sponsorship is called a sponsor. He or she supports the child or project.
37278.m: Someone who takes on a sponsorship is a sponsor.

37279.e: Aid organisations collect money and use it to help people in need. Many work in Switzerland and abroad.
37279.m: An aid organisation helps people in need.

37280.q: Which Swiss foundation runs the helpline number 147 for children and young people?
37280.e: Pro Juventute stands up for children and young people in Switzerland. On the number 147 they can get advice and help around the clock.
37280.m: Pro Juventute's number 147 helps children and young people.

37281.q: What is the name of the aid organisation founded in Lausanne in 1960 that helps children?
37281.e: Terre des hommes was founded in 1960 by Edmond Kaiser in Lausanne. It stands up for children in need.
37281.m: Terre des hommes was founded in Lausanne.

37282.q: Who does the Swiss Mountain Aid (Schweizer Berghilfe) mainly help?
37282.e: The Swiss Mountain Aid helps farming families and businesses in the mountains. That way the people there can carry on living and working.
37282.m: The Swiss Mountain Aid helps people in the mountains.

37283.q: In which village in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden is the Pestalozzi Children's Village?
37283.e: The Pestalozzi Children's Village was founded in Trogen in 1946. At first, war orphans from Europe lived there.
37283.m: The Pestalozzi Children's Village is in Trogen.

37284.q: What does the ZEWO seal of approval show about a Swiss aid organisation?
a: It is the biggest aid organisation
It belongs to the federal government
37284.e: The ZEWO foundation checks aid organisations. Those with the seal use donations honestly and carefully.
37284.m: The ZEWO seal shows a trustworthy aid organisation.

37285.q: Which Swiss aid organisation belongs to the Catholic Church?
37285.e: Caritas is an aid organisation of the Catholic Church. It helps poor people in Switzerland and abroad.
37285.m: Caritas is a Catholic aid organisation.

37286.q: Which aid organisation belongs to the Reformed churches of Switzerland?
37286.e: HEKS is today called the Aid Organisation of the Protestant Reformed Church of Switzerland. It helps at home and abroad.
37286.m: HEKS is the aid organisation of the Reformed Church.

37287.q: How can children raise money for an aid organisation?
a: With a trip to the cinema
With a trip to the zoo
37287.e: In a sponsored run, adults pay for every lap you run. The money goes to an aid project.
37287.m: Children can raise money with a sponsored run.

37288.q: After which major event was the Declaration of Human Rights written?
a: After the invention of the internet
37288.e: After the terrible suffering of the Second World War, countries wanted to protect the rights of all people.
37288.m: Human rights are a response to the suffering of the Second World War.

37289.q: Who adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
37289.e: The General Assembly of the United Nations (UN) adopted the Declaration. Almost all the countries in the world work together in the UN.
37289.m: The UN wrote down human rights for all countries.

37290.q: Which right does Article 19 of the Declaration of Human Rights protect?
37290.e: Article 19 says that every person may freely express and spread their opinion.
37290.m: Every person may freely express their opinion.

37291.q: Who do human rights apply to?
37291.e: Human rights apply to every person in the world, no matter where they come from.
37291.m: Human rights belong to all people.

37292.q: How does Article 1 of the Declaration of Human Rights begin?
a: All people are born free and equal
All children must go to school
All countries are the same size
37292.e: Article 1 says: “All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.”
37292.m: Article 1 says that all people are born free and equal.

37293.q: Which of these rights is in the Declaration of Human Rights?
a: Right to a house by the lake
37293.e: Article 26 says that every person has the right to education.
37293.m: Every person has a right to education.

37294.q: Into how many languages has the Declaration of Human Rights been translated?
37294.e: The Declaration exists in over 500 languages. It is one of the most translated texts in the world.
37294.m: You can read human rights in over 500 languages.

37295.q: What does the Declaration of Human Rights forbid?
37295.e: Article 5 says that nobody may be tortured or punished cruelly.
37295.m: Torture is forbidden under human rights.

37296.q: What does Article 4 of the Declaration of Human Rights forbid?
37296.e: Article 4 says that nobody may be held as a slave.
37296.m: No person may belong to another.

37297.q: In which Swiss city does the UN Human Rights Council meet?
37297.e: The UN Human Rights Council is based at the Palais des Nations in Geneva.
37297.m: The UN Human Rights Council meets in Geneva.

37298.q: Who led the group that drew up the Declaration of Human Rights?
37298.e: Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the UN Commission on Human Rights, which wrote the text.
37298.m: Eleanor Roosevelt helped to write down human rights.

37299.q: Which country did Eleanor Roosevelt come from?
37299.e: Eleanor Roosevelt was American. She lived from 1884 to 1962.

37300.q: What was the name of Eleanor Roosevelt's husband, who was President of the USA?
37300.e: Franklin D. Roosevelt was President of the USA from 1933 to 1945.
37300.m: Eleanor was married to President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

37302.q: What nickname was Eleanor Roosevelt given?
37302.e: Because of her work for human rights, President Harry Truman called her the “First Lady of the World”.
37302.m: Eleanor Roosevelt was called the “First Lady of the World”.

37303.q: In which city was Eleanor Roosevelt born?
37303.e: Eleanor Roosevelt was born in New York City in 1884.
37303.m: Eleanor Roosevelt was born in New York.

37304.q: What did Eleanor Roosevelt particularly stand up for?
37304.e: All her life she fought for the rights of women, the poor and the disadvantaged.
37304.m: Eleanor Roosevelt fought for the rights of all people.

37305.q: At which organisation did Eleanor Roosevelt represent the USA?
37305.e: From 1945 to 1952 she was a US delegate to the United Nations.
37305.m: Eleanor Roosevelt represented the USA at the UN.

37306.q: On which day is Human Rights Day?
37306.e: Every year on 10 December, human rights are remembered.
37306.m: Human Rights Day is on 10 December.

37307.q: Human Rights Day is on 10 December. Why on this particular day?
a: The Declaration of Human Rights was adopted on this day
The UN was founded on this day
It is the shortest day of the year
37307.e: On 10 December 1948, the UN adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
37307.m: The day celebrates the birthday of human rights.

37308.q: Which birthday did the Declaration of Human Rights celebrate on Human Rights Day 2023?
37308.e: Calculation: 2023 minus 1948 = 75. So the Declaration turned 75.
37308.m: In 2023, the Declaration of Human Rights turned 75.

37309.q: Since which year has Human Rights Day existed?
37309.e: The UN introduced the day in 1950.
37309.m: Human Rights Day has existed since 1950.

37310.q: How often is Human Rights Day celebrated?
37310.e: Human Rights Day takes place once every year.
37310.m: Human Rights Day comes once a year.

a: A right that every person has
37311.e: Every person is entitled to human rights, simply because they are human.
37311.m: Every person has human rights from birth.

37312.q: How many days after Human Rights Day is Christmas on 25 December?
37312.e: Calculation: 25 minus 10 = 15. Christmas is 15 days later.
37312.m: Christmas is 15 days after Human Rights Day.

37313.q: What should people think about on Human Rights Day?
37313.e: The day reminds us that human rights must be protected, because they are not respected everywhere.
37313.m: On Human Rights Day, people think about the rights of all people.

37314.q: In which year did the UN recommend introducing a World Children's Day?
37314.e: In 1954, the UN General Assembly recommended that all countries celebrate a day for children.
37314.m: In 1954 the UN called for a World Children's Day.

37315.q: On which day is World Children's Day in Germany?
37315.e: In Germany, World Children's Day is celebrated on 20 September.
37315.m: In Germany, World Children's Day is on 20 September.

37316.q: On which day do many countries, for example China, celebrate Children's Day?
37316.e: In over 40 countries, International Children's Day is on 1 June.
37316.m: In many countries, Children's Day is on 1 June.

37317.q: Who is the focus on World Children's Day?
37317.e: World Children's Day is about the needs of children.
37317.m: Children are the focus on World Children's Day.

37318.q: On which day does Japan celebrate its Children's Day?
37318.e: In Japan, 5 May is a holiday for children called “Kodomo no Hi”.
37318.m: Japan celebrates Children's Day on 5 May.

37319.q: Do all countries celebrate World Children's Day on the same day?
37319.e: Each country chooses its own date. That is why there are several children's days in a year.
37319.m: World Children's Day has different dates in different countries.

37320.q: What does World Children's Day aim to achieve?
37320.e: The day is meant to show what children need in order to be well.
37320.m: World Children's Day draws attention to children's needs.

37321.q: On which day is International Women's Day?
37321.e: Women's Day is celebrated every year on 8 March.

37322.q: In which year was the first Women's Day held?
37322.e: The first Women's Day took place on 19 March 1911.
37322.m: The first Women's Day was in 1911.

37323.q: Which country took part in the first Women's Day in 1911?
37323.e: In 1911, women in Germany, Austria-Hungary, Denmark and Switzerland celebrated the first Women's Day.
37323.m: Switzerland took part in the first Women's Day.

37324.q: Which woman proposed a Women's Day in 1910?
37324.e: The German politician Clara Zetkin proposed in 1910 that a Women's Day be celebrated every year.
37324.m: Clara Zetkin had the idea for Women's Day.

37325.q: What did women mainly fight for on the first Women's Day?
37325.e: Back then, in many countries women were not allowed to vote in elections or referendums. They wanted to change that.
37325.m: On the first Women's Day, women demanded the right to vote.

37326.q: Since which year have women in Switzerland been allowed to vote at national level?
37326.e: On 7 February 1971, Swiss men voted yes to women's suffrage at federal level.
37326.m: Swiss women have been able to vote nationally since 1971.

37327.q: Who is honoured on International Women's Day?
37327.e: On International Women's Day, people think about all women and their rights. Mother's Day is a different day in May.

37328.q: In which German city has Women's Day been a public holiday since 2019?
37328.e: The federal state of Berlin made 8 March a public holiday in 2019.
37328.m: In Berlin, Women's Day is a day off.

37329.q: On which day is Earth Day?
37329.e: Earth Day takes place every year on 22 April.

37330.q: In which year was the first Earth Day held?
37330.e: The first Earth Day took place in the USA more than 50 years ago.

37331.q: In which country did the first Earth Day take place?
37331.e: Earth Day began in the United States. Senator Gaylord Nelson came up with the idea.
37331.m: Earth Day comes from the USA.

37332.q: How many people took part in the first Earth Day?
37332.e: On the first Earth Day, around 20 million people in the USA took part in activities.
37332.m: Millions of people took part even in the first Earth Day.

37333.e: Earth Day is meant to show how important it is to protect the environment.
37333.m: On Earth Day, people think about protecting our planet.

37335.q: In how many countries is Earth Day celebrated today (as of 2025)?
37335.e: Today, people in over 190 countries take part in Earth Day, around one billion people altogether.
37335.m: Earth Day is celebrated almost all over the world.

37336.q: What can a school class do on Earth Day?
37336.e: On Earth Day, many schools collect litter or plant trees.
37336.m: On Earth Day, everyone can do something for nature.

37337.q: What changes every year on World Environment Day?
a: The host country and the theme
The colour of the UN flag
37337.e: World Environment Day is always on 5 June. But each year a different country takes on the role of host, and there is a new theme.
37337.m: Each year World Environment Day has a different host country.

37338.q: Since which year has World Environment Day been celebrated?
37338.e: World Environment Day was decided on in 1972 and celebrated for the first time in 1974.
37338.m: World Environment Day has been celebrated since 1974.

37339.q: Which organisation introduced World Environment Day?
37339.e: The United Nations declared the day so that all countries would think about the environment.
37339.m: World Environment Day is a UN day.

37340.q: In which city did the environmental conference that World Environment Day commemorates begin on 5 June 1972?
37340.e: On 5 June 1972, the first major UN environmental conference began in Stockholm.
37340.m: World Environment Day commemorates a conference in Stockholm.

37341.q: What does World Environment Day have every year?
37341.e: Every year there is a different theme and usually a host country.
37341.m: World Environment Day has a new theme every year.

37342.q: Which kind of waste was the theme of World Environment Day 2018 aimed at?
37342.m: Plastic waste is a big problem for the environment.

37344.q: What is the name of the UN environment programme that organises World Environment Day?
37344.e: UNEP stands for “United Nations Environment Programme”.
37344.m: The UN's environment programme is called UNEP.

37345.q: On which day is World Book Day?
37345.e: World Book Day is celebrated every year on 23 April.
37345.m: World Book Day is on 23 April.

37346.q: Which organisation introduced World Book Day?
37346.e: UNESCO is the UN organisation for education, science and culture.
37346.m: UNESCO celebrates World Book Day every year.

37347.q: Since which year has World Book Day existed?
37347.e: UNESCO declared the day for the first time in 1995.
37347.m: World Book Day has existed since 1995.

37348.q: Which famous English playwright and poet died in April 1616?
37348.e: William Shakespeare died in 1616. World Book Day also commemorates him.
37348.m: World Book Day commemorates William Shakespeare.

37349.q: Which book did the Spaniard Miguel de Cervantes, who is remembered on World Book Day, write?
37349.e: Cervantes wrote the novel “Don Quixote”. He died in April 1616.

37350.q: What do people in Catalonia give each other along with books on 23 April?
37350.e: On St George's Day (Sant Jordi), people in Catalonia give each other books and roses. That is where the idea for the world day came from.
37350.m: In Catalonia, people give each other books and roses on 23 April.

37351.q: What is the full name of World Book Day?
37351.e: The day is also meant to remind us that the works of authors are protected.
37351.m: World Book Day is also about copyright.

37352.q: What is World Book Day mainly meant to encourage?
37352.e: The day aims to encourage children and adults to read.
37352.m: World Book Day makes you want to read.

37353.q: On which day is World Water Day?
37353.e: World Water Day takes place every year on 22 March.
37353.m: World Water Day is on 22 March.

37354.q: Since which year has World Water Day existed?
37354.e: World Water Day was celebrated for the first time in 1993.
37354.m: World Water Day has existed since 1993.

37355.q: In which city was World Water Day proposed at a UN conference in 1992?
37355.e: World Water Day was proposed at the big environmental conference in Rio de Janeiro in 1992. The UN General Assembly adopted it that same year.
37355.m: World Water Day was proposed in Rio de Janeiro.

37356.q: How much of the Earth's surface is covered with water?
37356.e: Around 71 per cent of the Earth's surface is covered with water, mostly by seas and oceans.
37356.m: Most of the Earth is covered with water.

37357.q: How much of the water on Earth is salt water?
37357.e: Almost all water is salty seawater. Only a little is fresh water for drinking.
37357.m: Most of the water on Earth is salty.

37358.q: How many people have no safe drinking water (as of 2024)?
37358.e: According to the WHO and UNICEF, about 2.1 billion people had no safe access to drinking water in 2024. That is about one person in four.
37358.m: Many people in the world have no clean drinking water.

37359.q: What is Switzerland called because of its many lakes, rivers and glaciers?
37359.e: Large rivers such as the Rhine and the Rhône rise in the Swiss Alps. That is why Switzerland is called the “water tower of Europe”.
37359.m: Switzerland is the water tower of Europe.

37360.q: Roughly how long can a person survive without water?
37360.e: Without drinking, a person can usually only survive for about three days.
37360.m: People need water every day to live.

37361.q: Switzerland's most important law contains a sentence about all people. Which one?
a: All people are equal before the law
All people must ride a bike
All people must live in Bern
37361.e: The Federal Constitution, Switzerland's most important law, says: “All people are equal before the law.”
37361.m: In Switzerland, all people are equal before the law.

37362.q: Since which year has equality between men and women been in the Federal Constitution?
37362.e: In 1981, the people approved the article on equal rights for men and women.
37362.m: Equality has been in the Federal Constitution since 1981.

37363.q: Who gave the famous “I have a dream” speech in 1963?
37363.e: Martin Luther King dreamed of a country where black and white people would be treated equally.
37363.m: Martin Luther King fought for equal rights for all.

37364.q: Where did Rosa Parks refuse to give up her seat for a white person in 1955?
37364.e: Rosa Parks stayed in her seat on a bus in Montgomery (USA). This became an important sign against racial segregation.
37364.m: Rosa Parks bravely stayed in her seat on the bus.

37365.q: In which country did Nelson Mandela fight for equal rights?
37365.e: Nelson Mandela fought against the separation of black and white people in South Africa. Later he became president there.
37365.m: Nelson Mandela fought for equality in South Africa.

37366.e: Anyone who treats someone worse because of their origin, skin colour or sex is discriminating against them.

37367.q: On which day in 1991 did women all over Switzerland go on strike for equality?
37367.e: On 14 June 1991, hundreds of thousands of women took part in the women's strike.
37367.m: On 14 June 1991, women in Switzerland went on strike.

37368.q: How does Amnesty International often help people who are wrongly in prison?
a: It collects signatures and writes letters
37368.e: Amnesty International makes injustice public and collects signatures and letters to governments. This puts pressure on them to release prisoners.
37368.m: Amnesty helps prisoners with letters and signatures.

37370.q: What does Amnesty International mainly stand up for?
37370.e: Amnesty International helps people who are persecuted or unjustly locked up. The organisation stands up for human rights worldwide.
37370.m: Amnesty International fights for human rights.

37371.q: What does the Amnesty International symbol show?
37371.e: The candle in barbed wire stands for hope for people who are imprisoned.
37371.m: Amnesty's symbol is a candle in barbed wire.

37372.q: Which prize did Amnesty International receive in 1977?
37372.e: In 1977, Amnesty International was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for its work for prisoners and against torture.
37372.m: Amnesty International received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

37374.q: What do people write during Amnesty International's “Write for Rights” letter marathon?
37374.e: During the letter marathon, many people write letters to governments so that persecuted people are set free.
37374.m: You can help people in need with letters.

37375.q: Which punishment does Amnesty International campaign against?
37375.e: Amnesty International opposes the death penalty in all cases.
37375.m: Amnesty International wants to abolish the death penalty.

37376.e: In an amnesty, prisoners are let off their punishment and set free.
37376.m: Amnesty means that a punishment is cancelled.

37377.q: In which year did the UN adopt the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
37377.e: The UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989.

37378.q: Who counts as a child under the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
37378.e: Article 1 of the Convention says that every person under 18 counts as a child. Children's rights apply to all these children.
37378.m: Under the Convention, every person under 18 is a child.

37379.q: Which right do children have under the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
37379.e: Article 31 says that every child has a right to rest, leisure and play.
37379.m: Children have a right to play and leisure.

37380.q: What does every child receive after birth under the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
37380.e: Article 7 says that every child receives a name and a nationality from birth.
37380.m: Every child has a right to a name.

37381.q: Which country is the only UN member not to have ratified the Convention on the Rights of the Child (as of 2025)?
37381.e: The USA signed the Convention but never put it into force. All the other UN countries have ratified it.
37381.m: Almost every country in the world has recognised children's rights.

37382.q: What are children allowed to do under Article 12 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
37382.e: Children may give their opinion on matters that affect them.
37382.m: Children have the right to say what they think.

37383.q: What colour is one of the five Olympic rings?
37383.e: The Olympic rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red. The background of the Olympic flag is white.
37383.m: One of the Olympic rings is green.

37384.q: Which organisation is responsible for the Olympic Games?
37384.e: The International Olympic Committee, IOC for short, awards and oversees the Olympic Games. It also decides which city may host them.
37384.m: The IOC looks after the Olympic Games.

37385.q: How many rings does the symbol of the Olympic Games have?
37385.e: The Olympic rings are five interlocking rings. They stand for the five inhabited continents joining together.
37385.m: The Olympic symbol has five rings.

37386.q: Who founded the International Olympic Committee?
37386.e: The Frenchman Pierre de Coubertin founded the IOC in 1894. He wanted to revive the Olympic Games of ancient Greece.
37386.m: Pierre de Coubertin founded the IOC.

37387.q: What nickname does Lausanne have because of the IOC?
37387.e: Because the IOC and many sports federations are based in Lausanne, the city is called the “Olympic Capital”. It has officially held this title since 1994.
37387.m: Lausanne is also called the Olympic Capital.

37388.q: Since 2025, a woman has led the IOC for the first time. What is her name?
37388.e: Kirsty Coventry from Zimbabwe was elected IOC President in 2025 (as of 2025). She used to be a successful swimmer.
37388.m: Kirsty Coventry is the first female President of the IOC.

37389.q: How often do the Summer Olympic Games take place?
37389.e: The Summer Olympics take place every four years. The Winter Games also take place every four years, but two years apart from the Summer Games.
37389.m: The Summer Olympics take place every four years.

37390.q: In 1915 the IOC moved to Lausanne. In which city was it before?
37390.e: The IOC was founded in Paris and was first based there. During the First World War it moved to neutral Switzerland.
37390.m: The IOC moved from Paris to Lausanne in 1915.

37391.q: Which games took place in Lausanne in 2020?
37391.e: In January 2020, the Winter Youth Olympic Games took place in and around Lausanne. Young athletes competed against each other there.
37391.m: Lausanne hosted the Winter Youth Olympic Games in 2020.

37392.q: On which lake is the Olympic Museum?
37392.e: The Olympic Museum is in Ouchy, right on the shore of Lake Geneva. From the museum you can see across the lake to the Alps.
37392.m: The Olympic Museum is on Lake Geneva.

37393.q: What is the Olympic Museum about?
37393.e: The Olympic Museum shows the history of the Olympic Games from ancient times to today. You can see sports equipment, clothing and souvenirs there.
37393.m: The Olympic Museum tells the story of the Olympic Games.

37394.q: What can you see at the Olympic Museum?
37394.e: Many torches that carried the Olympic flame are on display in the museum. Each Olympics has its own torch.
37394.m: You can see Olympic torches at the Olympic Museum.

37395.q: Which medal do you get if you come second at the Olympics?
37395.e: At the Olympics there is gold for first place, silver for second and bronze for third. Many of these medals are on display in the museum.
37395.m: Whoever comes second at the Olympics gets silver.

37396.q: In which city is the Olympic Museum?
37396.e: The Olympic Museum is in Lausanne on Lake Geneva. The International Olympic Committee is also based there.
37396.m: The Olympic Museum is in Lausanne.

37397.q: What is there around the Olympic Museum in Lausanne?
37397.e: The museum is surrounded by a park. It has many sculptures and works of art on the theme of sport.
37397.m: Around the Olympic Museum there is a park with sculptures.

37398.q: In which country is the Olympic flame lit each time?
37398.e: The Olympic flame is lit with the sun's rays at ancient Olympia in Greece. Then runners carry it with torches to the host city.
37398.m: The Olympic flame is lit in Greece.

37399.q: Which Swiss resort has hosted the Winter Olympics twice?
37399.e: St Moritz in the canton of the Grisons hosted the Winter Olympics in 1928 and 1948. No other Swiss place has so far hosted the Winter Olympics for adults.
37399.m: St Moritz has hosted the Olympics twice.

37400.q: Which sport is FIFA responsible for?
37400.e: FIFA is the world governing body of football. The football associations of over 200 countries and territories belong to it.
37400.m: FIFA is the world governing body of football.

37401.q: In which city does FIFA have its headquarters?
37401.e: FIFA has been based in Zurich since 1932. Its main building is called the “Home of FIFA”.

37402.q: Which country does FIFA President Gianni Infantino come from?
37402.e: Gianni Infantino was born in Brig in Valais and has been President of FIFA since 2016 (as of 2025). He also holds an Italian passport.
37402.m: FIFA President Gianni Infantino comes from Switzerland.

37403.q: Which famous tournament does FIFA organise?
37403.e: FIFA runs the Football World Cup. National teams from all over the world play for the title.
37403.m: FIFA organises the Football World Cup.

37404.q: The 2026 Football World Cup took place in three countries. Which one was among them?
37404.e: The 2026 World Cup took place in the USA, Canada and Mexico. For the first time, 48 teams took part.
37404.m: The 2026 World Cup took place in the USA, Canada and Mexico.

37405.q: In which city was FIFA founded in 1904?
37405.e: FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904. Only later did it move to Zurich.
37405.m: FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904.

37406.q: What material is the World Cup trophy made of?
37406.e: The World Cup trophy is made of 18-carat gold and is hollow inside. The winning team may hold it up at the celebration.
37406.m: The World Cup trophy is made of gold.

37407.q: On which hill in Zurich are FIFA's headquarters?
37407.e: The “Home of FIFA” building stands on the Zürichberg. It is at the edge of the forest above the city.
37407.m: FIFA's headquarters are on the Zürichberg.

37408.q: Which country hosted the Football World Cup in 1954?
37408.e: The 1954 World Cup took place in Switzerland. The final was played at the Wankdorf Stadium in Bern.
37408.m: Switzerland hosted the World Cup in 1954.

37409.q: In which city is UEFA based?
37409.e: UEFA has had its headquarters in Nyon since 1995. The town lies between Lausanne and Geneva.

37410.q: Which continent is UEFA responsible for?
37410.e: UEFA is the football association for Europe. Other continents have their own associations.

37411.q: Which competition for football clubs belongs to UEFA?
37411.e: In the Champions League, Europe's best clubs play against each other. UEFA organises this competition.
37411.m: The Champions League is a UEFA competition.

37412.q: What is UEFA's tournament for national teams called?
37412.e: At the European Football Championship, Europe's national teams play against each other. It is often called the “Euros” for short.
37412.m: UEFA organises the European Football Championship.

37413.q: In which Swiss city was UEFA founded in 1954?
37413.e: UEFA was founded in Basel on 15 June 1954. Basel lies on the Rhine in the north-west of Switzerland.
37413.m: UEFA was founded in Basel in 1954.
