37414.q: In summer 2025, a European Football Championship took place in Switzerland. Who played in it?
37414.e: In 2025, Switzerland hosted the Women's European Championship. The matches took place in eight Swiss cities.
37414.m: The 2025 Women's Euros took place in Switzerland.

37415.q: Together with which country did Switzerland host Euro 2008?
37415.e: Euro 2008 took place in Switzerland and Austria. The final was in Vienna.
37415.m: Euro 2008 took place in Switzerland and Austria.

37416.q: Which sport is UEFA responsible for in Europe?
37416.e: UEFA is Europe's football association. It is based in Nyon on Lake Geneva and organises, for example, the European Championship.
37416.m: UEFA is the European football association.

37418.q: In which year was the World Trade Organization founded?
37418.e: The WTO was founded on 1 January 1995. So it is quite a young organisation.

37419.q: The head of the WTO is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. Which continent does she come from?
37419.e: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala comes from Nigeria in Africa. She has led the WTO since 2021 as the first woman to do so (as of 2025).
37419.m: The head of the WTO comes from Africa.

37420.q: How many members does the World Trade Organization have (as of 2025)?
37420.e: The WTO has 166 members (as of 2025). Almost all the countries in the world take part.

37421.q: Is Switzerland a member of the World Trade Organization?
37421.e: Switzerland has been a member since the WTO's first year. Trade with other countries is very important for Switzerland.
37421.m: Switzerland is a member of the WTO.

37422.q: The WTO deals with trade. What does trade mean?
37422.e: In trade, people or countries buy and sell goods. That is how bananas, for example, get to Switzerland.
37422.m: Trade means buying and selling goods.

37423.q: Which product does Switzerland sell to many countries around the world?
37423.e: Swiss watches are known all over the world and are sold to many countries. Bananas, coffee and oil, on the other hand, Switzerland has to import.
37423.m: Switzerland sells watches all over the world.

37424.q: What does the T in WTO stand for?
37424.m: The T in WTO stands for Trade.

37425.q: Which animal can be seen in the WWF logo?
37425.e: The WWF logo shows a black and white panda. The panda stands for endangered animals all over the world.
37425.m: The WWF logo shows a panda.

37426.q: In which town is the international WWF based?
37426.e: The international WWF has its headquarters in Gland. Gland is in the canton of Vaud on Lake Geneva.
37426.m: The WWF is based in Gland.

37427.q: What does the WWF stand up for?
37427.e: The WWF is a nature conservation organisation. It protects animals, plants, forests and seas.
37427.m: The WWF protects nature and animals.

37428.q: In which year was the WWF founded?
37428.e: The WWF was founded in 1961. Today it is one of the largest nature conservation organisations in the world.

37429.q: In which country was the WWF founded?
37429.e: The WWF was founded in 1961 in Morges on Lake Geneva. Today its headquarters are in Gland, also in Switzerland.
37429.m: The WWF was founded in Switzerland.

37430.q: What colours is the panda in the WWF logo?
37430.e: The WWF logo shows a panda with black and white fur. The model was Chi Chi, a female panda from London Zoo.
37430.m: The panda in the WWF logo is black and white.

37431.q: What do people switch off for one hour during the WWF's “Earth Hour”?
37431.e: During “Earth Hour”, people all over the world switch off their lights for one hour. That way they show that the environment and climate matter to them.
37431.m: During Earth Hour, you switch off the lights for one hour.

37432.q: What does the giant panda mainly eat?
37432.e: The giant panda eats almost nothing but bamboo. It needs many kilograms of it every day.

37433.q: In which country does the giant panda live in the wild?
37433.e: The giant panda lives in the wild only in the mountain forests of China. It is one of the animals the WWF protects.
37433.m: The giant panda lives in China.

37434.q: Near which city is the CERN research centre?
37434.e: CERN is in Meyrin near Geneva. Researchers from all over the world work there.

37435.q: What do the scientists at CERN study?
37435.e: At CERN, people study the tiny particles that everything is made of. They are much smaller than an atom.
37435.m: At CERN, people study the smallest particles.

37436.q: Where is CERN's large particle accelerator?
37436.e: The large particle accelerator is in a tunnel around 100 metres underground. That way it is well protected.

37437.q: Roughly how long is the tunnel of the large particle accelerator at CERN?
37437.e: The tunnel of the “Large Hadron Collider” is about 27 kilometres long. It is the largest particle accelerator in the world.
37437.m: The tunnel at CERN is about 27 kilometres long.

37438.q: Under which two countries does the CERN tunnel run?
37438.e: The tunnel runs under the border between Switzerland and France. So part of it is in Switzerland and part is in France.
37438.m: The CERN tunnel lies under Switzerland and France.

37439.q: Which important invention was made at CERN?
37439.e: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989. It lets us look at websites today.
37439.m: The World Wide Web was invented at CERN.

37440.q: What shape is CERN's large tunnel?
37440.e: The tunnel is a large ring. Inside it, tiny particles fly round and round until they collide.
37440.m: CERN's tunnel is a big circle.

37441.q: Which particle was discovered at CERN in 2012?
37441.e: In 2012, researchers at CERN found the long-sought Higgs particle. The electron, proton and neutron had been known much earlier.
37441.m: The Higgs particle was discovered at CERN in 2012.

37442.q: What is the official language of the Universal Postal Union?
37442.e: The official language of the Universal Postal Union is French. English is also used as a working language.
37442.m: The official language of the Universal Postal Union is French.

37443.q: In which Swiss city was the Universal Postal Union founded in 1874?
37443.e: The Universal Postal Union was founded in Bern in 1874 and is still based there today. It makes sure that letters can be sent to every country.
37443.m: The Universal Postal Union is based in Bern.

37444.q: What does the Universal Postal Union make sure of?
37444.e: The Universal Postal Union makes rules so that letters and parcels can be sent between countries. That way, a letter from Switzerland also arrives in Japan.
37444.m: The Universal Postal Union makes sure post reaches every country.

37445.q: On which day is World Post Day every year?
37445.e: World Post Day is on 9 October. It marks the day the Universal Postal Union was founded.
37445.m: World Post Day is on 9 October.

37446.q: What does the Universal Postal Union Monument in Bern show?
37446.e: The monument stands in Bern on the Kleine Schanze. It shows female figures representing the continents, passing letters to each other around a globe.
37446.m: The monument in Bern shows figures around a globe.

37447.q: What do you stick on a letter so that it can be sent?
37447.e: With a stamp, you pay for the postage. Thanks to the Universal Postal Union, stamps also work for letters going abroad.
37447.m: You stick a stamp on a letter.

37448.q: Roughly how many countries take part in the Universal Postal Union?
37448.e: Around 190 countries take part in the Universal Postal Union. That is almost every country in the world.
37448.m: Almost every country in the world is in the Universal Postal Union.

37449.q: Which large organisation does the Universal Postal Union belong to today?
37449.e: Today the Universal Postal Union is a specialised agency of the United Nations, the UN for short. But it is much older than the UN.
37449.m: The Universal Postal Union belongs to the United Nations.

37450.q: Where does the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum (WEF) take place?
37450.e: Since it was founded, the WEF's annual meeting has mostly taken place in Davos. Many important guests from all over the world come then.
37450.m: The WEF meets in Davos every year.

37451.e: Davos lies in the mountains in the canton of the Grisons. It is also known for winter sports.
37451.m: Davos is in the canton of the Grisons.

37452.q: In which month does the WEF in Davos usually take place?
37452.e: The annual meeting usually takes place in January. There is usually lots of snow in Davos then.
37452.m: The WEF in Davos is in January.

37453.q: Who founded the World Economic Forum?
37453.e: The economics professor Klaus Schwab founded the WEF. He led it for many years.

37454.q: In which year was the World Economic Forum founded?
37454.e: The World Economic Forum was founded in 1971. At first it was called the “European Management Forum”.

37455.q: Who meets at the WEF in Davos?
37455.e: Politicians, company bosses and experts come to the WEF. They discuss the big questions facing the world.
37455.m: Politicians and company bosses meet at the WEF.

37456.q: In which canton is Davos, where the WEF takes place every year?
37456.e: Davos is in the Grisons. During the WEF, guests from all over the world come to this holiday resort.
37456.m: Davos is in the canton of the Grisons.

37457.q: Who helps with security during the WEF in Davos?
37457.e: During the WEF, the Swiss Army supports the police. For example, it helps to monitor the airspace.
37457.m: The army helps with security at the WEF.

37458.q: What is the BIS often called?
37458.e: Countries' central banks hold their accounts at the BIS. That is why it is called the “central banks' bank”.
37458.m: The BIS is the central banks' bank.

37459.q: In which Swiss city is the BIS based?
37459.e: The Bank for International Settlements was founded in 1930 and is based in Basel.
37459.m: The BIS is based in Basel.

37460.q: What does the best-known BIS building in Basel look like?
a: A flat glass building by a lake
37460.e: The best-known BIS building is a tall, round tower. It was built in the 1970s.
37460.m: The BIS has a tall round tower in Basel.

37461.q: Which Swiss bank is a member of the BIS?
37461.e: Only central banks are members of the BIS. Switzerland's central bank is the Swiss National Bank.
37461.m: The Swiss National Bank is a member of the BIS.

37462.q: Can a child open a savings account at the BIS?
37462.e: The BIS is not a bank for ordinary people. Only central banks and international organisations may deposit money there.
37462.m: Only central banks can be customers of the BIS.

37463.q: What is special about the age of the BIS?
a: It is the oldest international financial organisation
It is the oldest bank in Switzerland
It was founded only after the euro
It is Europe's youngest central bank
37463.e: The BIS was founded in 1930 and is considered the oldest international financial organisation in the world. Other large financial organisations came later.
37463.m: The BIS is the oldest international financial organisation.

37464.q: On which river is Basel, the city of the BIS?
37464.e: Basel lies on the Rhine. Switzerland, Germany and France meet there.

37465.q: What does the organisation “Doctors Without Borders” do?
a: It helps sick people in need
37465.e: “Doctors Without Borders” helps people who are in need because of war, disease or disasters. It treats the sick and injured.
37465.m: Doctors Without Borders helps sick people in need.

37466.q: In which country was “Doctors Without Borders” founded?
37466.e: “Doctors Without Borders” was founded in France in 1971. Today the organisation helps in many countries.
37466.m: Doctors Without Borders was founded in France.

37467.q: Which famous prize did “Doctors Without Borders” receive in 1999?
37467.e: In 1999, “Doctors Without Borders” received the Nobel Peace Prize. This honoured its help for people in need.
37467.m: Doctors Without Borders received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1999.

37468.q: In which Swiss city does “Doctors Without Borders” have its international office?
37468.e: The international office of “Doctors Without Borders” is in Geneva. The Swiss section is also based there.
37468.m: Doctors Without Borders has an important office in Geneva.

37469.q: Where does “Doctors Without Borders” get most of its money from?
37469.e: Most of the money comes from donations by private individuals. That way the organisation stays independent.
37469.m: Doctors Without Borders lives mainly on donations.

37470.q: What is “Doctors Without Borders” called in French?
37470.e: In French, the organisation is called “Médecins Sans Frontières”. That is why it is abbreviated to MSF.
37470.m: Doctors Without Borders is called Médecins Sans Frontières in French.

37471.q: What colour is the “Doctors Without Borders” logo?
37471.e: The logo shows a running figure in red. You can see it, for example, on the organisation's vehicles and tents.
37471.m: The Doctors Without Borders logo is red.

37472.e: “Doctors Without Borders” helps all people in need. Origin, religion or opinion make no difference.
37472.m: Doctors Without Borders helps all people in need.

37473.q: In which city is the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) based?
37473.e: The ITU is based in Geneva. Experts from almost every country meet there.
37473.m: The ITU is based in Geneva.

37474.q: What does the International Telecommunication Union deal with?
37474.e: The ITU makes sure that telephone, radio, television and internet work between countries. To do this, it makes common rules.
37474.m: The ITU deals with telephone, radio and internet.

37475.q: What special position does the ITU have in the UN?
a: It is the oldest specialised agency
It is the youngest specialised agency
37475.e: The ITU is the oldest specialised agency of the United Nations. It is even much older than the UN itself.
37475.m: The ITU is the oldest specialised agency of the UN.

37476.q: In which year was the International Telecommunication Union founded?
37476.e: The ITU was founded on 17 May 1865. So it is over 150 years old.

37477.q: How were messages sent when the ITU was founded?
37477.e: The ITU began as a telegraph union. With the telegraph, messages were sent along wires as short and long signals.
37477.m: In the past, messages were sent by telegraph.

37478.q: What does the ITU allocate to countries so that radios do not interfere with each other?
37478.e: The ITU shares out radio frequencies among countries. That way radio, mobile phones and satellites do not interfere with each other.

37479.q: What is Switzerland's international dialling code?
37479.e: Switzerland has the country code +41. The ITU sets such codes for all countries.

37480.q: What does the ITU also allocate for satellites?
37480.e: The ITU allocates orbits for satellites. That way satellites from different countries do not get in each other's way.
37480.m: The ITU assigns satellites their places in space.

37481.q: What do you call a form of government in which one person or a small group rules without any checks?
37481.e: In a dictatorship one person or a small group has all the power. Nobody can really keep them in check.
37481.m: In a dictatorship a few people rule without checks.

37482.q: May people in a dictatorship freely criticise the government?
a: Yes, but only on the radio
37482.e: In a dictatorship criticism of the government is often forbidden. Anyone who criticises it anyway can be punished.
37482.m: In a dictatorship you usually may not criticise the government freely.

37483.q: What often happens to newspapers in a dictatorship?
a: They always belong to the readers
They are checked by the people
37483.e: In dictatorships the state often decides what goes in the newspapers. So people only find out what the rulers want.
37483.m: In a dictatorship newspapers are often controlled by the state.

37484.q: What does a dictatorship often do with the internet?
a: It makes it free for everyone
37484.e: Many dictatorships block websites so that people cannot read free information. This is called censorship.

37485.q: What can happen in a dictatorship to people who protest against the government?
37485.e: In dictatorships people who protest are often locked up. The rulers want no resistance.
37485.m: Anyone who protests in a dictatorship often risks prison.

37486.q: What do you call a police force that secretly watches people in a dictatorship?
37486.e: A secret police secretly watches what people say and do. Many dictatorships have such a police force.
37486.m: Dictatorships often watch their people with a secret police.

37487.q: Why do some people flee from a dictatorship?
a: Because they are not free there
Because there are too many bikes there
Because the holidays there are too long
Because all schools there are free
37487.e: In a dictatorship many freedoms are missing, and some people are persecuted. That is why they seek protection in another country.
37487.m: Many people flee a dictatorship because they cannot live freely there.
